evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-wsl-kit

**One line:** DeepSeek Harness agent in WSL, chat in a Windows browser — install this kit when paths, proxy, clipboard, and “open that file” must cross the OS boundary.

This is a **meta-repo** (docs + install script + [`cordis.patch.yml`](./cordis.patch.yml)). It does not ship plugin runtimes. Each plugin repo ships a homepage `README.md` (often Chinese-first for newer plugins) plus `README.en.md` / `README.zh.md` as needed.

[中文说明 → README.zh.md](./README.zh.md)

---

## How the pieces fit

The kit is not a runtime. `install.sh` loads **Daily / GitHub / LLM / Full** plugins into the dsh `web` profile. Chat stays on Windows; the agent and tools stay in WSL. A second tier of **Linux/local capability** plugins (inference, search, media, read-only DevOps, …) is **not** in `install.sh` — use [`link-linux-plugins.sh`](./scripts/link-linux-plugins.sh) or `dsh plugin add` as needed. IM / Obsidian / Jev are likewise off `install.sh`.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph win [Windows]
    browser["Browser :3081/?token="]
    host["Clipboard / Explorer / default browser"]
    vault["Obsidian vault (NTFS)"]
    localLLM["Ollama / llama.cpp / vLLM"]
  end
  subgraph wslbox [WSL]
    relay["port relay"]
    dsh["dsh web :3080"]
    subgraph kitPlugins ["install.sh suites · package.json bundle (npm-gated)"]
      daily["Daily: env net fetch open clipboard path browser launch"]
      guards["repeat-stop + tool-budget"]
      more["GitHub / LLM / Full doctors"]
    end
    subgraph winread [Windows read-only diagnostics · not in install.sh]
      wdiag["defender · eventlog · perf · power · registry · service"]
    end
    revive["dsh-wsl-revive — installs and reports the UI resident"]
    subgraph linuxOpt [Optional Linux local · not in install.sh]
      infer["ollama · llamacpp · vllm · vecmem"]
      media["media · search · secret · struct"]
      devops["git · tmux · compose · k8s · helm · terraform · …"]
      desk["playwright · mail · cal · pkg · rclone · db · glab"]
    end
    im["dsh-wsl-im — optional"]
    obsidian["dsh-wsl-obsidian — optional"]
    jev["dsh-wsl-jev — optional"]
  end
  api["DeepSeek API"]
  chats["Feishu / WeCom / DingTalk / QQ / Slack / Discord / Telegram"]

  browser --> relay --> dsh
  dsh --> kitPlugins
  dsh --> linuxOpt
  dsh --> api
  linuxOpt --> localLLM
  kitPlugins --> host
  chats --> im --> dsh
  obsidian --> vault
  dsh --> obsidian
  dsh --> jev
```

| Boundary | Who owns it |
|----------|-------------|
| Windows UI | Browser on `:3081` with a one-shot `?token=` (bare `:3081` is 401; `:3080` is WSL-only) |
| Agent | `dsh web` inside WSL, tools via plugin `ctx` |
| Cross-OS Daily | `path` / `open` / `clipboard` / `browser` / `launch` / `net` / `fetch` (`KIT_SET=daily`) |
| Linux local optional | Inference, media, sandboxed search, secrets, read-only DevOps — see [`docs/OPTIONAL_PLUGINS.md`](./docs/OPTIONAL_PLUGINS.md); `bash scripts/link-linux-plugins.sh` |
| IM | `dsh-wsl-im` outbound WS/Stream/Gateway → `ctx.agents`. One workspace per IM, one session per chat |
| Obsidian | `dsh-wsl-obsidian`: WSL agent ↔ Windows NTFS vault + `obsidian://` |
| Jev | `dsh-wsl-jev`: System One (`jev_ask` / `check` / `rank`) via OpenRouter or TypeSafe |

### The bundle package, and why `install.sh` is still the way in

There is a `package.json` here that describes the same 31 plugins as one bundle
(`dsh.bundle.patch` → `cordis.patch.yml`, which carries their `config`). **It does not install today**, and
the reason is worth knowing before you try it:

```
pnpm add github:173787247/dsh-wsl-kit
  → ERR_PNPM_EXOTIC_SUBDEP: Exotic dependency "dsh-wsl-tray-launcher" (resolved via
    git-repository) is not allowed in subdependencies when blockExoticSubdeps is enabled
```

pnpm refuses a git-resolved dependency inside another git-resolved package. A `github:` bundle therefore
cannot depend on `github:` plugins — so the bundle only becomes installable once the plugins are **on npm**,
at which point its dependencies become ordinary version ranges.

Until then: **use [`install.sh`](./install.sh)** (or `dsh plugin add` per plugin). The `package.json` is the
description of the destination, not a second route to it.

## Plugin versions

> **Three plugins install under a different name than their repository.** npm already had
> `dsh-wsl-tray`, `dsh-wsl-expose` and `dsh-wsl-workspace` taken by other authors' plugins, so these
> three publish under `dsh-wsl-tray-launcher`, `dsh-wsl-portproxy` and `dsh-wsl-workspace-check`.
> The repositories are unchanged — only `dsh plugin add` needs the package name. Everything else on
> this page links to the repository, which is what you clone or read.

## Compatibility (2026-09)

| Piece | Status |
|-------|--------|
| **dsh** | Verified against **`0.2.2-rc.4`** (npm package, 2026-11-18). rc.4 is a bug-fix release; the WSL plugin suite needs no source change: all 71 plugin `lib/` entry points import under rc.4 and the offline smoke passes; the full `web` profile has been restarted and serves the UI. rc.2+ retires `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team-profile`; remove it from profile dependencies/bundles, keep `agent-team` config to `maxTasks` only, and let the core Team support load. Kit scripts assume dsh **≥0.1.2** UI launch tokens (`?token=` on `:3081`). The `{{cwd}}` placeholder in [dsh-wsl-env](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-env) is gone. |
| **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash** | Official API model id is **`deepseek-flash`**. Legacy `deepseek-v4-flash` / `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp` temporarily route to V4.1 Flash. **Not configured by this kit** — set under `llm-deepseek` / default model in `~/.dsh/settings.yaml`. |
| **Agent Teams** | Core support in rc.2 (named subagents + shared task board). The old `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team-profile` is **retired**: remove it from profile dependencies and bundles, keep `agent-team` config at `maxTasks` only, and enable Team mode per Session. Expect longer “Deep diving” turns; use a fresh non-Teams session to smoke-test models. |
| **Plugins** | Snapshot: [Plugin versions](#plugin-versions) (sibling checkouts 2026-09-16). Floor: [`scripts/check-plugin-versions.sh`](./scripts/check-plugin-versions.sh). Daily includes [dsh-wsl-fetch](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-fetch) **≥0.1.1**. |

### ⚠️ Breaking changes in dsh 0.2.1-alpha.2 (released 2026-10-09)

These hit things in this kit. **Read this before upgrading**, not after the UI stops working.

| Change | Impact | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| **`{{cwd}}` is no longer a prompt variable** | The official `dsh-system-prompt` README states the loop does not register it. Leaving it in a prompt makes assembly **fail** — every message reports `unknown prompt variable` and the UI looks dead | Use plain prose. The working directory now comes from runtime context and the new `working_directory` tool. [dsh-wsl-env](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-env) is fixed (`a674c70`) |
| **`agent-instructions` drops per-line `dshHome` config** | Instruction directories now come from the process's `DSH_HOME` or the default | Check the profile patch for a `dshHome` entry under `agent-instructions` and remove it |
| **Tool display `both` mode removed** | Only `native` and `ptc` remain | Update old configs and API calls |
| **Agent Team messages go straight to the target Inbox** | The standalone outbox, auto-retry and resend dedup are gone | Config and result fields need migrating |
| **Python PTC now uses the session sandbox policy** | Custom compositions must provide `sandbox` and `sandboxPolicy` services | Add them to hand-made compositions |
| **Default SDK profile is now a general AI Agent** | No longer a fixed coding Agent | Compositions relying on the old default identity must state it |

**What you gain**: the `working_directory` tool, shared `AGENTS.md` from an agents directory (`DSH_AGENTS_HOME`), an experimental Git Worktrees plugin, session state-record APIs, Web binding to a chosen address with native HTTPS, pi-ai 1.0.2.

**One habit**: read the release notes' "Other changes" section before upgrading — every breaking change lives there. We upgraded first and read afterwards, and paid for it with a night of debugging.

### ⚠️ Breaking changes in dsh 0.2.1-alpha.3 and 0.2.1-alpha.4

Read from the upstream release notes on 2026-10-16, after upgrading to alpha.4 without
reading them first. The one change that mattered was a single line under **Other changes**.

| Version | Change | Impact | What to do |
|---|---|---|---|
| **alpha.4** | Plugin compatibility is decided by **`engines.dsh`** when a plugin declares it | A plugin declaring a range narrower than the core is **disabled outright**: `disabling profile plugin row "<id>": Plugin <pkg>@<old> is incompatible with dsh <new>`. It is not an error you see — the tools and panels are simply absent | Keep pinned `@deepseek-ai/*` plugins on the **same version track** as the core: `dsh plugin --profile <name> add <pkg>@<version>` |
| **alpha.3** | Credential precedence changed: Web and Desktop prefer **saved** credentials; headless uses environment and `.env` and **no longer reads saved keys** | A headless profile that relied on a saved key stops authenticating | Give headless an explicit key through the environment or `.env` |
| **alpha.3** | The Azure provider is now named **`azure`** | Provider configs still using `azure-openai-responses` stop resolving | Rename the provider |
| **alpha.3** | `--from-default-profile` now **replaces** the target custom profile, including its plugins and settings | Running it against a profile you care about destroys that profile's plugin set | Back the profile up first; do not use it to "refresh" a working profile |
| **alpha.3** | Fixes *"some sessions cannot be continued after a restart"* and *"history compatibility errors when switching to DeepSeek"* | Both symptoms are fixed upstream from alpha.3 | If they still happen on alpha.3 or later, the cause is local rather than the version |

**How to check the second row for yourself**

```sh
grep 'disabling profile plugin row' /tmp/dsh-web.log     # a plugin was disabled at startup
```

The log is appended across restarts, so count the lines **before** upgrading and compare
afterwards — a bare `grep -c` reports every past start as well.

### ⚠️ dsh 0.2.1-alpha.5 (released 2026-10-16)

**No breaking change.** Its "Other changes" adds one slot,
`conversation.input.model.label`, for plugins that relabel the composer's model
selector. Nothing in this kit is affected.

Recorded so the next upgrade does not have to re-derive it — and because the two
releases before it *did* break things.

### Upgrading, and what keeps the UI reachable

Use `scripts/upgrade-dsh-full.sh`; it reads the target release's notes before it
installs anything, and `docs/UPGRADE.zh.md` describes the layers and the traps.

Two scripts exist so a broken UI does not need a person at the keyboard:

| | |
|---|---|
| `scripts/dsh-web-watchdog.sh` | Probes the port on a timer and revives only when it is down; anything already answering is left alone |
| `scripts/dsh-rescue.sh` | Last resort. Assumes neither systemd nor the rest of this kit is intact, falls back to starting dsh directly |

### Plugin README policy### Plugin README policy

- **This Compatibility section is the suite matrix.** Each plugin README has a matching **Compatibility** table (EN + ZH): minimum dsh **≥0.1.2**, pointer here for **latest verified**, kit set, and notes that cloud Flash / Agent Teams are not owned by WSL plugins.
- When dsh ships a new line (e.g. `0.1.5` GA or `0.1.6`), **update this kit table first**, then refresh plugin “currently …” lines (or re-run the suite doc sync). Do not invent per-plugin “verified” dates without a smoke pass.
- API-sensitive plugins (`net`, `fetch`, `port`, `expose`, `tray`, `hostsvc`) carry an extra **Scope** paragraph; thinner Daily tools keep the shared table only.

No kit code change is required solely for V4.1 Flash — update model ids in settings if you still default to retired names.

---

## 60-second start (recommended: Daily set)

**Prereq:** `dsh` works inside WSL (profile usually `web`). Prefer `0.2.2-rc.4` or newer from the same train.

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-kit/master/install.sh \
  | KIT_SET=daily bash
```

Then:

1. Restart via [`scripts/restart-dsh-web.sh`](./scripts/restart-dsh-web.sh) (starts dsh on `:3080` **and** the Windows relay on `:3081`)
2. In Windows open the **URL printed by `restart-dsh-web.sh`** (dsh ≥0.1.2 includes `?token=`; bare `:3081` is 401. Not `:3080`). Token is also written to `/tmp/dsh-ui-url` (WSL).
3. Open a **new** session (old sessions keep the old toolset)
4. Optionally merge [`cordis.patch.yml`](./cordis.patch.yml) into your profile (a later plugin `config` **replaces** the whole object — restate every key you still need)

| Want | Command |
|------|---------|
| **Daily (recommended)** | `KIT_SET=daily bash install.sh` |
| Daily + GitHub App / credentials | `KIT_SET=github bash install.sh` |
| **Local LLM + network doctor** | `KIT_SET=llm bash install.sh` |
| Everything | `KIT_SET=full bash install.sh` (or omit `KIT_SET` — same as before) |

From a local clone: `KIT_SET=daily bash install.sh`

### What `restart-dsh-web.sh` loads

- `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`, `OLLAMA_API_KEY` default `ollama`
- `NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost` only (do **not** inherit Clash RFC1918 `NO_PROXY` globs — they make Node skip the proxy and timeout on `api.deepseek.com`)
- Optional: `source "$HOME/.dsh/dsh-wsl-github.env"` yourself before start when using GitHub App plugins

---

## What you get immediately

| Pain | Tool | Plugin |
|------|------|--------|
| Proxy / Node 24 blocks DeepSeek or npm | `net_doctor` | [dsh-wsl-net](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-net) |
| `web_fetch` `TypeError: fetch failed` (API works) | Install [dsh-wsl-fetch](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-fetch) ≥0.1.1 + `restart-dsh-web.sh` | [dsh-wsl-fetch](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-fetch) |
| Open a Linux path from chat on Windows | (clickable paths) | [dsh-wsl-open](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-open) |
| Path convert / slow `/mnt/c` | `path_convert` | [dsh-wsl-path](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-path) |
| Windows clipboard | `wsl_clipboard` | [dsh-wsl-clipboard](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-clipboard) |
| Open a PR / docs URL in Windows | `win_open_url` | [dsh-wsl-browser](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-browser) |
| Agent forgets it is in WSL | (system prompt inject) | [dsh-wsl-env](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-env) |

**Daily** = table above + `win_launch` + `dsh-repeat-stop` + `dsh-tool-budget` + **`dsh-wsl-fetch`**.

Smoke: in a new session ask “run `net_doctor`” and “copy this path to the Windows clipboard”. Prefer model **`deepseek-flash`** for cloud; keep Agent Teams off for first smoke.

---

## Install sets (short list)

| Set | Includes | Who |
|-----|----------|-----|
| **Daily** | env, net, **fetch**, open, repeat-stop, tool-budget, clipboard, path, browser, launch | Most WSL + Windows-browser users |
| **GitHub day** | Daily + [github](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-github) + [cred](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-cred) + notify | Also need PR/Actions status and `git push` credential hints |
| **LLM** | env, net, **fetch**, hostsvc, docker, dns, clock, gpu, port, expose, tray, open, path, browser | Local Ollama / vLLM / Unsloth + connectivity |
| **Full** | Everything in [`install.sh`](./install.sh) — Daily + GitHub extras + doctors, plus read-only Windows host observation (perf, service, eventlog, registry, defender, power) | GPU/Docker/clock doctors, tray, portproxy, etc. |
| **Desktop** | uia, winshot, winctl, wininput — `KIT_SET=desktop` | Want the agent to read **and drive** the Windows desktop |

**Do not** start with Full — get Daily working, then add plugins for specific pains.

**Desktop is a separate set on purpose.** `dsh-wsl-wininput` types and clicks,
`dsh-wsl-winctl` moves and closes windows; `dsh-wsl-uia` and `dsh-wsl-winshot`
are the observation half of the same pair. That is a different power level from
reading counters and an event log, so `full` never pulls it in.

### Optional: GitHub day

GitHub from WSL is credentials + API + browser open + proxy — not one mega-plugin. After `KIT_SET=github`:

1. Create the App per [dsh-wsl-github](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-github#readme) (read-only Metadata / PRs / Actions; webhooks off)
2. Before start: `source "$HOME/.dsh/dsh-wsl-github.env"`
3. New session → `github_app_hint` / `github_repo_status`; **never** paste PEM / PAT into chat

---

## Node 24 + Windows proxy

```sh
export HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7890   # or Clash mixed port, e.g. 16006
export HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7890
export NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1
# Prefer restart-dsh-web.sh so NO_PROXY stays loopback-only
```

Still failing → ask the agent to run `net_doctor`.

- **API works, `web_fetch` fails** → [dsh-wsl-fetch](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-fetch) (Daily already installs it).
- **Third-party Workers / Cloudflare 403 (1010) via Clash** → add a **DIRECT** rule for that host (plugin cannot override site WAF).

Local OpenAI-compatible backends on Windows: add [dsh-wsl-hostsvc](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-hostsvc), run `host_reach`, merge [`examples/local-llm-providers.settings.yaml`](./examples/local-llm-providers.settings.yaml).

---

## Troubleshooting

Connectivity, UI token 401, Ollama ctx, and fetch faults: **[docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md](./docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md)** (中文: [TROUBLESHOOTING.zh.md](./docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.zh.md)).

Order of play: `host_reach` → `net_doctor` → `dns_doctor` → `clock_doctor` → workspace/mnt → expose (LAN only).

---

## Maintaining this kit

Which file is generated and which is handwritten, what each of the thirty-two
scripts does and when to run it, and the invariants that keep twenty-six plugin
copies from drifting: **[docs/MAINTENANCE.zh.md](./docs/MAINTENANCE.zh.md)**.

# dsh-wsl-wslconfig
> **Install set:** part of [dsh-wsl-kit](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-kit). Prefer `KIT_SET=daily` | `llm` | `github` | `full`. Fault tree: [TROUBLESHOOTING.md](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-kit/blob/master/docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md).

DeepSeek Harness tool: **`wslconfig_hint`** — read-only parse of Windows `.wslconfig` (mirrored/memory) and advise dsh **:3081** relay (never `dsh --host 0.0.0.0`).

[中文说明 → README.zh.md](./README.zh.md)

## Where it sits

Reads Windows .wslconfig and says whether mirrored or NAT networking matches the :3081 relay.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  agent["dsh agent"] --> tool["wslconfig_hint"] --> cfg[".wslconfig mirrored or NAT"]
```

Suite diagram and version snapshot: [dsh-wsl-kit](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-kit#how-the-pieces-fit). This plugin is **0.2.0** (full). Do not copy that matrix into this README.


## Compatibility

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Plugin** | `dsh-wsl-wslconfig` **0.2.0** |
| **Minimum dsh** | ≥ **0.1.2** (web UI one-shot `?token=` on Windows relay `:3081`) |
| **Latest verified** | See [dsh-wsl-kit Compatibility](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-kit#compatibility-2026-09) (currently **`0.2.2-rc.4`**) — single source of truth for the suite |
| **Kit set** | `full` or install alone |
| **Cloud Flash** | Use model id **`deepseek-flash`** (V4.1 Flash) in `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` / `llm-deepseek` — not configured by this plugin |
| **Agent Teams** | Core support in dsh rc.2 (named subagents + shared task board); the old experimental profile is retired. Not required here |

Suite floor versions: kit [`check-plugin-versions.sh`](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-kit/blob/master/scripts/check-plugin-versions.sh). Fault tree: [TROUBLESHOOTING.md](https://github.com/173787247/dsh-wsl-kit/blob/master/docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md).

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:173787247/dsh-wsl-wslconfig
npm test
```

The fixed patch resolves the committed native index and local modules. wslconfig_hint reads the Windows profile .wslconfig and returns bounded advice; execute ignores caller arguments and does not write that configuration. The shared WSL helper contains command utilities, but the tool uses detection and read paths. No lifecycle hooks. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# dsh-aftermath

记录 AI 每轮对话对观测目录的文件改动。出事之后可以倒查：改了哪些文件、大概是哪条命令改的、怎么恢复。

DSH 插件，零依赖，不联网，不读文件内容。

> 第一次用、不想看技术细节：直接看 [GUIDE.md](GUIDE.md)，照着做就行。

## 用法

装上就不用管，它自己记。出事之后：

1. 直接跟 agent 说「桌面图标怎么全白了」，它会调 `aftermath_history` 查上一轮删了什么；
2. 或者自己输 `/aftermath report --last 1` 看明细；
3. 记录存在 `$DSH_HOME/state/aftermath/`。

## 工作方式

很多事故不是 `write`/`edit` 工具造成的，而是 agent 跑了一条 `pwsh`/`bash` 命令直接改磁盘——只在工具调用层做 hook 看不到这类改动。所以 aftermath 在文件系统层观测：

- 每轮开始和结束各对观测目录做一次快照（桌面 48 条实测约 0.3 ms），做差得到变更列表；
- 同时记下每次工具调用的起止时刻（`tool/call` 与 `tool/result` 各带一个时间）；
- 拿同一轮的调用证据给每条变更标归因，归因分四档，报告里逐条标注：

| 档位 | 判据 |
| --- | --- |
| ✔ 确定 | 命令里出现该文件的绝对路径 |
| ◐ 很可能 | 命令在处理这个目录，或本轮只有它提到这个文件名 |
| ○ 时间窗内 | 改动 mtime 落在某次调用的起止区间内（没等到结束时刻就落到整轮宽窗） |
| ？ 无法归因 | 没有证据。报告会写明，并附上该轮命令原文供自己判断 |

「时间窗内」分两级：先比**这一次调用自己的区间**（窄，几乎不会错配到别的调用）；区间全不命中，才退回**整个回合的宽窗**，那时它只说明「这一轮里有人动过」。表格的归因列会区分这两级，写成 `○区间内` 与 `○时间窗内`，依据列再给出具体判据（`call-interval` / `turn-window`）。

**观测根之外也不会完全瞎：**

- 一轮里观测根内没有变化、但确实执行过写操作时，仍会留一条轻记录（只含命令摘要，`kind: quiet`）。报告会写「这道改动可能落在根外」并列出命令原文，历史表里显示 `0（写过 N 条命令，根外？）`。
- 每次工具调用里出现过的绝对路径都会存进记录，报告多一节「命令提到、但不在观测根内的路径」。它**不扫盘**，只说「命令提到过」，所以写清了「插件没看过它们的磁盘状态」。
- 不想要这些轻记录，把 `recordQuietTurns` 设成 `false` 即可。

判「写操作」的规则：

- `printf x > a.txt` 这类靠重定向落盘的写法也算写（`>` / `>>` / `2>` / `Out-File` 都认），目标路径计入证据；引号里的 `>` 是文本，不算；
- `/c/Users/...` 这种 Git Bash 路径会翻成 `C:\Users\...` 再比对，不会因为写法不同就认不出来；
- `powershell -c "Get-Content x"` 是读、`powershell -c "Remove-Item x"` 是写：先看里面的动词，两者都对不上（`node build.js`）时才保守地算写；
- 只从命令参数和路径参数里取证据，`content` / `prompt` 这类载荷文本不参与。否则某个工具的参数里碰巧写了 `Out-File` 和一条桌面路径，那个文件就会被标成「确定」——这是真机记录里抓到过的误判。

否则这类调用会被当成只读，白白丢掉区间证据。

两条规则：只读命令不算证据（`Get-Content a.txt` 提到路径但不会把 a.txt 标成「确定」）；某个目录这轮扫描失败时整根跳过，不会误报一排「删除」。

报告长这样：

```
第 12 轮 · 2026-11-17 20:41 · 会话 #7
共 4 处变更：删除 3 · 修改 1
归因：✔确定 2 · ◐很可能 1 · ○时间窗内 1 · ？无法归因 0

| 变更 | 条目 | 大小 | 时间 | 归因 | 依据 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 删除 | Desktop\微信.lnk | 1.2 KB | 20:41:03 | ✔ 确定 | 命令里出现该绝对路径（bash） |
| 删除 | Desktop\QQ.lnk | 1.1 KB | 20:41:03 | ◐ 很可能 | 该调用在处理 Desktop\ 下的文件 |
| 修改 | Desktop\desktop.ini | 218 B | 20:41:04 | ○ 区间内 | 落在 bash 这次调用的起止区间内 |

报告健康度
- 快照耗时：本轮结束这次扫描 1 ms，覆盖 2 个根 / 446 个条目
- 归因分布：✔确定 2（50%） · ◐很可能 1（25%） · ○时间窗内 1（25%） · ？无法归因 0（0%）
- 时间证据：1 处 mtime 落在某次调用的起止区间内，0 处只落在整轮宽窗
- 调用区间：5 次调用、3 次写操作，3/3 拿到起止时刻（容差 1500 ms）

可能的症状：桌面图标变白/空白
  1) 检查快捷方式是否失效：powershell -c "..."
  2) 刷新图标缓存：ie4uinit.exe -show
```

末尾那段「报告健康度」是这份记录自己的可信度证据：扫描耗时、覆盖了多少条目、四档归因各占多少、有几条调用真正拿到了起止时刻、有没有因为条数上限被截断。数字难看的时候，就不该拿它当定论。

## 相比直接翻日志

会话日志里已经有每次工具调用和命令原文，那还需要这个插件吗？需要的地方在于：**日志记的是「发出了什么命令」，插件记的是「磁盘上留下了什么」。**

| | 翻会话日志 | dsh-aftermath |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 内容 | 意图层：工具名、参数、命令原文、返回值 | 结果层：哪个文件被建/删/改、大小与 mtime |
| 要回答「这轮改了哪些文件」 | 得自己把命令逐条读一遍，再脑内模拟 `rm -rf`、`git checkout`、脚本内部调用的效果 | 直接给变更表，四类分好 |
| 命令失败了会怎样 | 日志里照样有那条命令和报错，容易当成“干过这件事” | 磁盘没有变化，就不会出现在变更表里 |
| 覆盖范围 | `write`/`edit`、`bash`、`pwsh`、子代理、后台进程散在不同 step，得自己拼 | 只看磁盘结果，谁干的都要过这道账 |
| 判断是哪次调用造成的 | 日志时间戳是事件时刻，文件 mtime 是磁盘时刻，人工对时容易错 | 调用区间配对，误差有容差，依据列写明是哪一级 |
| 事后还查得到吗 | 长会话会被压缩/裁剪，早期工具输出可能已经不在上下文里；翻几十轮也很费劲 | 独立 NDJSON 存档，`--since 2h` 一条命令，还能 grep / jq |
| 看得懂吗 | 一堆命令与返回 | 先给结论、症状对应的检查命令，再给逐条明细 |
| 跨会话 | 每次对话各看各的 | 记录按日存、带会话短标，可以横向对比 |

要诚实的地方：**“是哪条命令干的”这个判断，插件同样只能从 `tool/call` 的文本里取证据**，和翻日志的信息源是同一个。差别在于它把「事实」和「猜测」分开了——磁盘上的变更是事实，归因是分级猜测，报告里逐条标出档位，标 `？` 就是真的没证据。

一句话：日志告诉你它**说过要做什么**，插件告诉你它**实际做成了什么**。两个都要看，只是顺序是插件先给事实、日志再给上下文。

## 安装

**Plugins → Add plugin → 选这个目录**。要求 DSH `>=0.2.2-0 <0.3.0`、Node `>=22.12.0`。

## 设置

Plugins 页打开 dsh-aftermath 的详情，卡片里能改：

- 总开关（关掉立即停止快照，历史记录保留可查）
- 观测目录（一行一个，内置标识或绝对路径）
- 递归深度、保留天数、路径打码

总开关点一下即时写入；其余几项改完点保存。保存是逐字段写入的：某个字段被宿主拒绝就停在那一条并显示失败，不会显示「已保存」。保存后立即生效，不用重启插件。

卡片能不能改这些字段，取决于宿主有没有拿到插件的设置 schema。用 `link:` 方式安装（本地开发目录）时，Node 默认按真实路径解析模块，插件目录可能和依赖不在同一个盘，`lib/schema.js` 因此按 `DSH_PROFILE_DIR`、`DSH_INSTALL_DIR`、`$DSH_HOME`、以及 exe 旁边的 `resources/app.asar/dsh/node_modules` 逐处找 `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`。

怀疑卡片不对劲时先跑 `/aftermath doctor`：它会打印 Config 是否导出、schema 从哪加载的、宿主给本插件建的设置命名空间在不在。同一份自检在每次启动时也会写到 `$DSH_HOME/state/aftermath/settings-probe.json`。如果确认 schema 没加载到，卡片里只会剩总开关，这时改用下面的 yml 配置。

## 配置（yml）

在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里写 config，全部有默认值：

```yaml
- id: dsh-aftermath
  config:
    roots: [desktop, downloads, documents]   # 内置标识或绝对路径，支持 "id=路径"
    depth: 2                      # 0 = 只看根目录这一层
    exclude: ['node_modules', '~$*']
    extraRoots: ['D:\项目']
    retentionDays: 7
    maskHome: true                # 报告里把家目录打码成 ~
    intervalSlackMs: 1500         # 调用区间归因的容差（毫秒），0 = 严丝合缝
    followCwd: true               # 当前会话的工作目录自动算进观测根（大目录只看顶层）
    recordQuietTurns: true        # 根内没变化、但执行过写操作时，也记一条只有命令摘要的轻记录
```

内置标识：`desktop`、`downloads`、`documents`、`pictures`、`music`、`videos`，依次探测 `%USERPROFILE%\<名>`、`OneDrive\<名>`、中文名（`桌面`/`下载`）。

Windows 上桌面被 OneDrive 重定向很常见。插件不读注册表，路径靠别名探测加显式配置，跑 `/aftermath roots` 确认实际观测的目录对不对。

## 默认排除表

下面这些名字默认不扫（`exclude` 里写的是名字或通配，不是路径；大小写不敏感）：

| 条目 | 为什么排除 |
| --- | --- |
| `node_modules` | 依赖目录，动辄几万个文件；删了重装即可 |
| `.git` `.svn` `.vs` | 版本库与 IDE 的内部目录，改动不反映你自己的文件 |
| `~$*` | Office 打开文档时生成的锁文件，开合一次就变，天天报一堆「新建/删除」 |
| `Thumbs.db` `desktop.ini` `.DS_Store` | 系统/访达的缩略图与文件夹配置，被反复重写 |
| `$RECYCLE.BIN` | 回收站：删掉的文件会落到这里，扫进来会把「删除」再报一遍 |
| `System Volume Information` | 卷影副本等系统信息 |
| `dist` `build` `.next` `.turbo` `coverage` | 构建产物与覆盖率报告，文件多、删了能重新生成 |
| `__pycache__` `.venv` `venv` `.mypy_cache` `.pytest_cache` | Python 缓存与虚拟环境 |
| `target` | Rust / Maven 的构建目录 |

默认值是为了让报告可读：不排除的话，`cwd` 自动跟随一旦落在大仓库上，一轮扫描会从几十毫秒涨到几百毫秒，报告里还会塞满构建产物。

两种改法：

- 想加：把新名字写进 `exclude` 数组（yml 里这个数组是**整体替换**，不是追加）
- 想减：如果某个目录叫 `build` 但里面确实有你心疼的文件，把它从数组里去掉

被排除的目录**不进快照、也不进报告**——排除的语义是「当它不存在」，不是「看到但不记」。

## 命令

| 命令 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `/aftermath report [--last N] [--since 2h] [--root desktop] [--save]` | 变更明细与归因 |
| `/aftermath scan [--keep]` | 立刻扫描，与上次基线对比 |
| `/aftermath roots` | 打印解析出的观测根 |
| `/aftermath roots --suggest` | 列出常用目录哪些已经盯上、哪些还没，并给出可直接粘的 yml |
| `/aftermath roots --add <路径>` / `--remove <路径>` | 预览加/减之后会变成什么样子，并给出可粘贴的 yml（不替你改配置） |
| `/aftermath status` | 配置、存档位置、记录条数 |
| `/aftermath doctor` | 自检：设置命名空间是否就绪、schema 从哪加载 |
| `/aftermath help` | 帮助 |

`--save` 把完整报告写到 `$DSH_HOME/state/aftermath/reports/`。

## 给 agent 的工具

`aftermath_history`（只读，参数 `since` / `root` / `limit`）。装上之后 agent 可以自己查「上一轮删了什么」，不用你翻日志。

## 存档与隐私

```
$DSH_HOME/state/aftermath/
├── baseline.json              最近一次快照（空闲期对比用）
├── turns/2026-11-17.ndjson    逐轮变更记录
└── reports/                   --save 的报告
```

只记路径、大小、mtime，不读文件内容、不存正文；命令原文只保留 ≤180 字符的片段用于归因说明，命令里出现的绝对路径最多留 12 条（每条 ≤320 字符）。不启子进程，不联网，恢复命令只打印不执行。记录按 `retentionDays` 自动清理。

记录格式 `v: 2`。每条带 `kind`：`changes`（有变更）或 `quiet`（根内无变化但执行过写操作，只含命令摘要，不含变更表）。

## 已知限制

- 只覆盖配置的根和深度，根之外看不到磁盘状态；根外只能靠「命令文本提到过哪些路径」间接提示，命令没提到的就无从得知。
- 观测根没扫全（条目超上限、子目录读不到）时，那个根整根跳过，报告开头直接写「本轮观测不完整」，不会把没扫到的算成删除；这轮也不更新基线。
- `moved` 是启发式判断（同名 + 同大小 + mtime 相近），报告里会标注。
- 归因是证据强度分级，标 `？` 就是没有证据。
- 调用区间依赖宿主给出 `tool/result`：命令用 `Start-Process` 或 `&` 拉起后台进程时，改动会发生在区间结束之后，只能落到宽窗。
- 跨进程、跨会话的手动改动只能落进「时间窗内」或「无法归因」。
- 不自动还原：只存路径不存内容，还原是 rollback 类插件的事。

## 开发

```bash
npm test   # 132 个测试
```

零运行时依赖，只用 `node:` 内置模块。观测走 `ctx.on('session/event')`，`inject: ['tools']` 仅用于注册 `aftermath_history`。

## License

MIT

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-firered-asr

DeepSeek Harness（dsh）的本地离线语音识别 provider。麦克风录音由本机 CPU 上的
**FireRedASR2-AED int8**（sherpa-onnx）转写，再用 **CT-Transformer** 补中文/英文标点；
官方语音输入 UI 的“识别器”列表会多出 **FireRedASR2-AED (int8)**；音频不上传、不落盘。

本包只注册一个 `host-local` 的 `speechToText` provider，不替换官方麦克风 UI，也不重复
插入官方 voice-input 的 `speech-to-text` / `api-speech-to-text` / `client-ui-voice-input`
行。官方 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-voice-input-bundle` 已启用时，安装本包后即可在
**设置 → 语音 → 识别器**看到并切换。

## 特性

- **本地 CPU 推理**：无 CUDA/ROCm、无 Python、无编译依赖；使用已发布的
  `sherpa-onnx-node@1.13.8` 及其预编译 ONNX Runtime。
- **复用运行中 DSH 的官方实现**：不把 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-speech-to-text` /
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-timeout` 装进 profile；启动时从 `DSH_INSTALL_DIR` 解析 DSH 自带的官方
  voice-input bundle，动态 import 官方 `validateWave` 与 timeout helper；官方服务行与
  FireRed provider 行保持独立，provider 行失败不会拖垮官方 SenseVoice 服务行。
- **按需准备**：激活只检查磁盘缓存，不下载、不加载模型；用户点“准备”才下载
  838,589,068 B 的 tar.bz2（以及 1.8 MB Silero VAD），并在解压后逐文件校验大小和
  SHA-256。
- **修正 SenseVoice 分段丢字**：≤ 30s 整段解码；> 30s 用 Silero VAD 切段，每段起点向
  前回填 0.3s、终点向后补 0.25s，且起点不越过上一段结束点、终点不超过总长；段间按
  CJK/英文规则拼接，而不是统一 `join(' ')`。
- **标点恢复（默认开）**：worker 内与 ASR 一起加载 64.7 MB 的中英 CT-Transformer
  标点模型，对**最终拼接后的整段文本**只调用一次 `addPunct`。标点模型缺失时激活会标记为
  **待准备**，官方“准备”按钮出现并下载标点包；准备/加载/推理失败时 fail-open 返回原文。
  `punctuation=false` 时完全不加载标点模型。
- **受管子进程**：一次只跑一个任务；回环 HTTP + 随机 bearer token；取消时终止并等待
  进程退出；空闲 5 分钟停止 worker，模型缓存保留，下次录音重新唤醒。

## 环境要求

- dsh `>= 0.2.2-rc.1 <= 0.5.0`（兼容检查开启 includePrerelease，0.2.2-rc.1/0.5.0/0.5.0-rc 可用，0.5.1 不保证），Node `>= 24.9.0`。
- 运行时必须存在 `DSH_INSTALL_DIR`（DSH 进程自带）；FireRed 从运行中的 DSH 安装解析官方
  speech-to-text/timeout 实现，不把官方包装进 profile。
- 官方 voice-input bundle（默认 web profile 已包含）：
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-voice-input-bundle`。
- CPU 推理；首次准备磁盘约 2.7 GB（ASR 压缩包/解压模型 + VAD + 64.7 MB 标点包 + 临时
  空间），运行内存约 3–4 GB，标点模型实测另加约 33 MB（保守按 <150 MB 估算）。16 核
  CPU 上 10s 音频约 1.5–3.2s 解码（RTF 0.15–0.32，实测见下）。

## 安装

### 从 tarball（推荐先验证构建产物）

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-firered-asr-0.1.3.tgz
```

### 从 GitHub（公开仓库）

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:744855705/dsh-firered-asr
```

### 从本地目录

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/packages/experimental/speech-to-text-firered
```

安装后重启/刷新 dsh（由 dsh 插件管理决定），首次使用：

1. 打开 **设置 → 语音 → 识别器**，选择 **FireRedASR2-AED (int8)**。
2. 点 **准备**：下载 ASR 模型 + VAD + 标点模型 → 解压 → 校验 → 加载 worker。下载进度
   显示真实字节；解压/校验/加载显示等待时间。准备阶段标点不可用不会阻塞 ASR（ready 后无标点）。
3. 回到输入框，点麦克风录音；停止后文本进入草稿，可编辑后发送。

模型缓存默认在 `~/.dsh/speech-to-text/firered`（bundle patch 里的 `dataRoot`）。

## 卸载 / 回滚

```bash
# 卸载 bundle（同时移除 firered-asr 行；模型缓存保留）
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-firered-asr

# 如确认不再使用，可删除模型缓存（用户自行确认路径）
rm -rf ~/.dsh/speech-to-text/firered
```

只想临时停用、不卸载：在 `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml` 追加

```yaml
- id: firered-asr
  disabled: true
```

本包不改官方 `packages/experimental/*` 现有文件；回滚只需移除本包/插件行。

## 配置

在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 中按 `id: firered-asr` 覆盖；`dataRoot` 必须是绝对路径。

| 字段 | 默认值 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `providerId` | `firered-local` | 注册 id；UI 用它切换。 |
| `dataRoot` | bundle patch 设为 `dshHomePath('speech-to-text','firered')` | 模型缓存、下载缓存、worker cwd 的绝对根目录。 |
| `modelDirectory` | — | 已解压目录（含 `encoder.int8.onnx`、`decoder.int8.onnx`、`tokens.txt`，可含 `silero_vad.onnx`）；跳过下载/解压，仍校验大小与 SHA-256。与 `archivePath` 互斥。 |
| `archivePath` | — | 离线 tar.bz2 绝对路径；跳过下载，仍解压并逐文件校验。与 `modelDirectory` 互斥。 |
| `modelUrl` | GitHub release 的固定 URL | 覆盖下载地址；**必须同时提供 `modelSha256`**，且只接受 HTTPS、无凭据。 |
| `modelSha256` | 固定值（默认 URL 时） | 覆盖时必填；同时会决定下载后校验的哈希。 |
| `punctuation` | `true` | 是否加载中英标点模型；`false` 时完全不构造 `OfflinePunctuation`。 |
| `punctuationModelDirectory` | — | 已解压标点目录（含 `model.int8.onnx`）；离线使用，跳过下载/解压，仍校验大小与 SHA-256。目录缺失时激活待准备；prepare 失败则 ready 无标点原文。 |
| `punctuationModelUrl` | GitHub release 的固定 URL | 标点包下载地址；覆盖时**必须同时提供 `punctuationModelSha256`**，只接受 HTTPS、无凭据。 |
| `punctuationModelSha256` | 固定值（默认 URL 时） | 覆盖标点包时必填；决定下载后校验的哈希。 |
| `threads` | 8 | CPU intra-op 线程数（ASR 与标点共用）。 |
| `directDecodeSeconds` | 30 | ≤ 此长度的录音整段解码，不切 VAD。 |
| `segmentSeconds` | 30 | VAD 最大语音段（再叠加两端 padding 后不超过此窗口）；也用于 VAD buffer 预算。 |
| `vadThreshold` | 0.5 | Silero 语音概率阈值。 |
| `minSpeechSeconds` | 0.1 | 最短语音段。 |
| `minSilenceSeconds` | 0.8 | 段间最小静音。 |
| `vadOnsetPaddingSeconds` | 0.3 | 每段起点向前回填；不越过上一段结束点。 |
| `vadTailPaddingSeconds` | 0.25 | 每段终点向后补齐；不超过录音总长。 |
| `maxAudioBytes` | 4194304（≈131s） | 解码 WAV 字节上限；超限在 worker 前拒绝。 |
| `prepareTimeoutMs` | 3600000 | 下载 + 解压 + 冷加载的预算。 |
| `inferenceTimeoutMs` | 600000 | 单次推理预算（CPU 慢，给足）。 |
| `idleTimeoutMs` | 300000 | 空闲后停止 worker；0 表示保持常驻。 |
| `maxPending` | 4 | 运行 + 排队任务上限。 |
| `graceMs` | 1000 | 终止 tar/worker 的宽限。 |
| `maxLogBytes` | 65536 | worker/tar stderr 保留上限。 |
| `maxResponseBytes` | 131072 | worker 响应上限。 |
| `progressIntervalMs` | 100 | 下载进度通知节流。 |

示例：使用本地 tar.bz2 与自定义缓存目录：

```yaml
- id: firered-asr
  name: 'dsh-firered-asr'
  config:
    dataRoot: /data/dsh-speech/firered
    archivePath: /data/models/sherpa-onnx-fire-red-asr2-zh_en-int8-2026-02-26.tar.bz2
    punctuationModelDirectory: /data/models/sherpa-onnx-punct-ct-transformer-zh-en-vocab272727-2024-04-12-int8
```

## 离线用法

1. 下载一次 ASR 包
   `sherpa-onnx-fire-red-asr2-zh_en-int8-2026-02-26.tar.bz2`（838,589,068 B，
   SHA-256 见下表），放到本机任意绝对路径。
2. 准备 Silero VAD：把 `silero_vad.onnx` 放到 `<dataRoot>/models/silero/silero_vad.onnx`，
   或放到 `modelDirectory` 同目录（推荐后者，`modelDirectory` 模式完全不需要网络）。
3. 标点模型（可选但默认开）：下载
   `sherpa-onnx-punct-ct-transformer-zh-en-vocab272727-2024-04-12-int8.tar.bz2`
   （64,717,756 B）并解压；把解压目录配给 `punctuationModelDirectory`（目录含
   `model.int8.onnx`）。不配或目录缺失时激活会提示准备；准备失败则 ready 但无标点原文。
4. 选择任一种 ASR 离线配置：
   - `archivePath`：插件解压到 `dataRoot/models/...`，逐文件校验；VAD 需按上一步预置。
   - `modelDirectory`：直接使用已解压目录（含 `silero_vad.onnx`），完全不下载、不解压。
5. `modelUrl`/`punctuationModelUrl` 覆盖时一定同时给对应 `modelSha256`/
   `punctuationModelSha256`；否则激活即报错，不会静默下载。

## 模型来源、版本与许可

| 资源 | 字节 | SHA-256 |
|---|---:|---|
| `sherpa-onnx-fire-red-asr2-zh_en-int8-2026-02-26.tar.bz2` | 838,589,068 | `43015b3f1643a5688b4821e8ed323473d38b798c4ec291471fe00df1bcfc4f1c` |
| `encoder.int8.onnx` | 817,286,833 | `54048d66b6e8f3c80ea7ce95efe794587b0fd81d7271651d0decd3803852ae82` |
| `decoder.int8.onnx` | 417,291,928 | `b840ce7196ae4a14d05ae84bbf56082b6b61ccec5610fda907dddbcea37354ff` |
| `tokens.txt` | 79,172 | `1bc613de2112d257e61a349c3e72d1b1a9cf19c33d3ca954197ad2171e5ea07b` |
| `silero_vad.onnx` | 1,807,522 | `a35ebf52fd3ce5f1469b2a36158dba761bc47b973ea3382b3186ca15b1f5af28` |
| `sherpa-onnx-punct-ct-transformer-zh-en-vocab272727-2024-04-12-int8.tar.bz2` | 64,717,756 | `c0d5aa5f8eeb686032345e180bedf39319dc2e0556781c6264bcadba8328a6e1` |
| `model.int8.onnx`（标点） | 75,519,198 | `65a3fb9f5ad7bfb96bf69e0dc4481df97f6ee60513c1d94ce981ba6effd524b1` |

- ASR 模型：**FireRedASR2-AED int8**，由 sherpa-onnx 转换；上游
  <https://www.modelscope.cn/models/FireRedTeam/FireRedASR2-AED>，
  下载自
  <https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx/releases/download/asr-models/sherpa-onnx-fire-red-asr2-zh_en-int8-2026-02-26.tar.bz2>。
- 标点模型：**CT-Transformer zh-en int8**，由 sherpa-onnx 转换；上游
  <https://www.modelscope.cn/models/iic/punc_ct-transformer_zh-cn-common-vocab272727-pytorch>
  （ModelScope 模型卡声明 **Apache-2.0**），下载自
  <https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx/releases/download/punctuation-models/sherpa-onnx-punct-ct-transformer-zh-en-vocab272727-2024-04-12-int8.tar.bz2>。
- 许可：ASR 与标点模型 **Apache-2.0**；sherpa-onnx / sherpa-onnx-node **Apache-2.0**；
  Silero VAD **MIT**。本插件代码 **MIT**。
- 模型权重**不在 npm 包里**，只在用户点“准备”时下载到本地缓存；本仓库不转存权重。
- 归属与更多第三方说明见 `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`。

## 分段与拼接（本插件与官方 SenseVoice 的差异）

- **≤ `directDecodeSeconds`**：整个 WAV 直接送入一个 stream，不切 VAD；首字/尾字不因
  分段边界丢失。
- **> `directDecodeSeconds`**：Silero VAD 产出绝对样本段；每段：
  1. `start = max(0, 段起点 - onsetPadding)`，再 `start = max(start, 上一段 paddedEnd)`；
  2. `end = min(totalSamples, 段终点 + tailPadding)`；
  3. 从原始录音 `slice(start, end)` 后单独 decode。
- 这样**每一段**都有起点回填和尾部 padding（不是只对第一段），且相邻段严格不重叠。
- 拼接：只看相邻两段的**边界字符**——任一侧是 CJK（Han/平假名/片假名/韩文）→ 直接
  相连；两侧都非 CJK → 一个空格。避免中文被空格切开，也避免“英文段尾 + 英文段首”被
  粘在一起（此前整段含中文会导致 `MONDAY`/`TODAY` 粘连）。

## 标点恢复

- `punctuation` 默认 `true`。worker 启动时与 ASR 一起构造
  `new sherpa.OfflinePunctuation({ model: { ctTransformer, numThreads, provider: 'cpu', debug: 0 } })`。
- 无论直接解码还是 VAD 分段，都先得到**最终拼接文本**，再只调用一次 `addPunct(text)`；
  不逐段调用，避免句间上下文被切断。
- 标点模型缺失（未准备/删缓存/离线目录不存在）时，激活 inspect 返回 `unprepared`，官方
  准备卡片出现“准备”按钮；点准备才下载/解压标点包，并进入现有 `model` 步骤。
- 准备阶段标点下载/解压失败、构造失败、`addPunct` 抛错或返回空串时，一律 fail-open：
  进入/保持 ready 并返回未加标点原文，只写 warn，绝不丢转写；已加载 worker 的标点文件
  被删也返回原文。
- `punctuation=false` 时完全不加载标点模型，内存/启动开销为零；不新增
  `SpeechPreparationStepKind`。
- 标点包下载失败不阻塞 ASR：准备仍可进入 ready，只是本次 worker 不加载标点；重启/重载后
  会再次显示“准备”。

## 开发、测试与性能

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm test                 # 94 个单测：配置/WAV/哈希/padding/CJK/队列/取消/协议/注册/兼容/标点/fail-open
# 真实模型集成（ASR 目录含 silero_vad.onnx；标点目录含 model.int8.onnx）：
FIRERED_E2E_MODEL_DIR=/abs/model \
FIRERED_E2E_VAD=/abs/silero_vad.onnx \
FIRERED_E2E_PUNCT_DIR=/abs/punct \
  pnpm test:integration
# 5/10/30s RTF、冷启动、峰值 RSS（标点开/关各跑一次）：
FIRERED_MODEL_DIR=/abs/model FIRERED_PUNCT_MODEL=/abs/punct/model.int8.onnx pnpm bench
FIRERED_MODEL_DIR=/abs/model FIRERED_PUNCT=0 pnpm bench
```

本机实测（Linux x64，16 核 AMD CPU，无 CUDA，`threads=8`，`sherpa-onnx-node@1.13.8`）。
主机共享且本轮负载更高（`/proc/loadavg` 6–20）；以下同时给出 0.1.1/0.1.2 的 ASR-only bench、
早先较低负载的 ASR-only 区间，以及 ASR+标点的隔离成本：

| 片段 | ASR-only | ASR + 标点 | RTF（ASR-only / +标点） |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 5s | 1.25s | 1.25s | 0.250 / 0.249 |
| 10s | 3.21s | 3.12s | 0.321 / 0.312 |
| 30s | 14.30s | 14.57s | 0.477 / 0.486 |

- 早先较低负载的 ASR-only 实测：5s 0.68–1.20s（RTF 0.14–0.24）、10s 1.65–2.79s
  （0.17–0.28）、30s 8.87–13.34s（0.30–0.44）；负载波动大于标点差异。
- 标点增量：`addPunct` 本身 0.8–8.4ms（0/1/3 转写为 2.8–8.4ms；相对 ASR 时间
  0.1–0.5%）；同主机 5/10/30s 的 RTF 变化为 -0.2% / -2.6% / +1.9%（最大 +1.9%，
  <5%）。标点包下载 64.7MB；峰值 RSS ASR-only 2.444GB → +标点 2.479GB（+约 33MB，
  <150MB）；`punctuation=false` 时为零。
- 冷加载：ASR-only 3.18s；+标点 3.28s；worker 端到端冷启动 4.16s（含 hash/spawn/两模型）。
- ASR+标点 integration：`0.wav` 10.05s → 2.67s；`1.wav` 5.1s → 1.59s；`3.wav` 8.83s →
  2.92s；66.3s → 12 段 / 15.50s（共享主机高负载）；三条文本均含中文标点。
- 规划建议：共享主机按 RTF ≈0.3–0.5 估算；120s 录音约 36–60s，worker 需约 2.5–4GB。
- 原始数据：`bench/results.json`、`bench-asr.json`、`bench-punct.json`；脚本
  `scripts/bench.mjs`；复现命令见 `bench/README.md`。

## 已知限制

- **CPU only**：AMD 无 CUDA/ROCm；不提供 GPU provider，也不自动降级到云端。
- **无流式**：官方 `SpeechProvider` 只接受完整录音；本插件不做实时字幕。
- **无热词**：AED 路径不支持 hotwords；不要设置 `hotwords`。
- **AED 有效窗口**：单段解码不超过约 30s；超长录音靠 VAD 分段 + padding。
- **标点模型可选**：默认下载 64.7 MB；缺包、删缓存、离线目录缺失时激活显示待准备；准备
  失败、加载失败或 `addPunct` 失败时 fail-open 返回无标点原文；已加载 worker 的标点文件
  被删仍可转写。想要零标点开销时设 `punctuation: false`。
- **标点内存**：标点模型实测约 +33 MB RSS（保守 <150 MB）；内存紧张时关闭标点。
- **首次加载慢/内存高**：int8 权重约 1.23 GB，ONNX Runtime 加载后 RSS 约 1.8 GB（10s
  片段）/2.4 GB（30s 批量 bench），长音频会继续增长；`expectedMemoryBytes` 只是规划估计。
- **录音上限**：`maxAudioBytes` 默认 4 MiB ≈ 131s；更长的录音在进入 worker 前被拒绝。
- **离线 VAD**：`archivePath` 模式仍需 VAD；请按“离线用法”预置，否则会尝试下载。
- **解压依赖系统 `tar`**：Linux/macOS 自带；Windows 10+ 的 bsdtar 可用。若环境没有
  `tar`，准备阶段会明确报错。
- **模型哈希固定**：`modelDirectory`/`archivePath` 与 `punctuationModelDirectory` 必须是
  上述 int8 发布版；换模型（如 fp32、v1、不同标点模型）需自行改 `runtime/assets.json`
  并重跑校验，不在本包支持范围。
- **标点离线**：`punctuationModelDirectory` 指向已解压标点目录；不配且无缓存时会尝试
  下载。标点包下载失败不会阻塞 ASR。
- **宿主官方 helper**：`DSH_INSTALL_DIR` 缺失，或运行中 DSH 的官方 `validateWave`/timeout
  API 发生破坏性变化时，FireRed provider 行会明确失败；官方 SenseVoice 服务行独立，不会
  因此整体禁用。

## 许可

本插件代码以 **MIT** 发布（见 `LICENSE`）。模型与运行时许可见
`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`；模型权重不随包分发，下载后仍受上游 Apache-2.0 约束。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# 梁文峰 / 梁文谷 峰谷价提示器 扩展鲸鱼联动版

> DeepSeek Harness 侧边栏插件：显示当前是高峰还是空闲、距离切换的倒计时，以及空闲时段的 5 折提示。扩展版增加了与小鲸鱼挂件的联动，不再有需要每年手改的数据文件，保证与小鲸鱼的峰谷价完全同步，也不会出现日历没写，峰谷价判断错误。

## 它做什么

在侧边栏底部常驻一行，实时回答三件事：

| 问题 | 显示 |
| --- | --- |
| 现在贵不贵 | `省钱中`（空闲）/ `挨宰中`（高峰） |
| 还有多久变 | 秒级倒计时到下一次切换 |
| 能省多少 | 空闲时段 5 折（官方：空闲价为高峰价的一半） |

时段规则取自 [dsh-whale-widget]小鲸鱼挂件，相比原版做了与小鲸鱼挂件的联动 [dsh-whale-widget]。推荐安装小鲸鱼。
![whale](assets/whale.png)

## 峰谷数据从哪来

v1.2.0 起不再自带节假日表，改成**link到 [dsh-whale-widge](https://github.com/moonlight328/dsh-whale-widget) 。**

```
GET /dsh-whale/balance.json
→ { isPeak: boolean, peakNextChangeAt: <unix 秒>, peakHolidays: [...], version: "0.4.2", ... }
```

- `isPeak`：对方按官方口径（周末 + 法定节假日 + 两个窗口）算好的结论；
- `peakNextChangeAt`：对方算好的下一次切换时刻；
- `peakHolidays`：它内置的法定节假日清单，本插件只用它做展示。

节日数据的年度维护交给 whale-widget（它每年 11 月需要补下一年），本插件不再有需要每年手改的数据文件。

### 降级路径

whale-widget 没装、被关、返回 401、或者载荷不合法，都会**静默退回本地规则**：周末 → 空闲；工作日只看两个窗口。这条本地规则在官方口径下对周末与工作日永远成立，唯一会错的情形是法定放假日落在工作日（元旦、春节、清明这类）——那天会显示成"高峰"，实际是谷价。

所以界面上有三种可见状态：

| 状态 | 表现 | 含义 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 徽章正常 | 实线 | 数据来自 whale-widget |
| 徽章灰色虚线 | 悬停提示「本地推算」 | 没拿到宿主数据，用本地规则 |
| 徽章点状 | 悬停提示「与宿主不一致」 | 双方判断相左，按宿主为准 |

想确认到底接上没有：把鼠标停在那行字上，title 会写明数据源；走本地规则时后面还会带上原因（`HTTP 401` / `payload` / 网络错误），照着它就能定位是哪一环断了。

### 元数据的鉴权

`/dsh-whale/*` 全部在 DSH 的信任栅栏后面：Host/Origin 必须同源，并且需要一个签名的会话 cookie（`dsh-client-connection` 的 `BrowserAuth`，`isAuthenticated` 校验的就是它）。页面里的同源请求会自动带上这个 cookie，所以插件在侧边栏里能取到；从 shell 里 `curl` 同一个地址会得到 401 —— 那是没有 cookie，不是插件写错了。

## 安装

本包是 DSH bundle（`dsh.bundle.patch` + `dsh.client`），Host 半是空实现，界面全在构建产物 `client.js` 里。

1. 克隆本仓库到本机；
2. 用 DSH 的插件管理器（`plugin_manager` / Plugins 页的本地安装）指向该目录；
3. 侧边栏底部出现提示条，无需重启 Host。

换机器重新安装一次即可。

## 目录结构

```
src/logic.mjs        峰谷判定、边界推算、宿主载荷校验、describe() 聚合（纯函数，可测）
src/frames.js        31 张 base64 档位图
src/style.js         样式（跟随 DSH 主题变量）
src/ui.template.js   组件与注册逻辑，构建时把上面三块内联进来
build.mjs            内联构建 → client.js
test.mjs             逻辑自测（76 项）
```

`client.js` 是构建产物，不要手改；改 `src/` 后跑 `node build.mjs` 重建，再 `node test.mjs` 自测。

## 显示效果

峰价（工作日 9:00–12:00、14:00–18:00）：

![峰价实机截图](assets/peak.jpg)

谷价（其余时段，含周末和法定节假日）：

![谷价实机截图](assets/valley.jpg)

- 谷价：`省钱中`，倒计时告诉你还有多久进峰；
- 峰价：`挨宰中`，倒计时告诉你还有多久回谷；
- 侧边栏收成 56px 图标条时只留头像。

## 为什么头像会变

31 张档位图（`00` 普通人 → `30` 梁祖），按当前时段的进度线性切换，**并且带方向**：

- 峰段：档位从 `0` 走到 `30`，人像一路"梁祖化"；
- 谷段：档位从 `30` 退回 `0`，人像一路退烧。

所以每次峰谷切换，头像都会从一端跳到另一端（峰起 → 档 0，谷起 → 档 30），段内再一档一档挪。谷段（尤其跨夜那段 15 小时）一档要走半小时，看着慢是正常的——它不是动画，是进度指示器。它只是视觉反馈，不参与任何判断；不看头像也不影响使用。

## 其他配置

`src/logic.mjs` 顶部还有两个常量：

- `PEAK_WINDOWS`：高峰时段（分钟数，默认 `[9:00–12:00]`、`[14:00–18:00]`）；
- `TZ_OFFSET_MS`：计价时区偏移，默认 UTC+8（中国 1991 年后无夏令时，固定偏移安全）。

时区按北京时间算，与宿主机时区设置无关。

## 副作用

- 13:59 会莫名焦虑；
- 可能为了看「梁祖」故意拖到 17:59；
- 不会让你的 token 变便宜，一分都不会。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# @automagik/acp-dsh

Agents other than DSH's own, as DeepSeek Harness models, over the
[Agent Client Protocol](https://agentclientprotocol.com) (ACP). The design is
[RFC 0003](../../docs/rfcs/0003-model-routes-and-acp.md).

- **Agents as DSH models.** Each agent is a provider route (`acp-<agent>`) whose models are the
  agent's own (Claude Code's Opus, Sonnet, Haiku…; Codex's GPT models), each with the reasoning
  efforts the agent offers for it. A chat or a Bot picks one like any model. DSH keeps the
  Session, its history and the sidebar.
- **The agent's own models and efforts.** They are read from the agent over ACP: its session
  config options of category `model` and `thought_level`. A probe starts the adapter, opens a
  session it never prompts (no turn, no tokens), reads the models, then picks each one to read
  its efforts, since an agent rebuilds that list per model. The result is kept in
  `$AUTOMAGIK_HOME/acp/catalog/<route>.json`, so the next start lists it at once while a new probe
  runs; a new adapter release probes again. Before any probe has answered, a short list stands
  in (Claude Code: `default`, `opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku` at low, medium or high effort; Codex:
  `default`). The model `default` is always listed: it is whatever the agent's own settings
  choose. An effort's default is the person's own setting for that model.
- **The Session's model and effort, before each prompt.** The agent's session is put on the
  Session's model, then its effort (the model first: the efforts are that model's). No effort
  leaves the agent's own. A model or effort the agent does not offer fails the turn, naming what
  it offers.
- **DSH tool cards and approvals.** With `dshTools` off (the kill switch), the agent runs its own
  tools. Each tool call it makes ends the model step with a call to `acp_tool`, a tool registered
  in that agent's scope only. DSH writes the `tool/call` and `tool/result` rows and draws the
  card (a terminal for a command, a diff for an edit, the generic card otherwise). When the agent
  asks permission for the call, `acp_tool` asks DSH's approval service
  (`approval/asked`, `approval/decided`) and gives the agent DSH's answer. On DSH's Auto
  review level that answer is the review. A call the reviewer allowed, or that the person
  allowed in the dialog the reviewer raised, gets `allow_once` for the agent's first question
  about it, with no second dialog; this holds in a subagent child too. These still ask as before:
  a later question, a call the agent changed after its review (in its question or after it), an
  agent that offers no `allow_once`, and a level that changed since the call.
- **DSH's own tools over the bridge (`dshTools`).** On, the agent gets the Session's preset tool
  set (standard, or cordis in creator mode) over one stdio MCP server per ACP session, named
  `dsh` and spawned by the adapter with that session's arguments. The bridge has no port; it
  reaches this plugin over a loopback back-channel with a per-session credential
  (`DSH_BRIDGE_CREDENTIAL`), which binds a request to its Session and is revoked with the
  bridge. Every DSH tool call is approved in DSH under the Session's level before it runs,
  whatever the agent's own allow rules or hooks say, and the bridge writes the `tool/call` and
  `tool/result` rows the chat shows. `acp-claude` runs with its built-in tools off
  (`_meta.disableBuiltInTools`); a structured call that is not an MCP name is recorded as
  `plugin:acp-dsh/toolset-drift` and its turn is cancelled — the detector runs at every session
  start, and it detects and cancels because the update arrives after the call began.
  DSH's `read_image` works for Claude Code because acp-dsh declares its models as taking images;
  other ACP agents keep no declaration.
  `acp-codex` has no such switch, so it is bridged only with an explicit `dshTools: true`;
  absent or `false` means no bridge and its built-ins stay its own tool set. Until a structured
  name is proven in its tool calls, it draws no ACP card for an MCP call. The person's
  own MCP servers load beside the bridge with their own tools and sign-ins: DSH hands the session
  only the `dsh` bridge, so any other `mcp__<server>__<tool>` is the CLI's own user-scope config
  (claude-agent-acp merges the person's settings MCP servers into the session), it passes the
  drift allowlist by design, and DSH's Auto review does not gate it: the agent's own rules and
  sign-in govern that call. A tool-list change
  (a preset or level change) is announced on `acp-claude` and arrives through `session/fork`
  plus `session/close` on `acp-codex`; a bridge that never lists its tools fails the turn
  (`acp_bridge_missing`) before the prompt. **Auto:** DSH's Auto preset is full access's sandbox
  with asks answered by auto-review. A bridge call adds one marked, tool-only assistant block:
  the advertisement the Session format requires before its tool/call row, which the reviewer
  reads too, and which is removed from the surface once the call settles and never replayed to
  another provider; the reviewer sees the bridge tool, its redacted arguments and its schema
  before the body runs. A denial is `AUTO_REVIEW_DENIED`, a failed reviewer refuses with
  `AUTO_REVIEW_FAILED`, a review past its deadline is `AUTO_REVIEW_TIMEOUT`, and the call never
  runs. A call that comes between two steps of a turn while the agent's prompt is still running
  (after a `step/end`, before the next `step/start`) waits for the next step, at most 30 s, and is
  recorded and reviewed there; it ends with no rows if the turn ends, its caller goes away, the
  bridge is revoked or the turn is stopped (#969). Otherwise a Manual or Full call with no open
  step is `BRIDGE_NO_STEP` (Auto: `AUTO_REVIEW_NO_STEP`); one whose advertisement or
  call row cannot be written is `BRIDGE_RECORD_FAILED`, and the call does not run. The rows' call
  id is the agent's own `_meta.callId` only when it is 1 to 128 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . : -`
  and does not start with `acp_` (the mirror's ids); otherwise the plugin mints `bridge_<16 hex>`
  and logs the replacement. **Codex's MCP approvals.** With `dshTools` on, `acp-codex`'s MCP calls
  get no mirror card (it gives them no structured name), so a `session/request_permission` Codex
  sends for one (codex-acp's MCP tool approval) is answered at once: allow once for the `dsh`
  server (the bridge's own approval is the one dialog), the agent's reject option for any other
  or unnamed server, which is logged (#969). **A call that
  outlives its step (#957).** The agent runs its calls in parallel, and the bridge puts no
  deadline on one (a long wait, a slow command and an open approval dialog are legitimate).
  Before its step ends, an own-tool card waits for bridge calls of that step asking for approval
  or under Auto review to write their results, with no deadline; Full-access calls are unchanged.
  Stop, revoke and the prompt's end release the wait.
  The write guard still closes calls a forced boundary leaves open before `step/end` and drops
  their late results; the agent still gets the real answer.
  Each call has its own abort controller: Stop, the end of its turn and a caller that
  went away (an MCP `notifications/cancelled`, a closed request) stop that call as
  `BRIDGE_CANCELLED` and keep the bridge. A call whose `tool/call` row cannot be written is
  answered with DSH's own not-started row, and a bridge revoked with a call in flight keeps
  the guard until that call is over. The reviewer
  goes to the same non-agent side model as a Session title. Manual asks (one dialog), Full
  access does not. A Session that moves between providers carries its transcript
  redacted at each crossing — the replay out to an agent, and the transcript handed back to a
  native provider — and each crossing writes a provider-boundary row the chat shows,
  "Switching to X": it is written before the reply and claims no answer, since the call can
  still fail after it. An agent whose CLI is signed out (ACP's `auth_required`, when its session
  opens or on a prompt) fails the turn as `MODEL_ACCESS_REQUIRED`, not `ACP_AGENT`. The
  reasoning effort the Session ran on crosses with it, both ways, when the target model offers
  that level (matched by id, else by name), replacing the target default DSH records on a model
  change; an effort DSH itself defaulted is not carried. The agents' levels are their own
  `thought_level` ids: Claude Code lists low, medium, high, xhigh and max, and Codex lists low,
  medium, high, xhigh, max and ultra, per model. A target with no reasoning levels, without
  that one, or whose levels cannot be read writes a notice row saying so and runs on its own.
  A switch back before the agent has answered drops the agent's chosen level; the native
  target's own default applies.
- **Only the chat reaches the agent.** DSH's side requests on an ACP route never become
  prompts. At the `llm/stream` waterfall a Session title (`purpose: session-title`) goes to a
  model that answers on its own, without the agent's effort. That is the first model the team
  can reach: DSH's default model (`agentDefaultModel`) when it is not an agent; else a
  `sideModel` the person chose; else each configured non-agent route in turn (its first model,
  at most eight); and only then the built-in DeepSeek Flash fallback. A credential or
  missing-route failure on one candidate moves to the next, so a team without a DeepSeek key
  reviews and titles on the model it does have; only no answer at all refuses. Auto review
  (`purpose: auto-review`) takes the same route, with its messages redacted first. Every other
  side request on an ACP route, a compaction summary included, is refused (`UNSUPPORTED`): it
  would carry the agent's whole chat to another provider, and the agent manages its own context.
  Sessions on any other route are left alone.
- **A switch onto an agent passes DSH's compaction guard.** `compaction-basic` prices every model
  switch on the destination's context window, which an agent does not declare, so a switch onto
  an agent in a Session with a request header used to fail with `MODEL_SWITCH_COMPACTION_FAILED`.
  This plugin wraps the engine's `compactPressure` (`src/host/pressure.js`, the method's only
  Automagik owner): an agent destination needs no compaction, every other destination goes to the
  engine unchanged. The wrapper is adopted when an agent is created and on its requests (a
  reloaded compaction plugin is a new engine), delegates to whatever is below it at call time, and
  on dispose unwinds only when it is on top. The method is private to `compaction-basic`; a guard
  test pins it, and a DSH flag for it is proposed upstream (RFC 0023). A switch *off* an agent is
  the destination's own business: for a Bot, the Bot team decides before the guard (its README,
  "Long chats").
- **Host only.** No browser half, so the plugin cannot stop the web UI from loading. With no
  agent CLI installed it registers no route. The welcome draws its setup from the `acpAgents`
  service below.
- **The Session's level, as the agent's own mode.** Before each prompt the agent's ACP session
  mode follows the Session: Manual is Claude Code's `default` mode, whatever default mode its
  own settings name; Codex runs in the sandbox that matches DSH's. DSH Auto review is Claude Code's `auto`
  and Codex's `agent`; it is the preset's identity, never just its sandbox and ask, so a custom
  preset with the same knobs keeps Manual (and the bridge's own approval). Full access lets every
  call through, as it does DSH's own tools. An agent that does not offer the strict mode fails
  the turn instead of running in its own default.
  A Workspace Session on unbridged Codex can instead take `agent` when the Bot team's
  `ownMode` answerer returns exactly `true` twice, before the prompt. After that agent session
  has attempted the own mode, any Workspace prompt that does not take it re-sends and confirms
  strict `workspace-write` (or its chat profile below), even if cached; refusal ends the agent
  session and fails the turn.
  Sessions that never attempt the own mode keep the usual mode cache and failure handling.
  Auto never requests `bypassPermissions` or
  `agent-full-access`. Codex's own reviewer decides those steps, based on the
  [Codex 0.167.0 capture](test/fixtures/permission-payloads/README.md); later versions may
  decide differently. Any approval Codex still requests goes to the person.
- **An agent that stops answering never holds the chat.** Its start (`initialize`,
  `session/new`, the bridge's first list) has 60 seconds, and each request after that and
  before a prompt (a model, an effort, a mode, a fork, a close) has 15. Past the deadline, or
  on Stop, the agent's process and its bridge are ended and the turn says what happened. A
  start that hangs is usually a CLI waiting for the person (a first-run question, a keychain
  dialog, an update), so that message says to open it once in a terminal. Stop ends the turn
  at once and gives the agent 5 seconds to end its prompt, because `session/cancel` is only a
  notification. An agent that ignores it is ended, and the next message starts a new agent
  session with the chat replayed to it (with `dshTools: false`, the new-session notice
  instead). A message sent while the agent is still on its last prompt waits those 5 seconds,
  then gets a new session in the same turn. Ending an agent ends what it started too (the
  command behind a stuck tool call): the agent leads its own process group, which is asked to
  end and killed 3 seconds later if any of it is left; on Windows its process tree is killed.
- **Claude Code keeps the person's own settings.** It loads their Claude Code settings (user,
  project and local) and asks DSH only for what those leave as "ask". A call their allow rules,
  saved "always allow" rules or PreToolUse/PermissionRequest hooks approve runs with no DSH
  dialog. This is the owner's decision (RFC 0003, Decided).

### Native-tools mode (`nativeTools`, #1564)

Claude Code keeps its own tools and Automagik adds its extras. The owner's words: "my intention
is to use claude code + automagik extras, not replace claude code native`s with automagik`s,
that makes your harness lose all your power."

- **The setting.** `nativeTools` in this plugin's config (the `acpAgents` service's plugin,
  `acp-dsh`), hidden from settings forms like `dshTools`. Absent (the default) or `false` is
  today's behaviour for everyone. `true` turns it on for every Claude Code Session; an object
  turns it on per Bot, by the Bot's name, or per DSH Session id. A key that says `false` wins
  over one that says `true`. For one Bot, in the profile patch:

  ```yaml
  - id: acp-dsh
    name: "@automagik/acp-dsh"
    config:
      nativeTools:
        Automagik: true
  ```

  It is read at each turn's start: a flip takes effect on that Session's next turn, in a new
  agent session (the replay carries the chat to it). Only `acp-claude` takes it (the only agent
  whose built-ins the bridge turns off); with `dshTools: false` it has no effect, since the
  agent then already runs only its own tools.
- **What changes when on.** The session starts with `_meta.disableBuiltInTools: false`, so
  Claude Code has its Agent (subagents), Bash, Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob, Skill, TodoWrite
  and the rest. The `dsh` bridge stays on but drops DSH's twin of each built-in and the DSH
  subagent family (`NATIVE_TWIN_TOOLS` in `src/host/backchannel.js`: `bash`, `job_*`, `read`,
  `write`, `edit`, `read_image`, `apply_patch`, `str_replace_editor`, `glob`, `grep`, `skill`,
  `todo_write`, `subagent`, `subagent_fork`, `list_agents`, `send_message`, `interrupt_agent`,
  `wait_agent`, `list_subagent_models`, and `web_search`/`web_fetch`/`exit_plan_mode` once they
  are offered). Everything else stays: the Bot team's tools (`message_bot`, `ask_user`,
  `show_view`, `remember`/`recall`, groups, secrets, browser, mail...), goals, `workflow`,
  `working_directory` and schedules. A built-in call is no longer drift.
- **Approvals stay DSH's.** Each native call ends the model step with its `acp_tool` mirror
  card, exactly as with the bridge off: when Claude Code asks permission, DSH's approval answers
  it at the Session's level, and a refusal reaches Claude Code as its own reject option before
  the call runs. The hard ask rules (`CLAUDE_HARD_ASK`) are injected as session settings, so the
  person's allow rules cannot silently skip the ask for those Bash cases. A subagent's nested
  call asks while its Agent card is still waiting: that card asks DSH for it, naming the nested
  call, and the nested call's own card follows, already answered. That nested ask does not go
  through DSH's Auto review: it goes straight to DSH's approval request, so the person's
  dialog answers it (or the Bot team's judge, where one is set; a delegated child that may never
  ask is refused). An unattended Session at Auto therefore waits on the person at each nested
  ask.

  | Level | Claude Code mode | What asks DSH | What can bypass DSH |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Manual | `default` | every native call its own settings leave as "ask"; DSH's dialog answers | a call its own allow rules or hooks allow (the hard asks still ask) |
  | Auto | `auto` | only what Claude Code's auto mode asks about; DSH Auto review answers a top-level call, the person answers a subagent's nested call | whatever its auto mode runs without asking |
  | Full | `bypassPermissions` | nothing; no hard asks injected | every native call |

  Manual is the guarded level; Auto is convenience, and its review sees only what reaches the
  mirror.
- **Native commands and edits run in Claude Code, outside DSH's file sandbox.** DSH's sandbox,
  its read-before-write policy and its write guard do not see them; the person's OS permissions
  and Claude Code's own permission mode and rules are the boundary. Claude Code's `CLAUDE.md`
  memory is the project's own context, loaded by the CLI; the Bot's memory stays `remember`.

## Agents

Unbridged Claude Code receives per-session ask rules for recursive deletion, destructive Git,
infrastructure and database shell commands at every asking level. These explicit rules also
ask in Claude's auto mode. They are never written to a CLI home and are absent at Full access,
where explicit ask rules would otherwise still ask. Crossing Full access restarts the unbridged
Claude session with the chat replayed, adding or removing the rules; staying at a level reuses it.
Bridged Claude has its built-in tools disabled, so DSH checks its calls instead.

Codex's own tools are excluded: prompt rules under Full access (`approval_policy = never`)
refuse rather than ask, its session-flags configuration has no rules folder, and in `agent`
mode prompt rules reach Codex's reviewer rather than the person. Replacing its entire reviewer
policy or changing codex-acp needs a separate owner decision.

| Route | Agent | Runs | Adapter (newest release) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `acp-claude` | Claude Code | managed or existing `claude` (`CLAUDE_CODE_EXECUTABLE`) | `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` |
| `acp-codex` | Codex | managed or existing `codex` (`CODEX_PATH`) | `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp` |
| `acp-hermes` | Hermes | existing `hermes`, started as `hermes acp` | none: the CLI is the ACP server |
| `acp-antigravity` | Antigravity | existing `agy`, started as `agy acp` | none: the CLI is the ACP server |
| `acp-omp` | omp | existing `omp`, started as `omp acp` | none: the CLI is the ACP server |
| `acp-fake` | `dev/fake-agent.mjs`, set as `fakeAgent` | Node | none; tests only |

An agent is offered when its managed CLI is ready, or an existing CLI is on PATH or where its
installer puts it (`~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, …). The settings `claude: false` or `codex: false` take one away;
`hermes`, `antigravity` and `omp` are off until set to `true` (below). They are
live settings: switching one (from the welcome's Connect AI, its Settings page *Claude Code and
Codex*, or the plugin's own settings form) offers or withdraws the agent at once, with no
restart, and a connector that lands puts its model in the picker the same way
(`llm/adapters-updated`).

### Native-ACP agents: Hermes, Antigravity, omp

These three speak ACP themselves, so there is no adapter package and nothing is installed for
them: the plugin starts the CLI it finds with `acp` (`src/host/agents.js`, `launch`). What
differs from Claude Code and Codex:

- **Off until turned on.** `hermes`, `antigravity` and `omp` are live settings that default to
  `false`. Turning one on is the person's word that Automagik may use the sign-in that CLI
  already has on this computer, shared with their terminal. No account is read for them (none
  of the three has a command that names one), so the account record and its confirm step
  (below) stay Claude Code's and Codex's.
- **Never installed by Automagik.** A CLI that is not here is listed as missing with its
  install page (`cli.state: 'missing'`, `connector.state: 'no-cli'`), never hidden and never
  "installing". Once found, the connector reads `ready` with `native: true`.
- **Sign-in in a terminal.** There is no sign-in from a Bot's chat: `loginStart` refuses with
  `acp-login/terminal` and the command (`hermes acp --setup`, `agy acp --login`, `omp login`),
  and a signed-out turn fails as `MODEL_ACCESS_REQUIRED` naming the same command. Whether the
  agent is signed in is what its own ACP session said: `true` when the session the model read
  opens, `false` on ACP's `auth_required`. That read runs when the CLI changes and once a day,
  and again when the person asks (`refresh()`) while it is not signed in; no other check opens
  a session, because each of these agents keeps every session it opens in its own history.
  A session that opens does not prove a provider key works: a turn that then answers
  `auth_required` reads as signed out at once.
- **Models.** Antigravity offers its models and efforts as config options, as the adapters do.
  Hermes offers them only as the session's own list (`models` in the `session/new` answer,
  switched with `session/set_model`); the plugin reads that list when the agent has no model
  option. omp offers no model list over ACP: it is one model, `default`, its own setting.
- **The level.** Each is put in its own `default` mode before every prompt, whatever the
  Session's level, and what it asks is answered by DSH's approval under that level. Its own
  permission settings still decide what it asks about. One that does not offer `default`
  fails the turn. A table agent with no mode for DSH's level would say so once in the chat.
- **No DSH tool bridge.** DSH's tools do not reach them, even with `dshTools: true`: their
  tool naming over ACP is not proven the way Claude Code's was, and an unrecognised bridge
  call would draw two cards and ask twice. They keep their own tools; the transcript replay on
  a model switch reaches them like any agent.

`dshTools` (live, no schema default) is the bridge, its DSH approval, the drift detector and live
switching above. Absent means the per-agent default: `acp-claude` bridges because its adapter can
drop its own built-in tools; `acp-codex` does not, because it cannot. Codex is bridged only with
an explicit `true`; absent or `false` means no bridge, and Codex keeps its own built-in tools as
its only tool set. An explicit `false` is the kill switch for Claude too: the 2026-11-03
behaviour, where each agent keeps its own tools and its own approvals. The key is public and
stays writable through
DSH's settings service or the profile patch, but it is hidden from settings forms (`.hidden()`):
it is a rollback lever, not a preference. Flipping it either way ends the running agent sessions
and revokes their bridges at once; the DSH Session keeps its transcript and the next turn starts
afresh under the new setting. A flip is also announced on the plugin context as
`acp-dsh/dsh-tools-changed` with `{ on }`: DSH delivers `loader/volatile-update` only to the
plugin whose config changed, so another plugin would never see this one. The Bot team watches
that event, so turning the switch off moves its Claude Bots back at once, and turning it on moves
them again. A listener that throws is logged as a warning; the flip itself and its ended sessions
still hold, and the Bot team reverses at its next start (the route reads off or gone). The default
moves Claude Bots once per team to `acp-claude` (the Bot team's README,
"Claude on ACP"); the bridge probe in `bridge()` still gates the move.

The transcript replay is independent of the bridge: only an explicit `false` turns it off.

| `dshTools` | Claude Code: tools | Claude Code: replay | Codex: tools | Codex: replay |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| absent | DSH bridge, its own off | yes | its own only | yes |
| `true` | DSH bridge | yes | DSH bridge and its own | yes |
| `false` | its own only | no | its own only | no |

With the Codex conversation open, choose **Account → Bot settings → Feedback** and look for its
row under **Permissions**. When the row includes agent details, it reports the DSH bridge state.
To confirm delivery, check the receiving Bot’s chat. If your team has a native browser Bot
(such as `@browse`), you can ask it directly to open a page. In a Bot conversation that offers
a **Browser** tab, you can also open it from **Details → Browser**.

So with `dshTools` absent Codex sees the chat but not the team's tools; those need an explicit
`true` (two tool sets). A replay reaches an agent in each of these cases, redacted and capped at
120,000 characters, the oldest messages dropped first with a marker: a move from another
provider (with its "Switching to X" row); a new agent session in a chat that already has answers
(after a restart, or a session a crossing or a flip ended), with no row since the chat stayed on
that agent; and a live session resumed after the chat answered elsewhere (a move off Codex keeps
its session), which gets only the turns it missed, from its own last answer on, with the row. A
Bot part's handoff package (a relay marked `handoff`) is carried as the record it is: in the
part's first turn it stays in the prompt beside the person's words, and once the Bot team has
answered that turn itself, the next new session gets it in the replay. Both pass the redactor.
With `false`, an agent sees only its own session, and a new one in a chat with answers writes the
"does not see this chat's earlier messages" row instead.

`sideModel` (`{ provider, model }`, default `deepseek-official/deepseek-flash`, live) is the
model a side request tries after DSH's default model. An explicit value the person chose is tried
before the configured non-agent routes (each in turn, its first model); the default DeepSeek
Flash is tried last, so a team without a DeepSeek key titles and reviews on the model it does
have. An agent route set here is ignored, and a credential or missing-route failure falls
through to the next candidate.

## The `acpAgents` service

A settings page reads the agents through this host service; the plugin stays host only.

| Method | Does |
|---|---|
| `status()` | Each agent: `{ id, key, name, on, cli: { found, installUrl, signInHint?, state, managed, version?, error?, diagnostic?, logPath?, updating? }, connector: { state, native?, version?, error?, diagnostic?, logPath?, updating?, startError?, previous?, rolledBack? }, signedIn?, signInCheck?, consent?, model: { provider, id, name, listed }, restartNeeded }`. CLI state is `missing`, `installing`, `failed` or `ready`; connector state is `off`, `no-cli`, `installing`, `failed` or `ready`. `connector.previous` is the release a failed start goes back to, while it is on disk; `connector.rolledBack` is `{ from, to, at, reason }` while a release that failed to start is held back. `connector.startError` is the short reason an installed connector's last start failed, until a session opens or Retry reinstalls it; a connector being reinstalled reads `installing`. A failed connector install always carries `error`; `diagnostic` (the end of the installer's output) and `logPath` (the file it was written to, shown from the home folder) are optional, as for a failed CLI install. `signedIn` is absent while the sign-in is unknown; `signInCheck` then says why the last check of the CLI's status command could not tell: `timeout` (the CLI was ended after 8 seconds) or `unreadable` (it could not be run, or answered something this does not read). Neither field: nothing is known of a check (none has run yet, or the agent has no status command: a native agent's sign-in comes from its own ACP session). Errors are redacted. Spawns nothing. |
| `inspect(id)` | One agent's `status()` row with a fresh sign-in check, for a Bot about to be put on it. Asks that CLI's sign-in status only; installs, enables and starts nothing. Simultaneous checks share one probe. An answer stands for 3 seconds, and a confirmed sign-in for 5 minutes, since the check starts the whole CLI; `refresh()` clears it, and so does the agent itself saying it is signed out (ACP `auth_required`). Undefined for an id that is no agent here. |
| `refresh()` | Looks for the CLIs again (one installed after DSH started is offered now), then asks each CLI whether it is signed in (`claude auth status --json`, of which only `loggedIn` is read; `codex login status`, by its exit code). No agent turn. |
| `retry(id)` | Retries the required CLI and its connector, and answers at once. A connector whose last start or install failed, or that is missing, is reinstalled at the release in use (below); else the connector is checked for a newer release. Does not turn its model switch on. |
| `loginStart(id, { label? })` | Starts the CLI's own sign-in (`src/host/login.js`), or answers the attempt already at work for that agent. Codex: a device code through `codex app-se
