## 交互式终端（terminal 工具）

`terminal` 工具在 PTY 接缝（node-pty；Windows 上因上游 `spawnTerminal` 的 process inspector 仅支持 POSIX，由 `lib/terminal.js` 直连 node-pty，非 Windows 仍走官方 `ctx.subprocess.spawnTerminal`）上提供**持久交互会话**：

- `action: open` 启动一个真实终端会话（按你设置的默认终端；wsl 可传 `distro`），返回 `sessionId`
- `action: send` 写入输入并读新输出；`action: read` 只读不写；`action: signal` 向前台进程组发信号（SIGINT = Ctrl+C）
- `action: close` 终止会话
- **会话状态跨调用保持**（cwd / 变量 / 别名），适合 REPL、ssh、交互式 CLI
- `send` 会等待输出稳定（300ms 静默，上限 5s）返回**完整回复**；输出超 1MB 时报 `truncated` 提示
- 输入用 `\\n`（或 \\r）结尾表示回车

## 沙箱（官方机制对接）

`shell` 工具走 DSH 官方沙箱接缝（`ctx.sandboxPolicy` + `ctx.sandbox`）：

- 每次调用解析当前沙箱策略；`danger-full-access` 会话直接执行（不包装）。
- PowerShell 后端经 `ctx.sandbox.confine` 包装 argv —— 与官方 executor 相同的 **fail-closed** 语义：请求受限模式但无可用后端时抛 `SandboxUnavailableError`，拒绝裸跑。
- Git Bash 后端不包装：DSH 的 Windows ACL 受限令牌 runner 与 Cygwin/MSYS2 不兼容（bash 启动即因 `CreateFileMapping` Win32 error 5 终止），因此 Git Bash 在受限模式下也不经沙箱包装；结果报告 `enforcement: gitbash-unconfined`。
- MSYS2 后端同样不包装（同一 Cygwin/MSYS2 运行时不兼容）；结果报告 `enforcement: msys2-unconfined`。
- WSL 后端不包装：WSL 独立 Linux 虚拟机本身就是隔离（结果报告 `enforcement: wsl-isolation`）。
- 受限模式下被沙箱拒绝时，结果携带官方标记 `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` 与同轮升级提示；模型可凭 `sandbox_permissions` + `justification` 发起一次升级（经 `ctx.approval` 用户审批），与官方 bash/pwsh 工具完全一致。
- 注意：DSH 的 Windows ACL runner 可用时，PowerShell 的受限模式会经它包装；Git Bash 与 MSYS2 因 Cygwin/MSYS2 不兼容而保持不包装。

## ⚠️ 安全说明

`shell` 工具在受限模式下：PowerShell 会经 `ctx.sandbox.confine` 包装（fail-closed）；Git Bash 与 MSYS2 因 Cygwin/MSYS2 与 Windows ACL 受限令牌不兼容而**不包装**（与 dsh 进程同权限）；WSL 因独立 Linux VM 不包装。它是**额外的多终端入口**，不享受官方 `pwsh` 工具的 ConstrainedLanguage 限制。DSH 的文件操作工具（read/write/edit）仍受文件沙箱约束。仅在你信任的会话中使用；需要受沙箱保护的 PowerShell 时请继续使用官方 `pwsh` 工具。

## 交互终端已知限制（ConPTY）

- **PowerShell 5.1 无法在 ConPTY 启动**（0x8009001d）—— 交互式 PowerShell 需要安装 [PowerShell 7](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/releases)（一次性命令不受影响）。
- **wsl.exe 交互模式在 ConPTY 下可能触发 WSL 服务 RPC 错误**（0x8007072c，偶发）—— 一次性 `wsl -e bash -lc ...` 命令正常；交互会话建议直接用 Windows Terminal / WSL 终端，或重试。
- **Windows 上 node-pty 不接受命名信号**：`signal` 的 `SIGINT` 映射为 Ctrl+C（`\x03`），其他信号（`SIGTERM` / `SIGKILL` / `SIGTSTP` / `SIGHUP`）退化为终止会话。
- Git Bash 交互会话完全正常。

## 已知限制

- WSL 后台进程在超时/中断后可能在发行版内短暂残留（WSL 实例在最后一个进程退出后自动关闭）。
- Git Bash 是 msys2 环境，与 WSL 的 Linux 行为存在差异（路径映射、包可用性）。
- MSYS2 后端需要本机安装 MSYS2（默认 `C:\msys64`）；未安装时 `shell` 报 `backend unavailable`，可用 `msys2Path` 指定自定义位置。候选顺序永远是 `bash.exe` 优先、`msys2.exe` 兜底——`msys2.exe` 在管道 stdio 下会静默返回零字节，仅作最后手段。
- 本插件的 `shell` / `terminal` 工具仅在 `win32` 平台注册；**底部终端不限制平台**（它在 win32 用 node-pty，在其他平台用宿主 `ctx.subprocess.spawnTerminal`）。

## 底部终端（浏览器内嵌 shell，0.8.0+）

一个面向**人**的终端，跟面向模型的 `shell`/`terminal` 工具共用同一套 shell 知识，但环境完全不同。

**入口**：[dsh-better-sidebar](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-better-sidebar) 0.25+ 的底部工作台。本插件在那里注册**自己的 tab「终端（多 shell）」**，四个 shell 都能用：

| 宿主 | 会发生什么 |
|---|---|
| 自带终端控制器（DSH 0.2.0-rc.2+，官方 CLI/GUI 构建） | 官方那行「终端」由宿主供电、照常可用；本插件**不碰** `webTerminals`，只额外提供自己的多 shell tab |
| 没挂控制器（部分 Desktop 构建，官方那行是死的） | 多 shell tab 照常工作。若你**确实**需要点亮官方那行，再往下面打开「接管官方终端行」开关 |

为什么要自己的 tab：官方终端菜单按**可执行文件名去重**（`shellKind` = 文件名去 `.exe` 转小写），而 Git Bash 与 MSYS2 的主 shell 同名 `bash.exe`，在默认候选下只能出现一个（本包用一步硬链接绕过了它，见下文）。本插件的 tab 按 catalog **行**选 shell，所以四个能并存；官方那行仍在原地，互不遮蔽。

> **「接管官方终端行」默认关闭，这不是保守而是必需**。`webTerminals` 这个名字宿主的控制器 client 半也会注册，而 cordis **拒绝同名二次 provide**、抛错的是后到的一方——控制器的 provide 没有保护，所以我们先到就会把**官方终端整个打挂**，页面变成 `Failed to load plugins / web boot: 1 entry did not activate`（实测于 0.2.0-rc.2）。开关打开时本插件会**先活读一次服务**，确认名字没人占才提供，并在设置行里明说结果（「已接管」/「宿主已提供，未接管」）。也就是说：这个开关只在没有控制器的部署上有意义，在有控制器的宿主上打开它也不会造成破坏。

这个 tab 只在 `ctx.betterSidebar` 存在时注册，走 `ctx.inject(['betterSidebar'])` 到达即注册（软读兜底）——**不能属性读** `ctx.betterSidebar`：client ctx 是 Proxy，读未声明的服务名会直接抛 `cannot get property "betterSidebar" without inject`。xterm **打包进本插件自己的 bundle**（DSH 的 client 模块表只认平台 seed words / shell 自有模块 / 已登记包工厂 / boot 模块四类，第三方包不在其中，外部 `require("@xterm/xterm")` 会在挂载时报 missed the module table）。设置节会明说当前是哪条路径（「当前由宿主终端提供」）。

设置面一共**两个落点**，两处渲染同一个组件（不会一边改了另一边没改）：

| 落点 | 插槽 | 适用宿主线 |
|---|---|---|
| 插件详情页（bundle 设置） | `plugins.bundle.config`（按包名 `dsh-bash-terminal-ts` 派发） | 0.1.7-rc.1+ / 0.2.0 |
| 家族节「起子插件设置」下的 tab | `dsh-family.tab`（容器 = dsh-thinking-levels） | 同上，且需安装 TL |

两个注册臂都在，哪个有渲染宿主哪个就生效。**没有可寄生的家族节时，本插件自己注册一个顶级 `settings.section`**（id `bash-terminal`，永远不冒用 `dsh-family`——同 id 遮蔽位会出双导航行）。这个判定发生在**宿主声明 section 的那一刻**（设置面板打开），不是 apply 期——容器是另一个插件的 client，apply 期赌的就是 bundle 顺序。

另外两个臂是为了跳版本：`settings.plugin.item`（key = 设置命名空间）是 0.1.2/0.1.5 上相当于 bundle 详情页的那个面；`shell.overlay` 浮窗**只在宿主自己报「没有设置页」时渲染**（组件其余时候 return null）。该判定不读版本号、也不依赖 import 宿主包（宿主包在 app 树里，插件目录根本解析不到），而是看 settings 服务实例的能力面：`installSection` 在 → 0.1.2/0.1.5（有页）；只有 `register` → 0.1.0/0.1.1（**槽位表在但没有页渲染它**，所以卡片注册了也打不开，只能自带入口）；两者都不在 → 0.1.7+/0.2.0（有页）。

### 开关与默认 shell

| 项 | 默认 | 语义 |
|---|---|---|
| Git Bash | 开 | 开关 = 允许；**实际可用 = 允许 ∧ 本机探到**，所以“探到即开”无需额外配置 |
| MSYS2 | 开 | 同上；候选永远是 `usr\bin\bash.exe` 优先，`msys2.exe` 拒用（它开自己的窗口，管道零字节） |
| WSL bash | 开 | 同上；`wslDistro` 为空用 WSL 默认发行版 |
| PowerShell | 恒开 | **保底后端，不可关闭**（关掉保底就不叫保底） |

`defaultShell` 下拉只列「已激活 ∧ 可用」项，服务端二次校验（越界回 `bad-request`）。分配时的回落链：

```
候选 = 已激活 ∧ 可用，顺序 [powershell, gitbash, msys2, wsl]
stored == ""      → 取候选首项，不提示（“用户未选”不是“选错了”）
stored ∈ 候选      → 用它
stored 越界        → 取候选首项 + 可见提示（不回写存值）
候选为空          → pwsh → powershell.exe → cmd.exe，提示“已兜底”
```

### UI 终端与模型工具的环境差异（为什么不能复用）

| shell | 模型工具 argv | 底部终端 argv | 底部终端 env |
|---|---|---|---|
| powershell | `-NoLogo -NoProfile [-NonInteractive -Command <cmd>]` | **`-NoLogo`**（保留用户 profile） | `process.env` + `TERM=xterm-256color` |
| gitbash | `-lc <cmd>` | `-i` | 同上，不注入 MSYSTEM（Git 自己会设 `MINGW64`） |
| msys2 | `-lc <cmd>` | **`-l`**（绝不 `-lc`：无操作数会 exit 2） | 同上 + `MSYSTEM=MINGW64`（显式值赢） |
| wsl | `[-d <d>] -e bash -lc <cmd>` | 有 distro `-d <d> -e bash -i`；无 `-- bash -i` | 同上 |

工具路径额外钉 `TERM=dumb`/`NO_COLOR=1`/`PAGER=cat`，这对一次性命令正确，对用户看到的屏幕错误（无颜色、无光标控制、无 profile）。两者共用同一个 node-pty 分配器（`spawnPtyHandle(spec, style)`），只是 `style` 不同 —— 写两份就会让其中一份慢慢漂到错的终端类型上。

另：ConPTY 下 bash 的 `$TERM` 实测为空（终端类型靠 node-pty 的 `name` 选项传递），所以 `TERM=xterm-256color` 主要作用于 POSIX 缝路径。

### 官方终端菜单也被改了（以及为什么需要两步机器前置）

本包的 `cordis.patch.yml` 覆盖宿主 `terminal-controller` 那一行的 `shellCandidates`，**只在原生列表前插一项**：

```yaml
- id: terminal-controller
  config:
    shellCandidates:
      - 'C:\msys64\usr\bin\msys-bash.exe'   # 硬链接，kind 不同 → 新增一项
      - zsh
      - bash                                  # ← 保留：Windows 上它解析到 WSL 转发器
      - fish
      - pwsh
      - powershell
      - cmd
    # …以及其余 10 个限制键，均照宿主默认值写全
```

**为什么不能把 `Git\bin\bash.exe` 也排到前面**（上一版就是这么写的，已回退）：`discoverShells` 按可执行文件名去重且**保留最早一条**，而 Windows 上裸名 `bash` 解析到的是 `C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe`——**WSL 转发器**。把 Git 排在它前面等于把 WSL 从官方菜单里**删掉**，这不是任何人的需求。Git Bash 拿不到自己的 key 是因为改名需要往 `C:\Program Files\Git\bin\`（需管理员权限）里建硬链接，而且该链接必须留在 Git 树内——Cygwin/Git-bash 按可执行文件所在路径推导它的 POSIX 根。所以 **Git Bash 由本插件自己的 tab 提供**，官方行只动了一处：把被去重抹掉的 MSYS2 加回来。

实测（`POST /api/terminal/shells`，同一沙箱实例）：

```
cmd.exe=C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe | msys-bash.exe=C:\msys64\usr\bin\msys-bash.exe
bash=C:\Windows\system32\bash.EXE   | powershell=...\powershell.EXE
→ WSL bash retained AND MSYS2 added
```

两个必须知道的风隙：

1. **整块替换**。patch 对该行是**全量替换 config**，少写一个键就是静默删掉那个限制（`.default()` 只在输入缺字段时生效）。所以十一个键全部显式写出，并由 `test/webterminals.ts` 断言键集完整**且六个原生候选一个不少**——以后谁再把绝对路径的 `bash.exe` 插到裸名前面，构建会直接失败。
2. **去重键是文件名**。所以 MSYS2 需要一个不同名的入口：

```powershell
# 前置一：给 MSYS2 一个不同名的硬链接（同 inode，不占空间，删文件即回滚）
New-Item -ItemType HardLink -Path C:\msys64\usr\bin\msys-bash.exe -Target C:\msys64\usr\bin\bash.exe
```

```bash
# 前置二：非登录 shell 不 source /etc/profile，/usr/bin 会缺（uname/ls 报“未找到命令”）
# 宿主给候选的参数是按文件名猜死的 `-i`，插件无法改成 `-l`、也没有 env 通道，
# 所以这一段必须落在 MSYS2 自己的 ~/.bashrc 里（幂等，删 sentinel 之间即回滚）
case ":$PATH:" in
  *":/usr/bin:"*) ;;
  *) PATH="/usr/bin:$PATH" ;;
esac
```

实测（真 node-pty，完全复现宿主的启动方式）：

| 条目 | `uname` / `ls` | `gcc` |
|---|---|---|
| `bash.exe`（Git Bash） | ✅ | —（Git 本身不带编译器） |
| `msys-bash.exe`（两项前置后） | ✅ | ✅ `/mingw64/bin` |
| `msys-bash.exe`（缺前置二） | ❌ MISSING | ✅ |

前置二用**前置** `/usr/bin` 在本机是安全的：`/usr/bin/gcc.exe` 不存在，所以 mingw64 工具链仍然优先；但如果你日后 `pacman -S mingw-w64-x86_64-gcc` 装了 MSYS 层级的 gcc，需要重新测一遍优先级。

### 边界

- 两条 HTTP 路由（legacy `/api/bash-terminal/config` 与新的 `/api/bash-terminal/terminals`）+ 一条 WS（`/bash-terminal/ws`），均**仅限回环地址**（防 DNS rebinding / 局域网，不是认证）。
- **不给模型新增任何能力**：不注册工具、不写 systemPrompt 段落、不碰沙箱审批。
- 生命周期沿用官方语义：关掉标签才终止进程；退出的终端仍占配额直到关闭；刷新页面靠 grace 重接同一 shell。

### 实测记录（win32 + 真 node-pty）

```
seam backend = node-pty | socket mount = mounted
PASS powershell  powershell.exe argv=[-NoLogo]   resized=true
PASS gitbash     bash.exe     argv=[-i]          resized=true
PASS msys2       bash.exe     argv=[-l]          msys=MINGW64 uname=MINGW64_NT-10.0-26300
PASS wsl         wsl.exe      argv=[-- bash -i]  uname=Linux
terminals after close: 0
```

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-media-lens

[简体中文](README.md) | [Português](README.pt.md)

媒体感知插件：把本地 video / audio / image 变成**结构化证据**（时间线 / 转写 / 版面区域）注入对话，让文本模型引用具体帧、秒、说话人 —— **Evidence, not imagination**。同时内置 provider 路由线：每个媒体一条 failover 链，预算超限自动降级，每次尝试记录在 `meta.attempts` —— **a fallback is never silent**。

```
media_read_video / media_read_audio / media_read_image
  → 路径守卫（存在性 + 扩展名白名单）
  → ffprobe 探测 + 预算裁决（full / reencode / sampleFrames / segment / downsample）
  → failover 链（首个成功即返回；全败抛带 attempts 的结构化错误）
  → MediaEvidence JSON（timeline / transcript / regions + meta.attempts）
```

## 链序（每媒体）

| 媒体 | 链 |
| --- | --- |
| video（≤10MB 且 ≤10min） | `multimodal`（注册全模态直传）→ `frames:`（ffmpeg 均匀抽帧 + 图片链）→ `local:metadata` |
| video（10–19MB） | `reencode:multimodal`（540p x264 压缩后直传）→ 同上 |
| video（>19MB 或 >10min） | 直接 `frames:` 抽帧路 |
| audio | `multimodal`（全模态直传转写）→ `asr:endpoint-N`（本地 ASR CLI，多端点按序）→ `local:metadata` |
| image | `registered:`（宿主已注册视觉模型）→ `configured:openai`（OpenAI-compatible 端点）→ `local:metadata` |

## 处理端来源（FR-9：已注册模型优先）

- **宿主已注册模型**：插件经 `ctx.llm.listProviders()/listModels()` 枚举（60s 缓存），按 `inputModalities` 分组构成首选链；图片原生 image 块直送。
- **显式选择**：配置 `models.{image,audio,video}: "provider/model"` 直接指定一个已注册模型 —— 视频的 MiMo 类全模态路就走这里（宿主模态词表当前只认 `text|image`，自动发现不了视频/音频声明，显式选择是唯一入口；实际承载由适配器（如 openai-completions 接管线）的模态硬闸把关，拒绝是响亮的）。
- **自配端点**：`providers.openai.{baseUrl, apiKey, model}`，apiKey 支持逗号分隔多 key（auth/429/quota 换下一个 key；网络/5xx 跳过保链）。
- **本地兜底**：strictLocalOnly 或全链失败时，`local:metadata` 只出 probe 元数据（时长/分辨率/大小），`degraded='local-metadata-only'`。

## 配置

```yaml
dsh-media-lens:
  strictLocalOnly: false      # true 时链中剔除一切远端 provider，媒体内容不出本机
  cooldownMs: 600000          # keyFailure 类失败的默认冷却时长（有 Retry-After/"Resets in" 线索时按线索）
  models:
    image: auto               # auto | '' | "provider/model"
    audio: auto
    video: auto               # MiMo 类全模态：填 "llm-pi-ai/你的mimo模型id"
  providers:
    openai:
      baseUrl: ''             # 例 https://api.example.com/v1
      apiKey: ''              # 逗号分隔多 key 轮换
      model: ''
      structuredOutput: false # true 时注入 response_format json_schema(strict)（不认识的网关会 400，故默认关）
    asr:
      command: ''             # 单端点写法：本地转写 CLI 模板，{input} 占位
      endpoints: []           # 多端点选择项，按序尝试；与 command 合并（command 在前）
  refine:
    enabled: false            # Phase 7：链出口一次 refine pass，默认关
    model: ''                 # 开启时必须写 'openai/<model>' 或裸 model；auto / 空串 = 未启用。转述手只认 configured 自配端点（registered:/插件注入模型无效）
```

ASR 命令模板示例（Windows，模板内双引号保护空格路径）：

```
python "C:\tools\sensevoice_cli.py" --input "{input}" --json
```

转写输出识别两种格式：JSON segments（`[{start,end,text[,speaker]}]` 或 `{"segments":[...]}`）与 SRT/时间行文本。

## 隐私说明（对照 dsh-vision-router 教训）

- **默认媒体内容会发往远端 provider**（注册模型 / 配置端点）。要内容不出本机，显式开启 `strictLocalOnly: true`——之后只剩本地 ASR CLI 与元数据兜底。
- `meta.attempts` 记录每次尝试（provider 名含来源前缀 `registered:` / `multimodal:` / `configured:` / `asr:` / `frames:` / `local:`，多 key 轮换带 `keyIndex`），`meta.warnings` 记录路由通告（failover 去向、冷却垫尾、轮换成功）——降级绝不静默。
- 媒体路径按不可信输入处理：只读取、存在性 + 扩展名 + **magic-byte 三重校验**（改名伪装的文件在入参侧拒绝）；处理指令显式声明媒体内出现的指令一律视为数据；内容永不执行。
- 错误文本先脱密（apiKey/baseUrl 精确匹配）再截断，密钥不进 attempts/日志。
- 音视频直传只在适配器接管线（如 openai-completions takeover）上真正内联；未接管线路上模型只看到文件 handle 文本 —— 插件检测到这种回声会放弃该跳并落到抽帧/ASR 兜底，**不产幻觉证据**。

## 冷却语义（modlens 软化熔断）

只有 **keyFailure 类失败**（auth/429/quota 正文）触发冷却——普通失败（网络抖动、5xx、解析失败）永不冷却，正文碰巧含 quota 字样也不算。冷却中的 provider **垫到链尾仍作最后尝试**（不是踢出）：穷途末路时仍试一把，成功即恢复。provider 给恢复线索（`Retry-After` 头或正文 `Resets in Xh Ym Zs`）时按线索计时，否则 `cooldownMs`。

## structuredOutput（FR-13，opt-in）

`providers.openai.structuredOutput: true` 时请求注入 `response_format json_schema(strict)`（由证据载荷派生，非手写镜像）。认识的网关（vLLM、官方 OpenAI 等）服务端强制形状能显著提证据质量；不认识的网关对未知字段直接 400——所以缺省关。

## refine pass（Phase 7，链出口一次，opt-in）

主链首个成功后、返回前可选地再过一次**文本模型**将证据精炼规范化（去重 / 紧措辞 / 保留不确定性）——对齐 medialens 型项目常见的 "visionModel 读手 + textModel 转述手" pair 设计。

```yaml
refine:
  enabled: true
  model: "openai/your-text-model"   # 或裸 model；auto / 空串 = 未启用
```

默认关，理由：

- **隐私**：多一跳远端 = 多一次媒体内容（raw evidence）暴露面；`strictLocalOnly` 下链仅到 `local:metadata`，此时 refine 自动跳过（无文本可精炼），不会拉回远端。
- **延迟**：直出证据已可用，refine 是锦上添花。
- **不作 auto**：auto = 随便把所有模型都加透镜，不允许。

**来源闸门（转述手只认用户自配端点）**：refine 这一跳只允许 **configured 端点**（`providers.openai` 配了 `baseUrl` + `apiKey`）——`model` 必须写 `openai/<model>` 或裸 model，实际请求 model 取 `providers.openai.model` 单源。**`registered:` / `multimodal:`（宿主 discovery 枚举，可能含其它插件注入的模型）一律不可信**：命中即静默跳过（不写 `refineAttempt`、不追 warning，行为与未启用一致）。传输走 configured 直连（不经宿主 runtime 路由表），`structuredOutput` 开启时注入 `response_format`。

失败行为（**不静默**，但**不撤销已成**）：refine 抛错 / 输出无 JSON / 校验不通过 → **保留 raw evidence**，`meta.warnings` 追加 `refine failed: <redacted>`，`meta.refineAttempt.ok = false`；主链 attempts 不新增（读手已成功，不浪费下一跳抽帧/ASR）。成功时 refine 归属写 `meta.refineAttempt.provider = 'refined:openai/<model>'`，`meta.provider` 保留读手前缀（registered / multimodal / configured / asr / frames / local）；`source` / `meta.attempts` / `meta.generatedAt` 不被 refine 修改。

传输硬化：`EVIDENCE_REFINE_INSTRUCTION` 四要素与读手指令同源（反注入 / verbatim / bbox 保守 / uncertainty），另加「保留原 source 与 attempts」一行——媒体内出现的指令会随 raw evidence 二次进入 LLM 上下文，反注入行必须再吃一遍，防洗证据。错误文本先脱密后截断。

## vision-bridge（v4，选择器可见的透镜包装，opt-in）

把透镜包装成宿主模型选择器里**可见的路由**：经宿主 `llm.registerAdapter` 注册 `media-lens-vision-<upstream>` 包装 provider，选择器出现 `<模型名> (media-lens vision)` 条目。选中它作主对话模型后，请求中的媒体在发送前经 media-lens 链（读手 = 上文「处理端模型」配置）转成证据文本，再委托真实路由——纯文本主力模型由此获得图片与音视频 sight（"让 deepseek 收到小米读出的证据"）。

```yaml
inject:
  enabled: true
  families: ["deepseek", "glm", "mimo"]   # 前缀过滤；"*" = 全部（仍受否决）
```

**包装判据 = 透镜能补模态就包，omni 坚决不包**：

- 纯文本模型（deepseek-v4.1 类）→ 包：图像 + 音视频全部证据化；
- 图像模型（声明 image、非 omni）→ 包：**图像块原样透传**（保留原生视觉），仅音视频证据化；
- omni 宽模态（MiMo bare 非 `-pro` 段，名字启发式）与 vision 专精词表（`deepseek-vl` / `glm-4v` / `*vision*` 等）→ 拒包，`resolveModel` 响亮拒绝并指路原路由。

机制要点（0.2.0-rc.2 实锚）：宿主在 adapter 前已把 file 块投影成确定性 handle 文本，桥按 `content.ts` 精确格式识别并提取只读路径走全链；改写永不 throw（读手失败落常量占位文本，请求继续）；证据按块缓存（重放零重读）；`llm/adapters-updated` 事件驱动重扫，迟注册路由（llm-pi-ai）自动跟进；discovery 快照剔除 `media-lens-vision-*`（读手永不选中自己的 wrapper）。宿主缺 `registerAdapter` 面时静默保持纯工具形态。

## 安装

```powershell
# 宿主 0.2.0-rc.1 / 0.2.0-rc.2（engines.dsh 与 peerDependencies 对齐）
pnpm add ./dsh-media-lens --ignore-workspace-root-check   # 或 npm pack 后装 tgz
```

`cordis.patch.yml` 提供 insert 注册行（`dsh.bundle.patch` 已在 package.json 对齐）。装完重启宿主。

## 依赖面

- 运行时依赖仅 `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`（Config schema）；`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`（defineTool）由宿主运行时提供（peer）。
- ffmpeg / ffprobe 在 PATH 上可用时启用抽帧/重编码/时长探测；缺失时元数据降级（记录在 attempts）。
- Node 原生 fetch（≥22.19）。

## 配合插件（可选 peer，非硬依赖）

media-lens 本身提供「工具处理多模态对象」（media_read_video/audio/image）。要把**多模态模型注册/认证进宿主**并让**音视频直传**真正内联（而非只看到文件 handle 文本），需两个姊妹插件配合——二者声明为 `optional` peer，不装则相应能力自动降级，不报错：

- **dsh-thinking-levels**：模型配置录入 / 认证与 reasoning_effort 管理面——音视频直传链路的模型由此登记。
- **dsh-llm-openai-completions**：OpenAI-compatible 传输接管（takeover）——把 file 块序列化成 video_url / input_audio 真正上送，未接管线路宿主只投影 handle 文本，插件检测到即落抽帧/ASR 兜底。

装机走宿主 profile（autoInstallPeers:false + hoisted），姊妹插件由 bundles 各自注册，optional peer 不触发 npm 拉装、不与宿主版本闸门冲突。

## 家族节与 tab 权重（bundle + 家族子 tab）

本插件为 host+client 双半 bundle（`dsh.plugin.json.client.main` 载 client 半身）。客户端半身把设置卡贡献进 `dsh-family` 家族节（顶级节 order 40、label「起子插件设置」，与本插件无关、由家族所有者统一渲染）：

| 注册面 | 槽 | 权重(order) | 语义 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 家族子 tab 贡献卡（主路） | `dsh-family.tab` | **65**（排现存贡献卡之后，靠后） | lazy：等家族所有者注入渲染；贡献卡不自渲染节体 |
| 独立兜底节 | `settings.section` | 24 | **无 injection 时自注册**：家族槽从未被渲染（无所有者/缺席）时，本卡以独立节出现，保留可见性 |
| bundle 详情卡 | `plugins.bundle.config` | —（按包名 keyed） | 0.1.7+ 插件管理器详情设置卡 |

lazy 机制（两路注入均在 apply 期顶层注册，工厂只在「声明事件=设置面板打开」fire，fire 序=注册序）：家族贡献卡先注册并在其工厂 fire 时置 `familySeated`；独立节工厂读到该标记即退场（避免与家族 tab 重复展示），读不到才自注册独立节。**禁止宽限期后注册**（§3 反例）。写路径：条目配置各顶层字段标 `.volatile()`，client 经 `configForms.get(entryId).set(field, value)` 权威写 + 热生效（0.1.7+/0.2.0/0.2.1 唯一活写面；`settings.register` 在 0.1.7+ 已移除，webServer 桥不可作写路径）。

## 边界（YAGNI）

有 host+client 双半身与设置卡（家族子 tab / 独立节 / bundle 卡，见上节），但除此之外无对话内卡片、无客户端粘贴拦截（vision-bridge 的请求改写发生在宿主 adapter 面，非 UI 拦截）、无 TTS / 媒体编辑、不内置任何 key。更多 UI 需求出现时另立计划。

## 版本线

`0.1.0`（engines.dsh `0.2.0-rc.1 || 0.2.0-rc.2`）。发布走 npm staged 人工审批；dist-tag 分层 `dsh-0.2.0`（对齐 date-wrapper 先例），latest 收敛在发版时统一处理。

## TUI 终端面（dsh-tui）

dsh-tui 不加载插件的 client 半边（面板/卡片/设置页），也调不到插件自有 RPC；工具调用只显示一行摘要。人可读、人可操作的面只剩宿主斜杠命令。输出约定：单行 ≤100 字符、总行 ≤40、无 ANSI、两空格对齐；写操作默认 dry、加 `--yes` 才执行；`--json` 输出单行 JSON。

| 命令 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `/media status` | 媒体路由设置节（终端不可视媒体本身） |

命令由插件自己在宿主侧注册（`ctx.inject(['commands'], …)`）：命令服务缺席的老宿主线上不激活、不报错。

> **Compatibility note:** v2.0.0 ships `ja` / `ko` dictionaries, but official DSH exposes
> only `zh` / `en` through `LocaleRuntime` (`LOCALE_IDS = ["zh", "en"]`). On stock DSH,
> selecting `ja` / `ko` fails with `locale "<id>" is not registered`. Use a DSH fork that
> updates `LOCALE_IDS` (locale-settings.ts) and `LOCALES` labels (client/index.ts), then
> rebuild.

> **▼ DSH version compatibility**
>
> Two DSH lines are served from two long-lived branches, each with its own version
> series, `engines.dsh`, and npm dist-tag ([release layout](./RELEASING.md)):
>
> | DSH version | Branch | Version | npm tag |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | 0.1.0-rc.7 ~ 0.1.1-rc.x | `legacy` | `1.x` | `@legacy` |
> | 0.1.2-alpha.1+ (incl. 0.1.5-rc.2) | `main` | `2.x` | `@latest` / `@dsh-0.1.2` (`@2.x` is a range) |
>
> The series number tracks the **DSH line** (`1.x` = DSH ≤ 0.1.1, `2.x` = DSH 0.1.2+),
> and the majors fence each other: a `^1.x` install never resolves a `2.x` release and
> vice versa. `engines.dsh` states the same split but DSH never reads it — the ranges
> and dist-tags are what hold an old DSH on `1.x`.
>
> `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime` was **removed** at `0.1.2-alpha.1` — it did not
> merely move. The `legacy` line still reaches `ctx.slots` through it; `main` gets
> the same declaration from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-renderer/client`. Two
> version-sensitive seams are handled by capability probes rather than version
> checks: (1) settings registration uses `register`, which exists on both lines
> (`installSection` is an addition, not a replacement); (2) `effectivePolicy` is a
> **private** method of the user-approval service on both, so it is read behind a
> `typeof` probe and degrades to “policy unknown” when absent or throwing.

Version **2.6.0** — see the [Changelog](./CHANGELOG.md).

A single, self-sufficient, deterministic-first, fail-closed permission gate for DeepSeek Harness.

`dsh-perm-gate` decides every tool call through a fixed priority chain:

| Stage | Decision | What it is |
| ---- | ---- | ---- |
| **P0** | `deny` | deterministic hard-deny: credential material, protected-path mutation, dangerous shell |
| **P1** | `allow` | a precise, bounded **session grant** |
| **P2** | `deny/allow/ask` | static rule chain: blacklist first, then allow, then ask |
| **P3** | `allow/deny/ask` | optional LLM semantic classifier (default **off**) |
| **P4** | `ask` | official approval seam |

Strictly fail-closed: a P0 decision is never overridden by a grant, a rule, the classifier, or a human.

- **Runtime-verified:** `0.1.0-rc.2`, `0.1.0-rc.3`, `0.1.0-rc.6`, `0.1.0-rc.7`, `0.1.0-rc.8`, `0.1.1-rc.1`, `0.1.1-rc.2`, `0.1.2-rc.1`, `0.1.5-rc.1`, `0.1.5-rc.2`, `0.1.5-rc.3`, `0.1.7-rc.1`, `0.1.7-rc.2`, `0.2.0-rc.1`, `0.2.0-rc.2` — evidence in `.compat-results/`
<!-- host-compat:end -->

## Why

The DSH safety ecosystem splits this across several plugins (`dsh-permission-rules`,
`dsh-auto-mode`, `dsh-auto-review`, `dsh-movein-permissions`). `dsh-perm-gate` merges the
gate + approval + (optional) classifier into one package, with one audit trail and no
cross-plugin version coupling.

## Features

- **Command whitelist / blacklist** — matched on an **argv decomposition** (not a raw string),
  with recursive descent into `sh -c`/`bash -c`, pipeline detection, redirect-target
  checking, and recursive/force (`rm -rf`) recognition.
- **Deny priority** — a matching deny rule wins over any allow rule.
- **Credential family ladder** — seven credential families (`ssh`, `cloud`, `package`, `gitcreds`,
  `env`, `cli`, `db`), each selectable at `deny` / `ask` (default) / `readonly` / `readwrite`.
  The rung lives in the rules document (`[deny-rule:cred.<family>]` row, section + `enabled`)
  plus the paired `credWriteExemptFamilies` list, written in one settings update — no mirror,
  no half-state. `readwrite` is the only rung that steps a piece of P0 aside (the credential-store
  *write* screen, npm-login style) and asks for an inline confirmation; roots, protected paths,
  `.dsh` and egress stay armed at every rung.
- **Protected-branch push switch** — `allowProtectedBranchPush` (off by default) keeps the P0
  floor on `git push --force/--force-with-lease/--delete` to protected branches; turning it on
  steps that floor aside into the seeded `git.push-force` ask (a person confirms each push) and
  exempts the three flat push keywords from the blacklist.
- **Session grants** — precise `(tool, canonical fingerprint)` grants with `TTL` + `maxUses`;
  re-running with a different target never reuses authority. Sub-agents inherit but cannot mint.
- **Pure-function rule engine** — glob/regex compilation with a ReDoS bound, loud fail on
  malformed rules, and source-hash compile caching.
- **Audit** — every decision is logged as an `{ignorable:true}` event with its `callId`; the
  model-visible reason matches the recorded outcome.
- **自动审查 tier** (`permissive`, plus `permissive-full`) — an **independent approval mode**
  (separate from read-only, full-access and whitelist tiers) that is neither "auto-approve" nor
  blanket trust. Front-end exposes a **single switch** (`permissive`); the four backend strategies
  are **combinable** and driven by plugin settings — still fail-closed against P0. The permission
  picker and the settings row both show it under the product label 自动审查, with no icon. The
  `permissive-full` variant keeps the identical approval behaviour but drops the built-in file
  sandbox, which otherwise denies the named pipes `git clone` / Cygwin / ConPTY need.
- **Sandbox-escalation auto-answer** (`trustEscalation`) — a sandbox escalation is asked from
  *inside* the shell / pwsh / edit tool body, after `tools/pre-execute`, so the gate never saw
  it and a call it auto-allowed still prompted you to approve the widening. With this strategy
  on, the exact call the gate cleared (matched by `callId`) is answered here instead.
- **Risk-graded `llmAssist`** — a custom OpenAI-compatible LLM grades each `ask` as
  `safe` / `risky:<category>`; hard categories (deletion, credential, remote, system, bulk)
  **always ask**, neutral enters verdict learning, and every failure stays fail-closed.
- **Verdict learning** — neutral-risk asks that the human approves and that actually execute
  count up; after the threshold, the *exact same operation* (fingerprint-matched) auto-allows.
- **Decision event feed** — every decision is appended to a JSONL feed and surfaced by the
  browser half as a notice strip above the conversation input plus an approval-records tab
  (newest first) in the conversation view.

A preset **deny-keyword blacklist** (inherited from dsh-approval-gate's `DEFAULT_DENY_KEYWORDS`:
`rm -rf`, `push --force`, `drop table`, `mkfs`, `git reset --hard`, `docker system prune`, …) vetoes
any call whose text contains a keyword — case-insensitive substring, applied before whitelist,
grants and LLM. It is editable as a list in the settings card (preset entries are tagged, and a
one-click restore brings the preset back); unset or empty applies the preset — the blacklist
never silently turns off.

## Install

Requires an existing [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) installation.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-perm-gate
```

Full install, upgrade, migration and troubleshooting steps live in the
[Installation guide](./INSTALL.md) — also available in
[中文](./INSTALL.zh.md) / [日本語](./INSTALL.ja.md) / [한국어](./INSTALL.ko.md) / [Português](./INSTALL.pt.md).

## Configuration

### AppContainer sandbox (Windows; beta)

`dsh-perm-gate` can run gate-allowed shell commands inside a **Windows AppContainer** instead of
handing them back unconfined. The container token is created with **zero network capabilities**, so
non-loopback egress is blocked by Windows Firewall (WFP) itself — not by an advisory environment
variable. The container SID is OS-derived from the fixed name `dsh-perm-gate.ac`, so the one-time
`CheckNetIsolation LoopbackExempt` (which lets the container reach `127.0.0.1`) is a per-machine
step, not a per-session one. Egress is therefore possible **only** through the network proxy:

- `sandboxEnabled` (default `false`) — master switch. When on, every **auto-allowed** shell call is
  rewritten into the launcher invocation; a human-approved call is out of scope (the user approved
  it consciously). If the launcher cannot be built or the OS rejects the container launch, the call
  is **denied** (fail-closed) with reason `sandbox: …` — never run unconfined.
- `sandboxMode` — `workspace-write` (default; workspace gets Modify + private temp FullControl,
  system dirs stay readable through the stock ALL APPLICATION PACKAGES ACEs) or `read-only`.
- `sandboxProxy` — **the proxy parameter**: empty (default) follows the builtin filtered proxy's
  actual `127.0.0.1:<port>` when `networkEnabled`; an explicit URL must be loopback-bound (the
  container cannot reach anything else) and destination filtering is that proxy's job.
- `sandboxLoopback` — `exempt` (default; attempt the one-time exemption, warn with the exact
  elevated command if denied) or `off`.

The launcher is a small C# program shipped as source (`assets/appcontainer-launcher.cs`) and
compiled on first use by the .NET Framework compiler every Windows carries (`csc.exe`); the plugin
itself keeps zero native dependencies. Verify a machine end-to-end with:

```
node scripts/smoke-appcontainer.mjs
```

Known boundary: on Windows 11 25H2+ builds where the classic AppContainer creation APIs have been
removed (verified on 26200) and the mxc replacement is not yet exposed (26600+), the launcher fails
closed at the kernel step; the sandbox then denies sandboxed calls with a clear reason instead of
running them unconfined. On Windows 10 / 11 ≤ 24H2 the documented classic path applies.

Add the plugin to `cordis.yml`:

```yaml
- id: dsh-perm-gate
  name: dsh-perm-gate
  config:
    rulesFile: ./permissions.yaml   # optional; defaults to $DSH_HOME/perm-gate/rules.yml
    dshHome: $DSH_HOME              # root pinned for protected-target checks
    defaultAction: ask              # allow | ask | deny
    gatePresets: [permissive, permissive-full]   # tiers where the gate is active (default)
    sessionSweep: true              # hourly cleanup of archived/dead sessions' gate data
```

### Session sweep

On startup and every hour the gate reads DSH's workspace store
(`$DSH_HOME/storages/workspace.json`, read-only) and classifies every session it
holds authorization-chain data for. Sessions DSH has archived (`global.archivedSessionIds`)
or no longer tracks at all have their decision events dropped from
`$DSH_HOME/perm-gate/events.jsonl` and their pre-change snapshot files deleted
from `$DSH_HOME/perm-gate/snapshots/` — history the review page can no longer
reach, for data the harness itself considers gone. Live sessions are untouched,
unattributable rows (empty session id) are never deleted, and any failure is
fail-open: the round is skipped and retried an hour later. Set `sessionSweep: false`
to disable; `workspaceStoreFile` overrides the store path. Restoring an archived
session does not restore its swept history.

### Rules file

```yaml
permissions:
  defaultAction: ask
  deny:
    - command: [rm#recursive]
      reason: no recursive rm
    - command: [ssh]
      reason: no direct ssh
    - paths: [.dsh/**]
      reason: protect harness metadata
  allow:
    - command: [pnpm, node]
      reason: dev tools
    - command: [curl, wget]
      args: ["https://*.example.com/*"]
      reason: allowed endpoint
  ask:
    - command: [bash, sh]
      reason: ask shells
```

A command entry `word#flag` matches the command word (`word`) with the modifier `recursive` or
`force` — so `rm#recursive` matches `rm -rf`, `env rm -rf`, and `sh -c "rm -rf /"`.

### Network policy (opt-in)

A local HTTP/CONNECT proxy that adjudicates the outbound traffic of **shell
subprocesses** against the same rules file, plus an approval path for targets no
rule covers. **Off by default** — enabling it binds a loopback port and rewrites
the proxy environment for child processes, so it is never turned on implicitly.

```yaml
- id: dsh-perm-gate
  config:
    networkEnabled: false          # master switch (default false)
    networkMode: whitelist         # deny-all | whitelist | allow-all
    networkUnlisted: ask           # ask | deny  — unlisted target handling
    networkUnattributed: allow     # allow | deny — traffic with no shell attribution
    networkInjectEnv: true         # rewrite HTTP(S)_PROXY/ALL_PROXY for children
    networkAskTimeoutMs: 120000    # approval wait before failing closed
    networkGrantTtlMs: 1800000     # how long one approval covers its target
```

**Tiered behaviour.** Nothing reaches the network without an allow rule.
An unlisted target is escalated to the interactive approval seam, raised on
behalf of the shell command that opened the connection; approving widens reach
for that target for the session. A `deny` rule is **never** escalated —
approval can widen what an unlisted target may reach, but it can never override
a rule that says no.

**The boundary — read this before relying on it.** The proxy is a *cooperative*
policy layer, not an enforcement boundary. It only sees traffic from clients
that read the proxy environment:

| Client | Covered? |
|--------|----------|
| `curl`, `wget`, `git`, Go `net/http`, Python `requests` | yes |
| **Node.js `http`/`https`/`fetch`** | **no — connects directly** |
| Java (without `-D` proxy flags), .NET `HttpClient` | no |
| Raw sockets, custom TCP | no |
| DNS, QUIC/HTTP3, non-HTTP protocols | no |
| Connections to a literal IP | no |

So a shell command like `node -e "require('http').get('http://host/')"` is not
intercepted. Treat this as a guardrail against accidents and a place to state
intent, not as a hermetic sandbox.

DSH's **own** network traffic — the built-in network tools and the LLM
transport — is deliberately left alone. Those connections carry no shell
attribution, and `networkUnattributed: allow` (the default) passes them
through unreviewed: reviewing them would let the host block *itself*, which is
a worse failure than a missed block. Set `networkUnattributed: deny` only if
you know your host's clients ignore the proxy environment.

Query the live state at `GET /api/dsh-perm-gate/network` (mode, bind, port,
proxy liveness, env-injection state, block counters, recent blocks).

## The 自动审查 tier (machine value `permissive`)

自动审查 is an **independent approval tier** in the DSH permission picker, parallel to
Read Only / Workspace Write / Full access / Whitelist. It is **not** generic "auto-approval" and
never mints blanket authority: it only narrows or widens the seam *before* the human/LLM step
while P0 hard-deny stays monotonic and non-negotiable **within the gate's own scope**.

> **P0 is scoped, not global.** The gate acts only while the session's permission preset is one
> of `gatePresets` (default `permissive` / `permissive-full`). Under any other preset — Read Only,
> Workspace Write, or Full access — the **entire** gate stands down, P0 hard-deny included,
> because the selected tier's own policy governs that session. This is deliberate (see
> `gatePresets` in the configuration table), but it means "P0 is non-negotiable" holds *inside*
> the gate's tiers rather than across every tier. A stand-down is not silent: the gate records one
> `stand-down` event per session/preset transition and the browser shows a sticky **GATE OFF**
> strip above the input. Set `gatePresets: ['*']` to make P0 global again.

**Two variants ship**, because a preset's `sandbox` and `approval` are independent knobs and
coupling them forced a bad trade:

| Picker label | Machine value | sandbox | approval |
|--------------|---------------|---------|----------|
| 自动审查 | `permissive` | `workspace-write` | `ask` |
| 自动审查（高权限） | `permissive-full` | `danger-full-access` | `ask` |

The plain tier keeps the built-in file sandbox. That sandbox also denies the named pipes a child
process needs to start, so `git clone`, MSYS2/Cygwin `sh.exe` and ConPTY fail under it with
`Win32 error 5` / `couldn't create signal pipe`. Because the gate is active **only** in the tiers
listed in `gatePresets`, wanting the gate meant accepting that restriction. 自动审查（高权限）
removes the coupling: identical approval behaviour, no file-sandbox restriction. The tier's own
description states the trade plainly — the workflow is smoother, approvals still apply per call,
but there is **no system sandbox left as a backstop**. Both are in the
default `gatePresets`, so either one gives you the full P0–P4 chain — the gate reads the preset
**name** only, never the sandbox mode.

The picker label is a **host-supplied product string**, not a per-locale dictionary entry: DSH
renders a plugin tier's `name:` verbatim on both permission surfaces (the General-settings
default row and the composer picker) and only supplies its own localized labels for the three
built-in values, so `cordis.patch.yml` ships the Chinese label for every session.

The **icon** is a different story. The composer's glyph map is closed, and its own comment states
the rule: *host-configured names outside the design set get none.* `permissive` is a built-in
value, so 自动审查 already has a shield+eye glyph; `permissive-full` gets the same glyph only
because `npx dsh-perm-gate-patch-glyph` adds it to that map. That patch edits a **host**
package, so it is lost on every DSH upgrade — see
[After a DSH upgrade](./INSTALL.md#after-a-dsh-upgrade-re-apply-the-composer-glyph-patch).

In `cordis.yml`:

```yaml
- id: dsh-perm-gate
  name: dsh-perm-gate
  config:
    rulesFile: ./permissions.yaml
    defaultAction: ask
    permissive: true            # single front-facing switch (independent tier on)
    permissiveStrategies:        # backend, combinable
      trustAutoAllow: true       # in-scope safe ops auto-allow; dangerous/unknown ask
      alwaysConfirm: false       # every crossing asks; allow-controls add repeat-allow / wl-migrate buttons
      llmAssist: false           # LLM classify first, human fallback on ask/failure
      trustEscalation: true      # a cleared call's own sandbox escalation needs no prompt
    yolo: false                  # unattended: never ask a human, block danger, run the rest
    yoloWorkspaceExempt: false    # YOLO only: stop treating "target unpinnable" as danger (see below)
    rulesFallback: false         # no reviewer available => decide on the rule nets alone
    scriptReview: true           # attach the body of a script the call runs to the review
    credentialPaths: []          # long-tail secret paths, held to the `.ssh` standard
    denyKeywordsExtra: []        # appended blacklist words (never replaces the preset)
    extraContentArgKeys: []      # argument fields that are documents, not operations
    extraOperationArgKeys: []    # argument fields that ARE executed code (wins on conflict)
    safenetPass: true            # the permissive-mech implementation exists (mechanical takeover)
    safenetAsk: false            # the permissive-snet implementation exists (mechanical screen, still asks)
```
Three switches, each owning exactly one permission preset the plugin contributes to the picker —
so a switch changes the behaviour of its own tier and of no other, and switching an implementation
off returns that tier to the ordinary human flow instead of quietly turning it into a different one.

| switch | tier | who settles an ask | asks a person | calls the model |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `permissive` | `permissive` / `permissive-full` | machine screen + grader refine, then a person | yes | per `llmAssist` |
| `safenetAsk` | `permissive-snet` | a person, with the machine screen's doubts listed | **yes** | **never** |
| `safenetPass` | `permissive-mech` | the machine screen alone: named danger blocked + fed back, rest runs | no | **never** |
| `yolo` | `permissive-yolo` | the grader answers in the person's place; risky blocks + feeds back | never | every residual |

`safenetPass` is the reviewed form of `approval: never` (that preset passes every ask with nothing
judging it) and what YOLO degrades to with no reviewer. `yolo` is the model-backed tier by
definition: with no reviewer in seat it still refuses to ask a person, settles on the machine
screen, and records `yolo-allow-no-reviewer` so the history cannot read as if a model had answered.
All five tiers ship in the plugin's own profile patch, so they are in the picker on install —
nothing to hand-edit. Presets outside `gatePresets` never reach any of this: the whole gate
stands down there, so there is no ask to settle.

### `yoloWorkspaceExempt` — the one thing YOLO may stop blocking on

Off by default. It relaxes exactly one signal: **the target could not be pinned down**. A call
whose *content* was never seen is still blocked, so the switch only affects the two shapes where
the act itself is ordinary and only its location is missing — a tool invoked with no arguments at
all, and a script outside the workspace whose body was never read.

| what was missing | switch off | switch on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no arguments to inspect (e.g. a directory-state tool) | block `opaque-payload` | **run** (reviewed, or mechanically when no reviewer) |
| script outside the workspace, body not read | block `opaque-payload` | **run** |
| encoded payload (`-EncodedCommand`, `FromBase64String`, …) | block | **block** |
| script body attached as unreadable (too large / binary) | block | **block** |
| script body missing, or the target is a directory (nothing will run) | ordinary layers | **unchanged** |
| prose with no parseable program | block | **block** |
| delete / remote write | handled by the ordinary layers | **unchanged** |
| P0, credentials, `irreversible`/`neverClear` | deny | **unchanged** |

Two more preconditions are checked before the signal is skipped: every target the call names must
resolve inside the workspace, **following links** (a prefix-only match like `/work2` is not `/work`,
and a link that points outside is refused; a path that cannot be resolved counts as outside), and
the ordinary write/edit contract must be intact. Only `permissive-yolo` reads the switch; the other
tiers ignore it. Allowed calls are recorded as `yolo-allow-opaque-location-exempt` (or
`…-exempt-no-reviewer`), so an exemption can always be told apart from "the screen found nothing".


`trustAutoAllow` is the baseline middle tier (rule-allow auto-passes). `alwaysConfirm` surfaces
the approval panel for every crossing; its "allow controls" add two extended buttons — 
**repeat-allow this type this session** (a bounded session grant) and **allow every occurrence**
(which persists the command word into the `permissions.yaml` allow whitelist via
`approveAllowEverywhere`). `llmAssist` consults a real, configurable LLM (`classifierEndpoint` /
`classifierModel`, any OpenAI-compatible API) to auto-decide an `ask`, and falls back to the
human seam on `ask`/error — always fail-closed. `trustEscalation` (on by default while the tier
is on) answers a `sandbox_permissions` escalation raised from inside a call the gate already
allowed; see below. When `permissive` is off, the gate behaves exactly as before.

### Unattended tiers, and how to protect a secret the preset never heard of

Three switches change **who decides**, seven keys change **what is known**. They are all
`volatile`: an edit in the settings card applies to the next tool call, no reload.

- `yolo` (the `permissive-yolo` tier) — never raises a confirmation. A dangerous ask
  (irreversible, unlearnable, an unreadable payload, or a hard-risk verdict from the configured
  reviewer) is blocked and the reason comes back to the agent as a `工具审核意见` message on
  the **steering lane** (`next-step`: beside the refused tool result, at the same turn's
  next step) rather than the user's input queue;
  everything else runs. With no reviewer in seat the tier does not quietly allow — the mechanical
  screen settles it and the event is recorded as `yolo-allow-no-reviewer`, because a tier that
  advertises a model must not report one it never got.
- `rulesFallback` — degraded review. Only when there is **no reviewer** (none configured, or the
  endpoint gave no verdict) the deterministic nets decide instead of parking the call on a popup
  nobody will answer. While a reviewer answers, nothing changes. It governs the ordinary 自动审查
  tiers (`permissive`, `permissive-full`); the three tiers that own an implementation already say
  who answers, so this switch does not degrade them.
- `scriptReview` (on by default) — when a call runs a script, its body is read (bounded, never
  executed) and shown to the model, the human card, **and** the deterministic nets: a delete that
  only appears inside `clean-home.sh` is now graded on code. A fully-read script also stops being an
  unreadable payload, so it leaves the `U` tier. Switch it off to keep file contents on the machine
  — out-of-workspace script runs then go back to "unknowable, ask a human".

The long tail of *what counts as a secret* is yours to extend, and each list only ever adds to the
built-in one — replacing the preset lists is deliberately not offered, because forgetting `content`
or `plan` would silently re-create a bug this gate already fixed:

- `credentialPaths` — path globs (`**` crosses directories, `*`/`?` stay in one segment; a plain
  entry matches a whole path fragment; `~/` expands to your home; a relative pattern also matches at
  any depth). A listed path is held to the same standard as `.ssh`: reading it outside the workspace
  is refused, mutating it through `write`/`edit` is refused. That tier is P0 — not appealable, not
  clearable by a reviewer — which is why it is a setting and not a `rules.yaml` rule: read-only tools
  are auto-allowed *before* the rule chain runs, so a rule cannot see them.
- `denyKeywordsExtra` — words appended to whichever blacklist is live (preset or your own
  `denyKeywords`), so a company CLI subcommand or token prefix gets a deterministic block without
  you copying fifty preset entries into your profile.
- `extraContentArgKeys` / `extraOperationArgKeys` — which argument fields are prose and which are
  operations. The first stops a host tool's `steps`/`notes` field from being read as an act (that
  is how issue #2 happened: an honest plan naming `rm -rf` got refused for describing it). The
  second opens the reverse route for a `workflowYaml` whose body really executes — and it wins if
  both name the same key. Naming a genuine document field there makes "the plan mentions `rm -rf`"
  a refusal reason again, so it is off by default.

Declaring `command` or `file_path` as prose cannot weaken the gate: the executed command and the
mutated path are judged by their own code paths, not by this table (asserted by tests).

### Sandbox escalation: why a `safe` verdict still prompted

A tool call can raise **two independent approvals**. The gate owns the first — its own `ask`, on
the `tools/pre-execute` waterfall. The second comes from `approveEscalation` **inside the tool
body**, at `tools/execute` time, whenever the model passed `sandbox_permissions` +
`justification`; by then `tools/pre-execute` has already settled, so the gate's allow never
reaches it. A call the LLM graded `safe` and the gate auto-allowed therefore still showed a
prompt asking you to approve the sandbox widening.

`trustEscalation` closes that gap. The gate remembers every call it positively allowed (keyed by
the host's `callId`, which the escalation request repeats) and answers the escalation
`allowed-once` itself. It applies only when *all* hold:

- the 自动审查 tier is on and `trustEscalation` is on;
- the request carries a `callId` the gate cleared, with a matching tool name;
- the reason is a recognized escalation naming `workspace-write` or `danger-full-access`.

Everything else — an unrecognized reason, a different call, a call the gate asked or denied, the
`approval: never` passthrough — delegates to the human unchanged, so a future DSH wording change
fails closed rather than open. The auto-answer is recorded on the event feed
(`verdict: "escalation-auto"`, `mode: <target>`). Turn the switch off to keep widening
human-gated while other allows stay automatic.


### Risk-graded llmAssist, verdict learning, and the event feed

When `llmAssist` is on, the configured LLM grades one `ask` at a time with a structured
protocol. Grading happens **inside the gate's `tools/pre-execute` waterfall, before the decision
is returned to the host**: a `safe` verdict delegates the call straight through, so the approval
panel never appears; only a genuinely uncertain verdict reaches you. Two receiver sources are

# dsh-flowing-plugins

Small [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) (DSH) Web UI plugins for
the composer's dock. Each package is self-contained plain
JavaScript: no build step, no dependencies, no install scripts.

| Package | What it shows |
|---|---|
| [`ollama-quota/`](ollama-quota) | Remaining Ollama Cloud credit and this Session’s estimated Ollama spend. |
| [`ollama-offpeak/`](ollama-offpeak) | Whether Ollama Cloud currently bills at the peak or off-peak rate, and the time left on it. |
| [`opencode-go-quota/`](opencode-go-quota) | OpenCode Go usage (5-hour / weekly / monthly), this Session’s estimated allowance spend, and a limited-time free-model watch. |
| [`provider-visibility/`](provider-visibility) | The active provider beside the model in the composer’s model selector, and the provider/model that served each completed chat turn. |

Both render as ambient chips in the `conversation.composer.dock` slot, below
the composer card alongside the shipped stat pills and the live-speed chip.
Clicking a chip opens a card above it — a headed panel with the figures, a
credit bar where one applies, and the full breakdown — rather than an app-wide
alert or a flat tooltip. Copy is Japanese and English; the chip follows the
active DSH language.

## Install

Install one package from this repository into a DSH profile. Replace `web` with
the profile you use.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:FlowingSPDG/dsh-flowing-plugins/ollama-quota
dsh plugin --profile web add github:FlowingSPDG/dsh-flowing-plugins/ollama-offpeak
dsh plugin --profile web add github:FlowingSPDG/dsh-flowing-plugins/opencode-go-quota
```

Both packages ship plain JavaScript, so a git install needs no build allowance
and no `prepare` script. Afterwards, reload the open Harness page once: a page
that was already open keeps the module graph it booted with, so a newly
installed browser half appears only after a reload.

To remove one:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove @local/ollama-quota
```

The same installs are available from the agent side through
`plugin_manager` (`install_bundle` with the package directory).

## `provider-visibility`

The shipped composer model seat and the chat flow name the model but not the
channel it runs on. Two shipped-slot contributions fill that in:

- **Model selector** (`conversation.input.model.label`) — the trigger, the
  root menu's current value, and each option row render
  `Provider · Model`, with the provider in the quieter label color. The
  provider truncates first in the narrow trigger, so the model name stays
  readable. A catalog badge keeps its shipped position (before the name in the
  trigger, after it in menus) as a neutral pill.
- **Completed turns** (`conversation.chat.turnTail`) — each finished turn
  shows quiet chips of the provider/model routes that actually served it, read
  from the turn's token-usage attribution. A turn without attribution renders
  nothing.

Both contributions are non-interactive; selection controls stay owned by the
shipped seat. Install as above and reload the open Harness page once.

## `ollama-quota`

One chip:

- **Balance** — remaining included credit and allowance, for example

  estimate uses Ollama's published per-token list prices, including the
  peak/off-peak rows at each record's timestamp. It reads the
  durable Session log, so usage from before a context compaction is included,
  and model switches inside one Session are counted per model.

closes on Escape or an outside press, not on transcript scrolling. While it is
open, Session usage refreshes every 10 seconds.

providers are shown separately and never folded into the Ollama spend. A

because their tokens are not logged.

browser never holds it. The Host half resolves the key per call from the DSH

folds the durable events (`request/header`, `assistant/message`,

```yaml
- id: ollama-quota
```

# dsh-flowing-plugins

Small [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) (DSH) Web UI plugins for

| [`provider-visibility/`](provider-visibility) | The active provider beside the model in the composer’s model selector, and the provider/model that served each completed chat turn. |

the composer card alongside the shipped stat pills and the live-speed chip.
Clicking a chip opens a card above it — a headed panel with the figures, a
credit bar where one applies, and the full breakdown — rather than an app-wide
alert or a flat tooltip. Copy is Japanese and English; the chip follows the
active DSH language.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:FlowingSPDG/dsh-flowing-plugins/ollama-quota

dsh plugin --profile web add github:FlowingSPDG/dsh-flowing-plugins/opencode-go-quota
```

and no `prepare` script. Afterwards, reload the open Harness page once: a page
that was already open keeps the module graph it booted with, so a newly
installed browser half appears only after a reload.

# dsh-flowing-plugins

Small [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) (DSH) Web UI plugins for
the composer's dock. Each package is self-contained plain
JavaScript: no build step, no dependencies, no install scripts.

| Package | What it shows |
|---|---|
| [`ollama-quota/`](ollama-quota) | Remaining Ollama Cloud credit and this Session’s estimated Ollama spend. |
| [`ollama-offpeak/`](ollama-offpeak) | Whether Ollama Cloud currently bills at the peak or off-peak rate, and the time left on it. |
| [`opencode-go-quota/`](opencode-go-quota) | OpenCode Go usage (5-hour / weekly / monthly), this Session’s estimated allowance spend, and a limited-time free-model watch. |
| [`provider-visibility/`](provider-visibility) | The active provider beside the model in the composer’s model selector, and the provider/model that served each completed chat turn. |

Both render as ambient chips in the `conversation.composer.dock` slot, below
the composer card alongside the shipped stat pills and the live-speed chip.
Clicking a chip opens a card above it — a headed panel with the figures, a
credit bar where one applies, and the full breakdown — rather than an app-wide
alert or a flat tooltip. Copy is Japanese and English; the chip follows the
active DSH language.

## Install

Install one package from this repository into a DSH profile. Replace `web` with
the profile you use.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:FlowingSPDG/dsh-flowing-plugins/ollama-quota
dsh plugin --profile web add github:FlowingSPDG/dsh-flowing-plugins/ollama-offpeak
dsh plugin --profile web add github:FlowingSPDG/dsh-flowing-plugins/opencode-go-quota
```

Both packages ship plain JavaScript, so a git install needs no build allowance
and no `prepare` script. Afterwards, reload the open Harness page once: a page
that was already open keeps the module graph it booted with, so a newly
installed browser half appears only after a reload.

To remove one:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove @local/ollama-quota
```

The same installs are available from the agent side through
`plugin_manager` (`install_bundle` with the package directory).

## `provider-visibility`

The shipped composer model seat and the chat flow name the model but not the
channel it runs on. Two shipped-slot contributions fill that in:

- **Model selector** (`conversation.input.model.label`) — the trigger, the
  root menu's current value, and each option row render
  `Provider · Model`, with the provider in the quieter label color. The
  provider truncates first in the narrow trigger, so the model name stays
  readable. A catalog badge keeps its shipped position (before the name in the
  trigger, after it in menus) as a neutral pill.
- **Completed turns** (`conversation.chat.turnTail`) — each finished turn
  shows quiet chips of the provider/model routes that actually served it, read
  from the turn's token-usage attribution. A turn without attribution renders
  nothing.

Both contributions are non-interactive; selection controls stay owned by the
shipped seat. Install as above and reload the open Harness page once.

## `ollama-quota`

One chip:

- **Balance** — remaining included credit and allowance, for example
  `$50.29/$60.00`. Clicking it opens the credit bar plus the purchased credit,
  the total, the current period, and when the reading was taken. A failed refresh keeps the last
  reading and marks the chip as stale; an unconfigured key shows
  `Ollama 未設定` / `Ollama not set up` instead of a guess.
- **Session spend** — the open panel also reports this Session's Ollama-only
  request count, token buckets, models, and an estimated USD spend. The
  estimate uses Ollama's published per-token list prices, including the
  peak/off-peak rows at each record's timestamp. It reads the
  durable Session log, so usage from before a context compaction is included,
  and model switches inside one Session are counted per model.

The panel stays open while the agent streams a reply or appends tool logs; it
closes on Escape or an outside press, not on transcript scrolling. While it is
open, Session usage refreshes every 10 seconds.

The shipped `usage` stat pill still owns the all-provider totals. This panel is
deliberately narrower: it answers "how much of my Ollama Cloud credit did this
Session consume?" rather than duplicating the whole-session token pill. Other
providers are shown separately and never folded into the Ollama spend. A
subagent's usage is added in a labelled subtree row when that child Session is
live; title-generation calls are counted as requests but cannot be priced
because their tokens are not logged.

### The API key stays in the Host

The balance endpoint needs the account key in an `Authorization` header, so the
browser never holds it. The Host half resolves the key per call from the DSH
credential store (falling back to the process environment), calls
`GET https://ollama.com/api/balance`, caches one answer, and serves the result to
the page over an exact `GET api/ollama-quota/balance` route registered through
`ctx.connection.fetch.register`. That route lives below the authenticated `/api`
carrier, so the page's own browser-session cookie is the only credential the
browser presents.

Session usage travels over a second exact route,
`GET api/ollama-quota/session?sessionId=…`. A host-only Session projection
folds the durable events (`request/header`, `assistant/message`,
`assistant/attempt`, `compaction/summary`, `subagent/catalog`) once per new
event and the route returns its attributed totals; the browser never folds
events itself. Fork-inherited history is not counted again:
only events owned by the Session contribute, so a fork cannot double-charge the
source conversation. The balance endpoint allows 10 requests per minute per
user, so the Host cache floor is 60 seconds no matter what the configuration
says.

### Configuration

The bundle's `cordis.patch.yml` inserts one row. Override any key in your
profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (a patch replaces the row's whole `config`, so
restate the keys you keep):

```yaml
- id: ollama-quota
  config:
    apiKeyEnv: OLLAMA_CLOUD_API_KEY   # credential reference (environment-variable name)
    baseUrl: https://ollama.com       # balance endpoint base
    refreshSeconds: 60                # Host cache window; minimum 60
    provider: ollama-cloud            # provider id whose calls count toward the balance
    # prices:                         # optional overrides/additions, USD per million tokens
    #   my-new-model: { input: 0.30, cached: 0.006, output: 1.20 }
```

The built-in price table mirrors `https://ollama.com/pricing` and includes a
peak/off-peak pair for `deepseek-v4.1-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro`. If Ollama
changes a price or adds a model, override that row in your profile rather than
editing the package.

Set the key once, either through the DSH credential store (the Models settings
page writes provider keys there) or as `OLLAMA_CLOUD_API_KEY` in the
environment that launches `dsh`.

## `ollama-offpeak`

One chip naming whether Ollama Cloud bills at the peak or off-peak rate right
now, with the time left before it changes:

- `ピーク · 1時間23分` / `Peak · 1h23m` — inside the peak window;
- `オフピーク · 2日3時間` / `Off-peak · 2d 3h` — outside it.

Clicking it opens a card with the current side, the published window, the next
change, and that change in the reader's local time.

The window is the published Ollama Cloud off-peak schedule: peak billing is
weekdays 12:00–18:00 UTC, and every other hour — the whole UTC weekend included
— bills at the off-peak rate. That is the same window the shipped `llm-pi-ai`
Ollama Cloud route carries for its peak routing. The chip recomputes twice a
minute and needs no network and no configuration.

> This chip reports the clock, not your provider's live pricing. If Ollama
> Cloud changes its peak schedule, update `PEAK_START_MINUTES` /
> `PEAK_END_MINUTES` in [`ollama-offpeak/client.js`](ollama-offpeak/client.js).

## `opencode-go-quota`

One chip for [OpenCode Go](https://opencode.ai/docs/console/go/):

- **Usage** — `5h 34% / 週 4% / 月 2%`, the three documented Go windows read
  from `GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage` with the Go API key. The open
  card draws one bar per window with its reset time in the reader's local
  clock; a window at 100% turns the chip red and the card points at free
  models and Extra Usage. The endpoint's live nested shape
  (`usage.rolling.percent` + `resetsAt`) and the early flat shape
  (`rollingUsage.usagePercent` + `resetInSec`) are both accepted.
- **Session spend** — the open card also reports this Session's Go-only
  request count, token buckets, models, and an estimated USD spend against the
  allowance. The estimate uses the published Go token prices, including the
  documented time multipliers at each record's timestamp and the long-context
  tiers. It reads the durable Session log, so usage from before a context
  compaction is included, and model switches inside one Session are counted
  per model; free models are tagged `無料` / `free` and cost zero, and a model
  id ending in `-free` counts as free even when no list price is published.
- **Free-model watch** — the Host half polls the public
  `GET https://opencode.ai/inference/go/v1/models` list (no key needed) every
  10 minutes and tracks the limited-time free models: rows whose published
  input and output token prices are both zero, and rows whose id carries the
  `-free` naming suffix (so a future `-free` listing with non-zero prices
  still counts as free). The chip always shows how many
  models are free right now — `無料` / `FREE` when a watched model is free, a
  green `+N` badge when new ones arrived since your last look, otherwise the
  plain count. The card's free list marks the arrivals `新` / `NEW`; opening
  the card acknowledges them. Each row also tags geo-restricted (`geo`) and
  training-consent (`training`) models.
- **Watched free windows** — `watchModels` (the shipped configuration watches
  `glm-5.3-flash`) names the models whose free windows should be called out by
  name. A watch name matches the list row's id or the bare name of its
  canonical id, so a limited-time `-free` variant published over a paid
  sibling's canonical id (for example `hy4-flash-free` over
  `tencent/hy4-flash`) also flips that sibling to 無料. The card shows each
  watched model as 現在無料 or 現在有料 with its published input list price,
  and a 最近の変化 / recent-changes list records when the watcher saw a model
  become free or paid again (in-memory, so it covers the current host run).

### About peak time

The Go allowance itself has **no peak-time schedule**: the 5-hour, weekly, and
monthly windows are pure percentages and cost the same at 3 a.m. and 3 p.m.
However, the published *token prices* of a few Go models do carry time
multipliers — `deepseek-v4.1-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro` double on weekdays
01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC, and `gemini-4-argon` doubles from
2026-12-01 — so the Session estimate applies them where documented and tags
such models `倍率適用` / `multiplied`. That is why the Session estimate can
move with the clock even though the quota windows do not.

### The credit balance is not readable by key

`GET /zen/go/v1/usage` reports only the three subscription windows; the
workspace's prepaid Zen credit balance is served by the web console's
authenticated session and has no API-key endpoint (tracked upstream in
[anomalyco/opencode#44189](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/44189)).
This package therefore reports allowance consumption the way the API allows —
window percentages plus the Session's estimated dollars — and does not guess a
balance. When the upstream issue lands, the Host half is the single place to
add the read.

### The API key stays in the Host

The usage endpoint needs the Go API key in an `Authorization` header, so the
browser never holds it. The Host half resolves the key per call from the DSH
credential store (falling back to the process environment), calls the usage
endpoint, caches one answer for the configured window (minimum 60 seconds),
and serves the result to the page over an exact
`GET api/opencode-go-quota/usage` route registered through
`ctx.connection.fetch.register`. Session usage travels over a second exact
route, `GET api/opencode-go-quota/session?sessionId=…`, and the free-model
watch over a third, `GET api/opencode-go-quota/free` (with `?ack=1` marking
the currently reported arrivals as seen). All three live below the
authenticated `/api` carrier, so the page's own browser-session cookie is the
only credential the browser presents.

### Configuration

The bundle's `cordis.patch.yml` inserts one row. Override any key in your
profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (a patch replaces the row's whole `config`, so
restate the keys you keep):

```yaml
- id: opencode-go-quota
  config:
    apiKeyEnv: OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY        # credential reference (environment-variable name)
    baseUrl: https://opencode.ai       # usage + models endpoint base
    refreshSeconds: 60                 # Host cache window for usage; minimum 60
    freeRefreshSeconds: 600            # free-model watch cadence; minimum 300
    provider: opencode-go              # provider id whose calls count toward the allowance
    watchModels: [glm-5.3-flash]       # models whose free windows the chip calls out
    # prices:                          # optional overrides/additions, USD per million tokens
    #   my-new-model: { input: 0.30, cached: 0.006, output: 1.20 }
```

The built-in price table mirrors `https://opencode.ai/inference/go/v1/models`,
including the DeepSeek time windows, the Gemini 4 Argon date multiplier, and
the long-context tiers. If OpenCode changes a price or adds a model, override
that row in your profile rather than editing the package.

Set the key once, either through the DSH credential store (the Models settings
page writes provider keys there), or in the launch environment — the same
process / project `.env` / user `.env` chain the OpenCode Go adapter resolves —
or as `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY` in the ambient environment. The free-model watch
needs no key and no configuration.

## Package layout

Each package declares `dsh.bundle.patch` (the Loader rows it inserts),
`dsh.client` (its browser half, served by DSH's client module system), a locale
file for Plugin Manager's title and description, and an icon:

```text
<package>/
  package.json       manifest: exports, files, dsh.bundle, dsh.client
  cordis.patch.yml   the Loader row(s) the bundle inserts
  index.js           Host half (apply(ctx, config))
  client.js          browser half (__ModuleLoader__.load factory)
  locale/{en,ja}.json  Plugin Manager metadata
  icon.svg           Plugin Manager artwork
```

The browser halves draw with the host's `--dsw-alias-*` theme tokens only, and
every resource they add (stylesheet, timers, slot registrations) is removed
with the plugin.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

window percentages plus the Session's estimated dollars — and does not guess a
balance. When the upstream issue lands, the Host half is the single place to
add the read.

### The API key stays in the Host

The usage endpoint needs the Go API key in an `Authorization` header, so the
browser never holds it. The Host half resolves the key per call from the DSH
credential store (falling back to the process environment), calls the usage
endpoint, caches one answer for the configured window (minimum 60 seconds),
and serves the result to the page over an exact
`GET api/opencode-go-quota/usage` route registered through
`ctx.connection.fetch.register`. Session usage travels over a second exact
route, `GET api/opencode-go-quota/session?sessionId=…`, and the free-model
watch over a third, `GET api/opencode-go-quota/free` (with `?ack=1` marking
the currently reported arrivals as seen). All three live below the
authenticated `/api` carrier, so the page's own browser-session cookie is the
only credential the browser presents.

### Configuration

The bundle's `cordis.patch.yml` inserts one row. Override any key in your
profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (a patch replaces the row's whole `config`, so
restate the keys you keep):

```yaml
- id: opencode-go-quota
  config:
    apiKeyEnv: OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY        # credential reference (environment-variable name)
    baseUrl: https://opencode.ai       # usage + models endpoint base
    refreshSeconds: 60                 # Host cache window for usage; minimum 60
    freeRefreshSeconds: 600            # free-model watch cadence; minimum 300
    provider: opencode-go              # provider id whose calls count toward the allowance
    watchModels: [glm-5.3-flash]       # models whose free windows the chip calls out
    # prices:                          # optional overrides/additions, USD per million tokens
    #   my-new-model: { input: 0.30, cached: 0.006, output: 1.20 }
```

The built-in price table mirrors `https://opencode.ai/inference/go/v1/models`,
including the DeepSeek time windows, the Gemini 4 Argon date multiplier, and
the long-context tiers. If OpenCode changes a price or adds a model, override
that row in your profile rather than editing the package.

Set the key once, either through the DSH credential store (the Models settings
page writes provider keys there), or in the launch environment — the same
process / project `.env` / user `.env` chain the OpenCode Go adapter resolves —
or as `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY` in the ambient environment. The free-model watch
needs no key and no configuration.

## Package layout

Each package declares `dsh.bundle.patch` (the Loader rows it inserts),
`dsh.client` (its browser half, served by DSH's client module system), a locale
file for Plugin Manager's title and description, and an icon:

```text
<package>/
  package.json       manifest: exports, files, dsh.bundle, dsh.client
  cordis.patch.yml   the Loader row(s) the bundle inserts
  index.js           Host half (apply(ctx, config))
  client.js          browser half (__ModuleLoader__.load factory)
  locale/{en,ja}.json  Plugin Manager metadata
  icon.svg           Plugin Manager artwork
```

The browser halves draw with the host's `--dsw-alias-*` theme tokens only, and
every resource they add (stylesheet, timers, slot registrations) is removed
with the plugin.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-composer-plus — Composer Plus for DeepSeek Harness [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-composer-plus)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-composer-plus) [![test](https://github.com/furkancak1r/dsh-composer-plus/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/furkancak1r/dsh-composer-plus/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![license: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) **English** · [中文](README.zh.md) · [Türkçe](README.tr.md) · [Español](README.es.md) · [Português (Brasil)](README.pt-BR.md) · [Français](README.fr.md) · [Deutsch](README.de.md) · [Русский](README.ru.md) · [日本語](README.ja.md) · [한국어](README.ko.md) · [Bahasa Indonesia](README.id.md) · [Tiếng Việt](README.vi.md) · [हिन्दी](README.hi.md) Codex-style quality-of-life features for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh) desktop and web UI: a Changes panel, swipe-card feature ideas, sidebar search in message text, turn rollback with file restore, chat deletion to the Trash, the project name under the composer, project status in the sidebar, input history, a plan-mode shortcut, one-click Continue, resume running chats after a restart, queue drag-and-drop, session deeplinks, chat export as Markdown, per-chat Auto Review grants, background notifications, iPhone access with the Tether app and automatic updates. **In one line:** a single DeepSeek Harness plugin (npm `dsh-composer-plus`, shown as **Composer Plus** in Settings → Plugins) that adds a git Changes panel, Tinder-style feature idea cards, sidebar search that also finds words in messages, ↶ turn rollback (chat only, or chat and files), Delete chat, the project name under the composer, ↑/↓ input history, a Shift+Tab `/plan` toggle, one-click ▶ Continue, Resume after restart, drag-and-drop queue reordering, Copy session link, Export as Markdown, Auto Review “Allow for this chat”, background notifications, iPhone access (Mobile connect, Tether app), 11 extra interface languages and automatic updates.

Unofficial community plugin. The update check (GitHub releases and the npm registry) makes network calls; switch off **Automatic updates** to stop them at startup. **Turkish skill pack** (on by default) downloads the turkish-anti-ai-skill from GitHub and checks it for a newer version once a day, only while **Application language** is Türkçe; switch it off in **Settings → Composer Plus** to stop these calls. **Feature ideas** calls your chat's own model only when you click **Suggest features**. **Next message prediction** (on by default) calls the model chosen in Settings (dsh's default unless you pick another) once after each finished turn, without a click. Switch it off in **Settings → Composer Plus** to stop these calls. **Complete while typing** (off by default) calls its chosen model (by default the prediction's) at each pause while you type, after you switch it on. **Improve prompt** calls a model only when you click its magic wand. **Task board** calls the new chat's model once for the tags of each task that you start on the board. With its **AI summary** setting (the default is **Fast (no AI)**), it also calls a running chat's model for a short progress note while you look at that task's progress on the board or in Tether. **Goal check** (on by default) calls a model once each time the agent marks a `/goal` complete in an automatic round. **Mobile connect** (off by default) accepts iPhone connections from your local network or tailnet only after you switch it on. ## Install **Desktop app:** Settings → Plugins → **Add plugin** → enter `dsh-composer-plus` → **Enable now**. You can also paste `https://github.com/furkancak1r/dsh-composer-plus` instead of the npm name. **Web / CLI profile:** ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-composer-plus ``` Then restart dsh. (The CLI can't install into the desktop profile; the app manages it.) > dsh's pnpm skips versions younger than 24 hours. Right after a release, add the version: `dsh-composer-plus@1.30.1`. ## Features | Feature | How to use it | Screenshot | |---|---|---| | **Changes panel** | Right sidebar → `+` → **Changes**. The page opens on **Tree**: a branch map of the chat's repository. Three cards count the branches: all of them, the merged ones and the ones that wait to merge. Click a card to show only those branches; click it again to show all. Each branch is a box with its last commit: green when the main branch has its work, orange when not, blue for the main branch. An arrow goes from each branch to the branch that took it (✅ **Merged**) or to the branch that it started from (⏳ **Waiting**, dashed). Click a box to see the branch's commits, then click a commit to see its files and their diffs. Click **Merged** to see the files of the merge commit, or **Waiting** to see the files that the branch brings into its target. A remote branch shows only when no local branch has the same name. In the mode menu, pick **Uncommitted**, **Unstaged**, **Staged** or **Branch** to see changed files with `+/-` counts; click a file for its diff. **Last Turn** opens dsh's own review of the latest turn. **This chat** lists only the files that the open chat's file tools (write, edit) wrote, in all its turns, and their total diff since its first message. The **␣** button hides whitespace changes (`git diff -w`): lines that changed only in indentation or line endings do not show. A file's **…** menu → **Chats that changed this file** lists the chats of the same repository whose write or edit tools changed that file, newest first, with the request that did it; a click opens that chat at that request. | | | **Feature ideas** | Right sidebar → `+` → **Feature ideas** → **Suggest features**. The chat's own model reads a short summary of the chat's project (top-level files, the README and manifest heads, an outline of the rest of the README, the titles of recent commits) and suggests up to 8 features, shown as a stack of cards in dsh's UI language. Swipe a card right (or click **✓**, or press `→`; the card flies off to its side in each case) to start a new chat in the same project: it starts in plan mode with the idea as the request, so nothing changes before you approve the plan. To skip the plan, click **▶ Build now** (or press `↑`; the card flies up): the new chat starts at once with the idea as an ordinary request, and the model makes the change and runs its checks (approvals apply as usual). Swipe left (or **✕**, or `←`) to skip; **Undo** (or `Z`) brings a skipped card back.
