evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# @dsh/remote-ops

DeepSeek Harness plugin for SSH, Windows desktop, web and RESTful API operations. Users and Agents share visible terminals, application windows, webpages and request records.

## Local terminals on demand (v0.16.0)

Startup opens **one default local terminal**, initially CMD on Windows. The **+** beside the terminal tabs opens another default terminal; its dropdown opens CMD, Windows PowerShell 5.1, PowerShell 7 or one installed WSL distribution. Unavailable entries are disabled with a reason. Install PowerShell 7 or WSL distributions on the DSH host first, then use **Settings → Terminal → Redetect**.

**Settings → Terminal → Local terminal** stores the default shell and starting directory, plus an optional WSL user. Use `~` or an absolute Linux path for WSL. Saving affects future opens and the next startup; existing processes remain unchanged. An empty Windows directory uses `$DSH_HOME/remote-ops`. Local terminals are shared across conversations in the DSH workspace, with separate processes, output and logs. A restart opens only the default, without restoring additional tabs.

The default tab stays pinned; additional local tabs can be closed individually. After `exit`, the tab turns grey and retains its last output with an explicit **Reopen terminal** action. Reopening never replays commands. **Close all** remains limited to current-conversation remote tabs and preserves every local terminal. Copy/paste, echoed-command highlighting and TXT/ZIP export work across local terminals. Log retention is bounded and in memory; export required records before restarting.

Agents load the bundled `remote-ops-environments` skill, discover engines and sessions with `remote_local_shells`, then call `remote_local_open`. It reuses a matching running session with no known active task by default; use `reuse:false` for an independent process. Route subsequent operations to its returned `sessionId`. The pinned default retains the legacy ID `local-cmd`; inspect `shell` instead of assuming CMD syntax.

## Encrypted SSH private keys (v0.15.12)

In **环境 → 终端环境**, create or edit an SSH environment and enter the private key path on the DSH host. Enter the key’s decryption passphrase in **私钥口令（可选）**. Leave it empty for an unencrypted key. DSH stores the account password and key passphrase separately. Leaving the passphrase blank while editing keeps the saved value. To remove it, select **清除已保存的私钥口令** and save. Use the environment’s Test or Connect action to verify the login.

## Collapsible environment groups (v0.15.4)

Click a group name in the environment drawer to collapse or expand it. Groups start expanded. Terminal and API environments remember their groups independently. Searching reveals matches and clearing the search restores your layout. Bulk selection includes only visible environments in expanded groups.

## Environment drawer and compact toolbar (v0.15.3)

Environments open in a left drawer inside the plugin: overlay by default, optionally pinned on wide panels, and full width on narrow panels. Escape restores focus; drafts, terminal sessions, webpages and recordings remain available. Compact toolbars and row More menus free workspace space. Verified locally with DSH Desktop 0.2.1-rc.5.

## Web recordings and bundled browser (v0.15.2)

Start, stop, read and export human/Agent webpage operations from the Web toolbar or `remote_browser_recording`. The bundled `remote-ops-web-recordings` skill teaches the Agent to interpret records, parameterize device addresses and generate code in the user's chosen framework or template.

Windows x64 and Linux x64 packages include the embedded Chromium. The plugin prepares it offline on load and the first page open waits for it. Linux requires Chromium system libraries. Sites using the matching intranet bridge can upgrade v0.14.0 and v0.14.1 with one click in the plugin. The ZIP includes deployment instructions.

## Serial terminals (v0.14.1)

In **Environments → Terminal environments → Add**, select **SERIAL** beside SSH and TELNET. Select a port or enter the device path available to the plugin host, such as `COM3`, `/dev/ttyUSB0`, or `/dev/cu.usbserial-001`. Set the baud rate, data bits, stop bits, parity, flow control, encoding and line ending to match the device. Defaults are 9600 baud, 8N1, no flow control and CR. Save and enter the environment to open its terminal tab.

The user and Agent share input, device output and log exports. Agents can list ports with `remote_serial_ports`, save `transport: "serial"` with `serial.path` through `remote_environment_create`, then use the existing terminal tools. Only one connection can own a port at a time. Closing the tab releases it. The connection test opens and closes the port; inspect device output to verify commands.

## Save environment credentials from chat (v0.13.2)

When you explicitly provide an account/password for an environment, the Agent can create or update it directly. SSH/Telnet use `username` and `password` in `remote_environment_create/update`; API uses `auth.username` and a top-level `password` in `remote_api_environment_save`. GUI entry remains optional.

Passwords go to DSH credentials; environment files store references and tool results omit plaintext. Replacing a password affects only that environment. Omit/null preserves it; an empty string is rejected. Choose either password or passwordRef. Existing terminals stay connected; API environments require login again after edits. DSH manages its own conversation and tool-call history.

## Telnet terminals (v0.13.1)

Choose **Environments → Terminal environments → Add**, select Telnet, and save the host, port (default 23) and login mode. Supports username/password, password-only, no-login and manual terminal login. Automatic credentials are submitted once; a failed login leaves the output available for inspection.

Users and Agents share the visible terminal, tabs, status indicators and log exports. Close all now includes this conversation's SSH, TELNET and SERIAL tabs while keeping local CMD. Connection, login readiness and command results are separate. Configure encoding, line endings and prompt patterns for device CLIs. Telnet is unencrypted; file transfer uses SSH/SFTP.

Existing `remote_environment_*` and `remote_terminal_*` tools and bundled skills cover the flow without Agent changes. See the [Telnet guide](TELNET.md).

## Windows desktop operations

The **桌面** workspace shows real Windows application windows. Connect the DSH Windows host or a saved Windows SSH environment, launch software, inspect UIA controls, fill fields, click buttons and verify outcomes. Users can operate the same window; native DSH cancellation stops later steps. Export this conversation's desktop records and last captured windows as a ZIP.

The tgz includes the pinned worker and dependencies plus the native `remote-ops-desktop` skill. Use a logged-on, unlocked Windows 11 or Windows Server Desktop Experience session; the SSH account must match that desktop user. Hot reload waits for active desktop work and retains connections and logs. See the [Windows desktop guide](DESKTOP.md).

Start with [remote Windows setup](DESKTOP.md#远程电脑的一次性配置), then copy the [complete Notepad task](DESKTOP.md#完整示例打开记事本输入并保存) into DSH (guide in Chinese). It opens a new document, enters text and saves through the application UI, then reads the saved file independently over SSH to verify its contents.

## Hot reload after updates

v0.12.3 also supports hosts that reload plugins during package installation. When needed, it first waits for active work and preserves the running state before installing; final activation still waits for idle. Update submission returns immediately while the operation continues in the background. Brief connection gaps recover automatically; persistent failures show the request address and details. **刷新更新状态** reads progress without repeating installation. An installation that has not returned after 10 minutes explicitly reports an unconfirmed result.

Starting with v0.11.0, **设置 → 更新 → 检查并更新** downloads, verifies and installs a newer release, then automatically applies it when work is idle. DSH keeps running. The update view explains waits for conversation activity, terminal waits and independent commands, transfers, browser jobs/runtime installation, and API requests. Browser uploads defer reload until the whole batch finishes or is cancelled, including the gaps between file requests.

The handoff preserves the current conversation and draft, saved settings, live terminal/browser connections, terminal logs, and API authentication and records. No command or request is replayed. Output silence is not treated as proof that a manual terminal command finished: its connection is retained. New connections use the new implementation; existing transports retain the implementation they were created with.

A failed startup restores the previous runtime and exposes **重试应用已安装版本** (retry activation). Running and installed versions remain distinct. Missing host reload APIs or an incompatible runtime state format produce an explicit restart requirement.

**For the first migration from v0.12.2 or earlier, finish active work and install this tgz through DSH plugin management or the CLI.** After CLI installation, if the running version is still old and the page responds, use **重试应用已安装版本** in the update settings to activate the installed package without reinstalling it. Hosts without hot-reload support need a restart. If the old updater is already stuck, check the host installation log and installed version, then restart DSH once after installation completes; do not submit another install. Subsequent compatible updates from the fixed runtime can hot reload. A full restart requires reconnecting terminals and webpages but preserves saved configuration and conversations. Refreshing the browser alone does not update the backend. See the [v0.12.3 acceptance record](https://github.com/Ssshake1996/myterm/blob/main/docs/testing/dsh-remote-ops-v0.12.3-acceptance.md).

## Remote tab status and close all

The terminal strip exposes **全部关闭** (close all). It closes the current conversation's SSH tabs and their connections captured when clicked, preserving local CMD, saved environments and other conversations. Live connections or known running commands receive one combined confirmation with an active-operation count; disconnected tabs without running commands clear immediately. Failed closures remain visible with a reason. Connections opened during confirmation are excluded from that selection.

| Indicator | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Amber ring | Waiting for output, executing an independent command or closing; hover for the specific state and whether the Agent initiated it |
| Green dot | Connected; not proof that a command finished or a business operation succeeded |
| Hollow gray dot | Disconnected without a known running command; received output is retained for inspection or export |

Shapes, text and accessible descriptions accompany the colors; blue still marks the selected tab. Amber is informational and human input remains available. Ordinary keystrokes and new output are not treated as reliably timed command executions.

Closing cancels associated waits and independent commands and requests SSH channel shutdown. Remote process termination remains unconfirmed; commands are not replayed. Closing tabs does not erase retained logs, which remain available through log tools or **更多 → 一键打包本会话全部日志** within the retention limits.

## Windows OpenSSH

Windows desktop and Server use the existing SSH environment, terminal, file and log workspaces. Choose the target platform and server-default, CMD, Windows PowerShell 5.1 or an installed PowerShell 7 in **环境 → 终端环境 → SSH**. **测试** reports authentication, detected system, PTY, SFTP and the host fingerprint separately.

`remote_environment_create/update/test` manages and diagnoses targets. `remote_command_execute` accepts a Windows shell, literal working directory and named PowerShell parameters, and returns exit status and separate error output. Windows independent commands authenticate a separate SSH connection while preserving the visible terminal. SFTP handles drive paths, Unicode and spaces; existing file and multi-terminal log tools remain available.

The package includes the native DSH `remote-ops-windows` skill. See the [Windows guide](WINDOWS.md) and [verification matrix](https://github.com/Ssshake1996/myterm/blob/main/docs/testing/dsh-remote-ops-v0.10.2-acceptance.md). No Agent modification is required.

## Workspace tabs

Terminal, Web, Files and API now form a compact left-aligned group. The blue selection line spans the complete tab button. Narrow panels use smaller padding while retaining labels, background activity badges and arrow / Home / End navigation. Switching preserves workspace contents.

## Terminal layout and request diagnostics

- Session tabs, close all, search and the current TXT download share one row, with approximately 32px desktop tabs. All-log ZIP export lives under **更多**; the bottom status bar shows the path, quick commands remain below, and **设置 → 终端** controls the active SSH size.
- Error headings distinguish state refresh, terminal output refresh and plugin update failures. Expand **错误详情** for the request method, redacted URL, HTTP status, stage, timestamp and bounded response preview. Network failures explicitly say that no HTTP response was received.
- Update failures identify the version manifest, SHA256 file or archive, including the actual failed URL. Upstream HTTP status and the plugin endpoint status are labeled separately.
- The same background refresh failure is automatically announced once per DSH/plugin runtime. Dismissing it, switching workspaces or refreshing the page does not repeatedly reopen it. Background retries continue; explicit **刷新状态** still reports its result. Recovery clears the corresponding state error; a new backend runtime enables notifications again.
- Diagnostics redact URL query values and common password, Token, Cookie and Authorization fields. They do not collect request bodies or headers.

For a 404, first identify whether the failed URL is `/api/dsh-remote-ops/state` or an update-source file, then check plugin loading, service routing or the release directory accordingly. Version checks remain manual.

## Workspace layout

- All workspaces share one **设置** entry with general, terminal, browser and update categories. **环境** manages SSH and API environments together, retaining their separate forms and credentials.
- Local CMD and SSH use one consistent terminal tab strip, with a filled background, border and bold text for the active tab. Arrow keys switch terminals. Environments open in a drawer on the left of the plugin workspace, with a persistent close button. Escape closes it and restores focus to the environment entry, retaining terminal and request drafts. The terminal row contains close all, search, current TXT download and **更多** (more). Quick commands start as a compact strip; expand it or open **命令库** to manage saved commands.
- Workspace tabs show unread terminal output, file transfers and browser execution. Viewing the corresponding terminal clears its unread indicator. Transfers show a percentage only when the total is known reliably.
- API results have **响应 / 记录** tabs. Expand JSON nodes and click a field name to copy its JSON Pointer, with selectable text when clipboard access fails. HTTP status uses both color and text; 2xx also says **请检查业务结果**. Large trees render in batches and retain a raw view.
- Workspace/settings switches preserve terminal, browser and API state. Background work continues while hidden browser views suspend frame requests.

## Manual intranet HTTP/HTTPS updates

Open Remote Ops → **设置 → 更新**, save a source, then choose **仅检查版本** (check only) or **检查并更新** (check and install). Choose the default GitHub Release source or an intranet HTTP/HTTPS URL. Clicking a button starts the check; a newer stable version can then be installed. Running and installed versions are shown separately. Compatible updates automatically activate when ongoing work finishes; the view reports the waiting reason and the resulting running version.

Keep `latest.json`, `dsh-remote-ops-v0.16.0.tgz` and `SHA256SUMS-dsh-remote-ops-v0.16.0.txt` in the feed directory. Generate the manifest from the unchanged official release pair:

```sh
node integrations/dsh-remote-ops/scripts/create-update-manifest.mjs ./release/dsh-remote-ops-v0.16.0.tgz
```

The installed package also includes `scripts/create-update-manifest.mjs`. An optional second argument chooses an existing parent directory's `latest.json`, allowing version subdirectories. The script verifies checksum and package identity, refuses a lower version, and writes the manifest atomically. Upload the tgz/checksum first and publish the manifest last. Serve the directory over HTTP/HTTPS. GitHub Release provides the tgz and SHA256 checksum file.

- HTTP(S): use a directly readable directory URL or `latest.json` URL containing the scheme, host and path. All files and redirects must remain on that origin; the server must allow the DSH host to download them directly. Trust internal HTTPS certificates in the DSH Node process.
- Dependencies use the DSH registry, proxy and build-approval configuration. Provide an accessible internal npm registry when needed. The embedded browser ships with the plugin. Full Chromium for independent windows is optional.

Verified packages are cached on the DSH host and installed by the current profile's native DSH plugin manager. Source settings live in `$DSH_HOME/remote-ops/update-settings.json` and are shared within that DSH home; installation affects the current profile. Installation errors provide a reason and log location. Failed hot reload restores the previous runtime and allows an explicit activation retry. Follow the activation or restart steps above for the first migration; a full restart does not restore process-local connections or records. The bundled `remote-ops-updates` skill covers configuration, feed generation and diagnostics.

## Saved RESTful environments and execution workspace

- The **API** workspace saves base URLs, groups, common headers, timeout, private CA and login configuration. API targets work without SSH; an optional SSH environment ID links the same device without sharing credentials.
- A single POST login sends username/password as JSON or form and extracts a Token through JSON Pointer or a response header, or stores scoped Cookies. Cookie-to-CSRF-header mapping is supported. Passwords use DSH credentials; configuration stores references. Login sessions are isolated by conversation and remain in memory only.
- UI and Agent requests share visible login/request records, HTTP status, timing, redacted responses, errors and unknown outcomes. Export the current conversation's records as JSON. HTTP 2xx still requires checking the business response.
- The bundled `remote-ops-api` skill guides Agent operations: select a target with `remote_api_environment_list`, manage it with `remote_api_environment_save/delete`, then use exact returned IDs with `remote_api_login`, `remote_api_request` and `remote_api_records`.
- Requests originate on the DSH host. Both `/items` and `items` preserve the base URL's path prefix. No automatic redirects, reauthentication or replay. After a timeout/cancellation with an unknown outcome, query device state before any retry.
- Configuration persists in `$DSH_HOME/remote-ops/api/environments.json`; login state, records and duplicate-ID protection cover only this process's last 100 requests per conversation. Response preview: 128 KiB; request body: 1 MiB. Edits invalidate login; running requests keep their captured target. Switching tabs does not cancel requests.
- Credentials and known authentication values are redacted; business payloads may still contain sensitive data.

## Local CMD commands and directory colors

The terminal uses a [Catppuccin](https://catppuccin.com/palette/)-inspired Latte / Mocha palette following the DSH light/dark theme: purple commands, teal directories and blue files. Light accents are darkened for readable text contrast. Error, warning and success prefixes also receive emphasis; verify outcomes from the actual output. Surrounding plugin controls use host styling.

Commands echoed after a standard prompt now use the same accent, weight and subtle background whether typed manually, sent as a complete Agent command or entered through raw keys. Recognition runs after terminal cursor redraws, so visible edits/backspaces remain readable. No extra command is executed and hidden input is never added to the display.

Standard `dir` rows show directory names in teal and file names in blue, leaving timestamps, sizes and totals unchanged. Existing ANSI colors are retained. Common CMD, PowerShell and `user@host` Shell prompts are recognized; custom prompts and formats without type information, such as `dir /b`, are not guessed. Full-screen applications do not receive these semantic colors. Terminal display settings can disable them; copied, searched and exported text stays unchanged.

## Reveal environment passwords on demand

The SSH password field in the environment editor has an eye button. It stays masked by default and resolves the currently effective saved credential only on request. Hiding the password or closing the editor/drawer clears the revealed value. Newly typed passwords can also be shown for checking.

Viewing alone never changes the credential: saving other fields preserves it; typing a replacement updates it. Missing configuration, missing credentials and unavailable providers have clear retry/re-entry messages. Revealed values are not written to browser storage, environment listings, diagnostic records or Agent tool results. The bundled environment-management skill describes the user-facing path.

## Terminal copy and paste

Local CMD, SSH, Telnet and Serial terminals share copy/paste behavior. Select output and press `Ctrl+C`, or right-click and choose **复制选中内容**. With no selection, `Ctrl+C` remains the terminal interrupt signal. `Ctrl+V` and **粘贴到终端** send clipboard text to the active session; single-line text is sent immediately, while multiline text opens a confirmation dialog before submission.

The context menu also provides **全选输出**. Copied text is plain text without terminal colors or cursor decoration. If browser clipboard permission is unavailable, the UI explains the reason and you can select text manually or type it. Copy/paste changes only the visible terminal; it does not change Agent tools or add hidden input to retained logs.

## Terminal logs

- The download button beside terminal tabs exports the current terminal as UTF-8 TXT. **更多 → 一键打包本会话全部日志** exports all available conversation logs as ZIP, including retained closed SSH records and the shared local terminal. Each ZIP contains separate transcripts and a `manifest.json` with source, time and coverage metadata.
- `remote_terminal_logs`, `remote_terminal_log_read` and `remote_terminal_log_export` provide discovery, raw-cursor pagination and packaging. The export tool returns SHA256 and an absolute download link for the observed trusted DSH browser origin (or null when unavailable; use the toolbar); the Agent need not copy screen text, read every page or run archive commands.
- The bundled `remote-ops-terminal-logs` skill is automatically discoverable through DSH, with `/remote-ops-terminal-logs` also available. The tgz carries both tools and instructions.
- Retention is process memory: 4 MiB per terminal, trimmed to the latest 3 MiB on overflow; closed records share a 16 MiB / 32-record limit. APIs disclose truncation and evictions. History does not survive restart. Hidden/raw input is not logged separately, but secrets printed by programs can still be present.
- A package accepts at most 32 logs / 32 MiB raw output. Download cache is limited to 10 packages / 32 MiB; links expire after one hour, earlier eviction or host restart. Exports freeze current buffers; later output needs a new export. Progress frames are retained as lines, not a replay of a full-screen application. Independent commands and browser activity are separate records.

## Agent environment management

`remote_environment_list/create/update/delete` manages SSH environment definitions. The bundled `remote-ops-environments` skill covers targets, updates, groups, credentials and existing connections. It registers through DSH's native skill provider; user/project skills retain their normal precedence.

## Interface and interaction

- Terminal, web, files, environments, saved commands and diagnostics share consistent typography, spacing, controls and host-aware light/dark surfaces. Workspace tabs stay at the top; version, diagnostics and comfortable/compact density live under **设置 → 通用**. Updates live under **设置 → 更新**. Density persists in this browser.
- Local CMD and SSH share one tab row with search and export fixed on the right. When tabs overflow, left and right buttons scroll to earlier or later tabs without closing connections; each button is disabled at its boundary. Arrow keys and Home/End select and reveal a terminal. Background output and status refreshes preserve manual scrolling.
- The web workspace prioritizes the address and live page. **设置 → 网页** contains engines, browser runtime status, viewport and zoom. **收藏** manages sites and flows; **操作记录** expands below the live page. Returning to the workspace retains the URL draft and current page.
- Switching an open page between embedded and independent display requires confirmation. Cancel dispatches nothing; confirming reloads the page and may lose unsent form content. Switching cannot be submitted repeatedly while pending.
- File batch actions appear after selection. Upload controls match other buttons, and browser uploads show byte progress. Module switches retain selection, drafts and background jobs; completed transfers still use coalesced directory refreshes.

The left action opens the native DSH right sidebar. Human and Agent input is shared; use native conversation cancellation to stop the Agent.

## Embedded browser and independent windows

On Windows x64 and Linux x64 the plugin verifies its bundled Headless Shell in a per-user cache when it loads. Opening an embedded URL waits for local preparation and restores damaged cache files from the plugin. Linux requires Chromium's system libraries. Full Chromium for independent windows is optional.

- Independent windows follow the Windows user's default HTTP(S) browser on the DSH host, supporting installed Chrome / Edge with an isolated plugin profile. Embedded mode still defaults to matching Chromium. Each mode has its own engine preference. Explicit saved-site or tool browser choices take precedence. Unsupported/unavailable defaults report an error instead of silently opening Edge. A remote DSH host's default is separate from the client viewing DSH.
- Prefer an action array for `steps`. Single action objects, a sole `{steps:[...]}` envelope and JSON-encoded versions are accepted. Prefer `{kind,value,name?,frame?}` locator objects for `target`; JSON-encoded locator objects and CSS/XPath strings (`css=#id`, `xpath=//button`, `#id`, `//button`) are accepted. All steps normalize and validate before dispatch. Equivalent requests deduplicate under the same `requestId`.
- Open embedded URLs directly using `remote_browser_open`. After a preparation failure, use `remote_browser_runtime` action `repair` to retry offline. Action `install` downloads full Chromium for a requested dedicated independent window.
- `BROWSER_STEP_INVALID` identifies the field, accepted format and no-dispatch status. Correct the argument instead of repeating an unchanged invalid call; preflight rejection does not reserve the request ID. The bundled `remote-ops-browser` skill describes argument formats and recovery steps. Restart DSH and refresh its webpage after upgrading; verify the current version in **设置 → 通用**.

## Workspaces and interaction

- Environments use a 360px overlay drawer inside the plugin. It fills panels below 480px; panels at least 960px wide can pin it at 320px. Opening and closing the overlay preserves terminal, browser and API instances, the webpage viewport and active recordings. Search, group selection and the list share the drawer. Rows expose Connect/Use and More; editing, testing, deletion and independent SSH connections live in More. Sticky Save/Cancel actions remain available; ordinary drafts persist, while revealed passwords clear on close. Batch management confirms selected names and addresses before deletion, retains failed selections with reasons, and leaves configuration unchanged on cancellation. SSH group menus rename or delete empty groups; API groups are set in the form.
- **终端 / 网页 / 文件 / API** workspace tabs support arrows and Home/End. Environment management opens inside the panel; **设置 → 通用** contains diagnostics and refresh, while **设置 → 更新** handles updates. The native DSH right Sidebar and the main conversation are preserved.
- The module, selected terminal and environment filter recover per conversation after closing/reopening or refreshing. File path/sort/scroll/bookmarks keep their existing persistence. File filters, path drafts and reconciled selections survive module/panel switches within one webpage; a full reload fetches fresh entries and does not restore old selections.
- **设置 → 终端** contains font size, wrapping, highlighting and the active SSH connection size. Search and current transcript export are directly beside the session tabs; **更多** contains independent commands and all-log ZIP export. The path and technical status sit in the bottom status bar. ASCII/SGR logs use a fast parser; cursor control, Unicode and full-screen programs retain the VT model.
- Embedded pages default to **

# dsh-machine-status

Read-only host health snapshots for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) 0.2.2-rc.3, profile `web`.
One model-facing tool answers "what did the machine last report, when, what changed and why it
needs attention" without running a command, sampling on demand, asking for approval, or showing a GUI.

An independent **systemd user timer** samples the host every 60 s and writes three versioned JSON
documents. The Host row and the CLI only read them. Repeated status calls cost no new sampling.

## Verified host contract (not assumed)

Checked against the installed 0.2.2-rc.3 sources on 2026-11-18:

| Contract | Verification |
|---|---|
| Host plugin form `export function apply(ctx, config)` + `export const inject = ['tools']` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-manager` docs; the installed `@sulytwelve/dsh-context-manager` uses the same form |
| `ctx.tools.register(def)` returns the disposer; definitions may be plain objects without `@deepseek-ai/*` imports | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` service contract; context-manager `index.js:204-217,724` |
| Tool shape `{name, description, parameters, output:{schema, render}, execute}`; `render` returns `[{type:'text', text}]` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-todo/src/index.ts:136-213` |
| Bundle manifest `dsh.bundle.patch` + `cordis.patch.yml` `- insert:` row | installed context-manager `package.json`, `cordis.patch.yml` |
| `dsh plugin --profile web add <spec>` installs the package **and** selects the bundle in `dsh.profile.bundles` | run against the target profile on 2026-11-18; `dsh-plugin-manager/src/index.ts:1270-1288` |
| `ctx.tools.schemas()` projects the registered tool into the model-facing schema list | invoked from `apply`; the heartbeat records `modelFacing: true` |

## How it works

```
systemd user timer (60 s)
  └─ bin/sampler.mjs  → collects (timeouts, read-only)
                      → evaluates rules + incident streaks
                      → atomic writes: snapshot.json, state.json, status.json
                                               (notifications.jsonl when opted in)

DSH Host row `machine-status`          CLI `dsh-machine-status`
  └─ machine_status tool (pure read)    └─ status / evidence / sources / doctor / export
```

No part of the read path spawns a process, writes machine state, or calls a model.
The plugin's only side effect is `plugin-loaded.json`, a heartbeat that records whether the
running Host registry projects `machine_status` into the model-facing schemas.

## Install

### 1. Plugin row (on the DSH host, as the DSH user)

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:Sulytwelve/dsh-machine-status#v0.1.4
```

This also appends the bundle to `dsh.profile.bundles` (verified on the reference host; no hand edit
needed).

Restart the DSH process that serves the profile so it loads the new JavaScript. **DSH's CLI does not
install, provide, or manage a systemd unit** — how that process is supervised is deployment-specific.
Use whatever starts your server: a terminal launch, a container, or your own supervisor.


### 2. Sampler timer (same user, no root)

```sh
node <profile>/node_modules/@sulytwelve/dsh-machine-status/bin/cli.mjs install
# or, with the package on PATH: dsh-machine-status install
```

`install` writes `~/.local/state/dsh-machine-status/config.json`, copies the runtime to
`~/.local/lib/dsh-machine-status/`, writes two user units and enables the timer.
The user timer survives logout only with lingering enabled (`loginctl show-user <user> -p Linger`);
this host already reports `Linger=yes`.

`dsh-machine-status install --dry-run` prints every action without changing anything.

## Paths and permissions

| Path | Owner / mode | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.local/state/dsh-machine-status/` | DSH user, `0700` | config, snapshot, status, state, notifications |
| `…/snapshot.json`, `status.json`, `state.json` | `0600` | versioned documents; every write goes through a same-directory temp + rename |
| `~/.local/lib/dsh-machine-status/` | DSH user | stable runtime copy used by the units |
| `~/.config/systemd/user/dsh-machine-status.{service,timer}` | DSH user | user units |
| `~/.dsh/storages/agent_memory` | **never touched** | owned by the context-manager plugin |

Cleanup ownership: this plugin owns only the three paths above. `uninstall` keeps the state
directory unless `--purge` is passed; `--purge` removes only its own directory.

## Tool usage

`machine_status` with `op=status` (default), `op=evidence&id=…`, or `op=sources`.
The model sees a compact summary with stable evidence ids; drill-down is one more call.

```
machine_status: HEALTHY · SULY-HPED800 · sample 2026-11-18T09:05:29+08:00 · 11s old (ttl 180s)
disk     / 8.9% used, 106 GiB free · /srv/storage 2.0% used, 108 GiB free
memory   2.5 GiB available / 3.7 GiB · load 0.1 0.04 0.01 · 4 cpus
services dsh-web active/running · forgejo active/running · memory-probe unknown (plugin-hosted service has no systemd unit; no telemetry source is configured)
backup forgejo-backup.service success/0 · last completion 4h29m ago (limit 26h) · artifact unknown (journal evidence is opt-in (backup.journal); unit completion is the default evidence)
ipv6     eno1 2408:825c:260:b0c::/64
findings 0 · unknowns 1 · incidents 0
  [unknown expected] svc.unhealthy memory-probe: plugin-hosted service has no systemd unit; no telemetry source is configured · hint: telemetry: none evidence=svc:memory-probe
evidence host disk:/ disk:/srv/storage mem load svc:dsh-web svc:forgejo svc:memory-probe backup:forgejo-backup.service ipv6:eno1
```

Stale data is never presented as current:

```
machine_status: STALE · SULY-HPED800 · last sample … · 7m28s old (ttl 180s)
last known: HEALTHY · findings 0 · unknowns 1 · open incidents 0
diagnostic: reading never samples; this is not current machine state. Run `dsh-machine-status doctor`.
```

More samples: [docs/SAMPLES.md](docs/SAMPLES.md).

## CLI

| Command | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `status [--json]` | the same summary as the tool; exit 0 fresh/healthy, 2 degraded/stale, 3 missing/unknown, 1 failure |
| `evidence <id> [--json]` | one evidence record from the current snapshot |
| `sources [--json]` | paths, mtimes, freshness, heartbeat, sampler state |
| `doctor [--json]` | writability, documents, heartbeat, runtime version, timer, sampler result |
| `notifications [--limit N] [--json]` | opt-in transition log |
| `export [--finding RULE] [--json]` | read-only finding export with observation time and advisory expiry |
| `sample [--json]` | run one sampling cycle now (what the timer runs) |
| `install [--dry-run] [--force]` / `uninstall [--purge]` | manage the user units and runtime copy |
| `version` | package and Node version |

`--state-dir DIR` (or `DSH_MACHINE_STATUS_STATE_DIR`) overrides the state directory for testing.

## Decision policy

- A rule breaches or is healthy per sample; **two consecutive breaches** open one incident,
  **two consecutive healthy samples** close it.
- `unknown` (failed collector, unreadable mount, unreadable unit) is tracked separately in
  `unknowns`, not in `findings`: it never closes an incident and never counts as healthy. An
  **expected** unknown is a source the operator declared absent (`telemetry: none`, e.g. the
  plugin-hosted memory probe): it is listed once with its hint, does not degrade the sample and is
  not repeated as a finding. Any unexpected unknown still degrades the sample.
- Boot-id change (host reboot) restarts per-rule streaks and records `host.reboot` information.
- A changed IPv6 /64 prefix is **information only**; a missing global address alerts only when
  `collect.ipv6.requireGlobal` is true.
- With `notify.enabled: false` (default) no notification is written at all. When enabled, exactly one
  JSONL row is written per incident transition; an unchanged failure is not repeated.

## Defaults: measured or calibrate-required

Measured on **SULY-HPED800** (Arch Linux, 4 GB RAM, Node v26.13.1, DSH 0.2.2-rc.3) on
**2026-11-18 09:05 +08**, sample `387e0698-901d-4d4f-b2ac-6d473bad6205`:

| Setting | Value | Class | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| sampler wall duration | 26 ms | measured | `snapshot.durationMs` |
| collector duration | disk 0 ms, memory 1 ms, services 12 ms, backup 10 ms, ipv6 2 ms | measured | `snapshot.collectors.*.durationMs` |
| sampler CPU per run | 94,795,000 ns ≈ 94.8 ms | measured | `systemctl --user show … -p CPUUsageNSec` |
| document sizes | snapshot 9,437 B; status 902 B; state 4,245 B | measured | `fs.statSync` |
| backup age at the sample | 16,172,019 ms ≈ 4 h 29 m | measured | `collectors.backup.ageMs` |
| IPv6 /64 lease at the sample | valid 6,706 s / 7,022 s (≈1.9 h) | measured | `ip -6 -j addr show dev eno1` |
| sampling cadence | 60 s | calibrate-required | brief starting policy; not tuned |
| freshness TTL | 180 s | calibrate-required | brief starting policy |
| disk floor | 10 % free **or** 2 GiB | calibrate-required | not measured against this host |
| disk drop | 20 % and 1 GiB over 6 samples | calibrate-required | not measured |
| memory floor | 10 % and 512 MiB | calibrate-required | not measured |
| load threshold | 2 × CPU count (load1) | calibrate-required | not measured |
| backup age limit | 26 h (daily 04:17 job + slack) | calibrate-required | job schedule observed, limit not tuned |
| incident open/close | 2 / 2 samples | calibrate-required | brief starting policy |
| notification retention | 512 rows | calibrate-required | not measured |
| collector timeout | 2,000 ms | calibrate-required | max observed 12 ms, 2 s is headroom |
| unknown telemetry | separate `unknowns`; `telemetry: none` is expected and does not degrade | product choice | memory-probe declared absent with a hint |
| notifications | off | product requirement | silent by default |

## Tests

```sh
npm test          # 10 files, 55 assertions; no dependencies, no Linux required
npm pack          # tarball includes test/
```

The clean-install check used on the target host:

```sh
mkdir /tmp/dsh-ms && tar -xzf sulytwelve-dsh-machine-status-0.1.4.tgz -C /tmp/dsh-ms
cd /tmp/dsh-ms/package && node test/*.mjs
```

Tests cover a healthy cache hit, sustained service failure, stale backup, routine prefix change,
host reboot, partial collector failure, recovery, the stale-but-last-known-healthy sample, one
notification per transition, zero default notifications, zero sampler starts from status reads,
failed writes keeping the previous snapshot, and the unit/config installer.

## Limits and boundaries

- Collectors target Linux. On other platforms disk/memory degrade to OS fallbacks and
  services/backup/IPv6 report `unknown` with a diagnostic; nothing throws.
- `memory-probe` has no systemd unit (it is a plugin row). It is declared `telemetry: none`, so it is
  listed once as an **expected** unknown with its hint; it does not degrade the sample and does not
  repeat as a finding. It is never guessed as healthy.
  This plugin does not read the context-manager's data.
- Backup evidence is the job's systemd completion record (`Result=success`, `ExecMainStatus=0`,
  completion time). The artifact name/count lives in a journal line the `dsh` user cannot read by
  default; set `collect.backup.journal: true` only after granting journal read access.
- No remediation commands are produced or executed; remediation is out of scope.
- A model-facing call in a live server session was **not** exercised; the heartbeat proves the
  running process's registry projects the tool (`modelFacing: true`), and the CLI exercises the same
  read path.

## Rollback

```sh
# sampler
dsh-machine-status uninstall            # keeps state for postmortem
dsh-machine-status uninstall --purge    # also removes the state directory

# plugin row
dsh plugin --profile web remove @sulytwelve/dsh-machine-status
# then restart the DSH host process you run (see Install §1); DSH provides no unit
```

The profile `package.json` backup taken before installation is
`~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json.bak-20261118-ms`. See [docs/OPERATIONS.md](docs/OPERATIONS.md).

## Distribution

Three install paths, in preference order:

1. **npm** — the package is published manually: pm stage publish from the tagged tree, then approve the staged version on npmjs.com. The account uses passkey 2FA, so a token-driven publish workflow is not used.
2. **GitHub tag** — `dsh plugin --profile web add github:Sulytwelve/dsh-machine-status#vX.Y.Z` (pin the tag).
3. **Release tarball URL** — `dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/Sulytwelve/dsh-machine-status/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/sulytwelve-dsh-machine-status.tgz`.
4. **codeload tarball** — when git fetches or GitHub release downloads are blocked, `dsh plugin --profile web add https://codeload.github.com/Sulytwelve/dsh-machine-status/tar.gz/refs/tags/vX.Y.Z` installs the tagged tree directly (the spec shape already used for the context-manager on this host).

**Upgrading:** DSH hot-updates code inside an installed plugin (HMR), but it does not overwrite an
installed plugin package. A new version therefore needs remove then add (restart only if the Host
does not hot-load the new module generation):
tag, then restart the process that serves the profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove @sulytwelve/dsh-machine-status
dsh plugin --profile web add github:Sulytwelve/dsh-machine-status#v0.1.4
```

Until npm publishing is enabled, use the GitHub tag or the release tarball spec after the remove.
## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# LoopForge DSH 插件 这个插件是一个适用于 DSH 0.2.1 及后续 bundle-compatible 版本的 Host bundle，把 LoopForge Local 接入 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）Profile。它复用项目中 `.dsh/skills/devflow` 的 Portable 工作流，不复制工作流规则或产物模板。 ## 本地安装 先在目标项目安装 DSH Portable Skill： ```bash loopforge skills install dsh ``` 再从 LoopForge 源码目录把 bundle 加入目标 DSH profile（`web` 也可以换成你自己的 profile 名称）： ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add -w /path/to/LoopForge/local/dsh-plugin ``` 安装器会把 `@tencent/loopforge-dsh` 写入 profile 的 `dsh.profile.bundles`，并由 `cordis.patch.yml` 插入插件行；旧版 `dsh-plugin.json` 清单不会被当前 DSH Loader 读取。安装后可用下面的只读检查确认 bundle 已组合： ```bash dsh --profile web --dump-config dsh --profile web --dump-config-schema ``` 输出应包含 `@tencent/loopforge-dsh`、`loopforge-dsh`，且 schema 的 `diagnostics` 为空。 重启 DSH 后可用： - `/devflow <需求>`：直接按 Skill 执行完整工作流。 - `/loopforge start <需求>`：初始化一个 medium 任务并显示状态文件位置。 - `/loopforge status`：查看最近任务、当前阶段和待审批门禁。 - `/loopforge result`：查看任务状态和产物目录。 - `/loopforge approve [阶段]`：批准当前人工门禁；REQUIREMENT 会强制带用户确认。 - `loopforge_status`：供 DSH Agent 读取结构化状态。 阶段 Agent 使用 DSH 的 `subagent` 工具。没有该工具时，工作流必须按协议记录 `single-context` 降级原因，不能伪造隔离执行器。 ## 卸载 ```bash dsh plugin --profile web remove loopforge-dsh loopforge skills uninstall dsh ```

English · 简体中文

Two ways to work · Quick start · SOPs · Features · Local · FAQ · Docs

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8af401d9-1aae-427c-b4bc-455c12d17beb

80-second product tour (1080p, with sound).

**LoopForge** is a self-hosted workspace where your team ships software with coding agents. Describe what you need to **Main Bot** in chat: it opens a Docker sandbox, checks out your repositories, delegates to project roles, and opens the PR. When a way of working proves itself, save it as an **SOP** (a standard workflow of agents, scripts and human gates) so the next requirement is delivered the same way, with review and approval built in. Coding-agent CLIs do the work: CodeBuddy, Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Antigravity, Kimi Code, Pi, DeepSeek Harness and ZCode. LoopForge adds the roles, sandboxes, checkpoints and history around them, all on your own infrastructure under the MIT license. ## Two ways to work | | **Chat with Main Bot** | **Run an SOP** | | --- | --- | --- | | Best for | Exploring, quick fixes, iterating with the agent | Repeatable delivery with fixed stages and sign-off | | How it runs | Main Bot opens a [conversation workspace](docs/conversation-workspaces.md) (a Docker sandbox with your repos) on demand and calls project roles as subagents | The engine runs Agent, Script, Human-gate and sub-SOP nodes in order, in their own sandbox | | You stay in control by | Queuing or steering messages mid-reply, and pausing, resuming or taking over a running SOP from chat | Approving at human gates, sending work back to a chosen step, retrying or rerunning from any node | | Delivers | A PR/MR, or a direct merge into a shared branch (`mode=direct`) | Documents, code or a PR, plus per-node artifacts and logs | Both paths track the same **requirements**, so every change, whether made in chat or by an SOP, links back to what was asked for and counts toward delivery and cost reports.

The chat home. Type a request, @ a role, skill, requirement, SOP or repository, and pick the executor, model and permission mode per conversation.

## Why LoopForge Ask a coding agent to "fix this bug" and the result depends on that run. It might skip the plan, forget the tests, review its own code, or stop halfway without anyone noticing. That's fine for a demo, but it isn't how a team ships. - **Repeatable.** Same SOP, same stages, same checks for every requirement. Start from built-in backend, frontend, bug-fix and product SOPs. - **Separated roles.** Planning, implementation, review and testing each get their own prompt, executor, model, rules, Skills and MCP tools. A role works as an SOP node or as a subagent in chat. - **Human in the loop.** Approval gates where they matter. Read the report, approve, or send the work back to a chosen step. - **Observable and resumable.** Node status, tool traces, logs and artifacts in one place. Pause, retry a failed step, or rerun from any node. - **Your stack, your servers.** Ten coding-agent CLIs as executors, from CodeBuddy, Codex and Claude Code to OpenCode, Cursor CLI and more. GitHub, Skills and MCP as tools. Docker sandboxes or your own machine as the runtime. ## Quick start Install **Git** and clone the repository first. The installer checks Docker, Compose, Python 3 and curl and offers to install missing components. Python/curl installation supports apt, dnf and yum on Linux; the Compose plugin supports x86_64/arm64 and verifies the official release SHA-256. macOS needs a working Python 3 and Docker Desktop; Homebrew can install missing components. Ordinary Linux users are supported through Docker group access or sudo. Set `LOOPFORGE_YES=1` to accept installation prompts. Package and image downloads require internet access. ```bash git clone https://github.com/Tencent/LoopForge.git cd LoopForge ./start.sh ``` `./start.sh` pulls the GHCR release image pinned in `compose.yaml` without building locally (`bash scripts/install.sh` does the same). It creates the MySQL and platform services, generates configuration and session secrets, and installs the built-in sandboxes, starter SOPs and welcome project. Host Go and Node.js installations are not required. Configure model API keys and GitHub authorization after startup. Use `./start.sh logs`, `stop`, `restart` or `pull` to manage it, and `./start.sh dev` to build the checkout from source. If downloads from `ghcr.io` stall, set `MIRROR` to a registry host that can stand in for `ghcr.io`. `./start.sh` pulls from that host and tags the image back to the name pinned in `compose.yaml`. Setting `MIRROR` trusts that host, because the download is tagged with the official name. The GitHub Release records the digest; `docker image inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' ghcr.io/tencent/loopforge:` should show the same digest after `@`. Without `MIRROR`, `./start.sh` still pulls `ghcr.io` directly, and `compose.yaml` stays unchanged. Upgrade with the same variable and `./start.sh pull`. [ghcr.nju.edu.cn](https://doc.nju.edu.cn/books/e1654/page/ghcr) is one such host. A Docker `registry-mirrors` entry such as `https://docker.nju.edu.cn` only accelerates Docker Hub and is not a value for `MIRROR`. ```bash MIRROR=ghcr.nju.edu.cn ./start.sh ``` Open the address printed by the installer and create your account; the first one becomes the administrator. The service listens on `0.0.0.0:8090` by default. On a cloud host, the installer reads the public IP from the provider's metadata service and prints it; allow the port in your security group, or put an HTTPS reverse proxy in front. Restrict access to your own IP until the administrator account exists. The home page's quick-access guide walks you through adding a model key, connecting a repository and choosing an SOP. For GitLab, Gitea, Gogs and other Git hosts, [set up Git SSH](docs/deployment.md#git-repositories-over-ssh) to check out and push branches with a personal key. PR/MR and Issue automation requires a hosting API token or a separately configured MCP. ### Try it without an API key New accounts join the **LoopForge demo project**, which includes an SOP made only of a script and a human gate: 1. Switch to the demo project, open **Templates**, and open **Platform check · script & approval**. 2. Click **Run SOP**. A real script writes a report, then the run waits for you at the approval step. 3. Approve it from **Needs review** or the run page, and watch the run continue to its final artifact. ### What you need for real work | I want to… | You need | | --- | --- | | Run the script + approval demo | Nothing | | Chat with Main Bot, generate a document or a new project | An API key for the selected executor | | Change an existing repository (in chat or via an SOP) and open a PR | Model credentials and a GitHub repository (connect GitHub in personal settings) |
More setup details: executors, GitHub, sandboxes, access model
- **Executors.** Pick one of ten CLIs beside the home composer, then a model. Every SOP role can choose its executor independently (built-in roles default to CodeBuddy). Requirement clarification, AI notification summaries, Bot replies and run evals currently use CodeBuddy, so their model pickers list CodeBuddy models only and the server refuses a model of another CLI instead of switching it to CodeBuddy; scheduled assistant tasks run on the CLI the task selects. | Executor | Credentials | Installation | | --- | --- | --- | | **CodeBuddy** | Personal key, or a shared key an administrator configures for chat and SOP runs | In the Docker image | | **Codex** | Personal key; a connected execution machine can use its local login | In the Docker image | | **Claude Code** | Personal key; a connected execution machine can use its local login | Installed from npm on first use, then cached | | **OpenCode · Kimi Code · Pi** | Personal key only | Installed from npm on first use, then cached | | **DeepSeek Harness** | Personal key only | In the Docker image | | **Cursor CLI · Antigravity** | Personal key only | Provider installer on first chat use; not installed into SOP sandboxes | | **ZCode** | Personal key only | Not bundled; install it on the service or execution machine PATH | The seven agent CLIs after Claude Code keep their model and MCP configuration in a private home directory per run, so they always use the responsible user's own key and Base URL from personal settings, even on a connected execution machine. When rolling them out to a team, each member configures their own credentials. First-use installs need npm or provider access; [native deployments](docs/deployment.md#workers-and-runners) need the CLI for the executor you choose. - **GitHub is optional.** All built-in generic SOPs run without a repository: product SOPs deliver documents, and new frontend/backend projects deliver source files in the task workspace. Bug fixes still need source code and reproduction details. Connect a repository when you work on existing code or want PRs. - **Delivering to a repository.** Choose **Connect GitHub** in personal settings, approve the device code on GitHub and pick your repository (the LoopForge OAuth App is built in; no PAT required, manual PAT entry still works). Set executor credentials (or bind a local execution machine), then either run a project SOP or ask Main Bot to change the code and submit a PR/MR. - **Sandboxes.** In the default Compose installation, SOP runs and conversation workspaces both use Docker sandbox containers started through the host Docker socket. Default sandboxes reuse the installed runtime image, so nothing extra is built after installation; custom Dockerfiles still build their own images. Docker socket access grants control of the host daemon, so this setup is for trusted teams, not untrusted multi-tenant isolation. See [deployment boundaries](docs/deployment.md#accounts). Re-running the installer keeps your data. - **Accounts and access.** New installations listen on all interfaces (existing bind settings are kept) and are designed for a trusted team: signed-in users can read project data across the instance, and teammates can sign up from the login page (`AGENTFLOW_ALLOW_SIGNUP=false` in `.env` turns that off). Read the [account and access model](docs/deployment.md#accounts) before exposing it beyond your team. - **Remote access, HTTPS, separate workers.** See [Deployment](docs/deployment.md). - **Hacking on LoopForge itself?** `bash scripts/dev.sh` runs it natively (Go 1.26.11+).
## How SOPs work An **SOP** is the workflow a delivery follows. Agents, scripts and people take part in the same run:

The SOP designer with the built-in bug-fix SOP. Each step picks a role; failed checks can send the work back to an earlier step.

| Node | What it does | | --- | --- | | **Agent** | A role (prompt, executor, model, rules, Skills and MCP tools) that designs, implements, reviews or tests. | | **Script** | A deterministic shell step: build, test, lint, generate a report. No AI where AI is not needed. | | **Human gate** | Pauses the run until someone checks the artifacts and approves, or sends the work back to a step. | | **Sub-SOP** | Runs another SOP as a sub-workflow. | | **Preview build** | Builds a static site and archives it for review. | Each node declares its artifacts and dependencies, and the engine starts each step once its dependencies complete. Start from a built-in SOP, adapt its roles, rules and environment to your project, and publish versions as it evolves.

A run waiting at a human gate: approve and continue, add context and rerun the step, or send the work back upstream.

**A delivery we actually ran:** four CodeBuddy roles planned a Python fix, implemented it, reviewed it independently and summarized the delivery. Three real tests passed; the run waited for human approval, then verified the accepted code had not changed. The [reusable acceptance case](e2e/api/45-delivery-model.test.mjs) checks the files and results. See the [validation record](docs/validation.md) for scope and known gaps. ## Features | Area | What you get | | --- | --- | | **Chat workbench** | Main Bot with per-conversation executor, model and permission mode. `@` references for roles, skills, requirements, SOPs and repositories. Messages queue while a reply runs; *Steer* interrupts and sends now. Generated files open in a side panel with preview, source and download. | | **Conversation workspaces** | On-demand Docker sandboxes with the project's repositories checked out, project roles as native subagents, and direct control of a running SOP workspace: pause, resume or take over. | | **SOP designer** | Visual canvas with Agent, Script, Human gate, Sub-SOP and Preview nodes, rework-on-failure edges, validation, version history and publishing. Built-in backend, frontend, bug-fix and product SOPs. | | **Roles** | Reusable definitions: prompt, executor, model, rules, Skills, MCP tools, artifacts and gates, shared across SOP nodes and chat subagents. | | **Requirement → delivery** | Requirements tracked end to end, whether shipped by an SOP or straight from chat, with PR/MR status tracking, merge detection and direct-branch merges. | | **Runs & approvals** | Live node status, tool traces, worker logs, per-node artifact snapshots and workspace previews. A single **Needs review** inbox for every gate waiting on you. | | **AI scheduled tasks** | Recurring agent tasks with full workspace, SOP and MCP access; a shared market of versioned, parameterized task templates; automatic SOP dispatch for new requirements. | | **Insights & cost** | Engineering metrics, business-domain reports with static HTML/SVG export, and token/cost accounting for SOPs and conversations at public list prices. | | **Execution environments** | Platform workers, Docker sandboxes, or a connected local execution machine using your own tools and repositories. | | **Team-ready** | Password accounts, projects and members, light/dark/system themes, an OpenAPI-described HTTP and MCP API. Management pages are in English and Chinese; the chat workbench is Chinese for now. |

Built-in SOPs are read-only blueprints; copy one into your project to run and edit it.

## LoopForge Local Don't want to run a server? **LoopForge Local** brings the built-in delivery workflows straight into the coding assistant you already use: ```bash # Run inside your target project, e.g. for Claude Code npx -y loopforge-cli@latest install claude ``` Then run `/start-devflow ""` in Claude Code. | Host | Supported | | --- | --- | | Claude Code · CodeBuddy · Codex · Cursor | Classic (default) and Portable editions | | Pi | Portable edition | | DeepSeek Harness | Portable edition | | Hermes Agent | Portable edition | See the [local guide](docs/local/usage.md) for each host's entry point and [editions](docs/local/editions.md) for the differences. Source lives in [`local/`](local/). Local runs the built-in workflows today; exporting a platform SOP for standalone local execution is planned. | | Platform | Local | | --- | --- | --- | | Best for | Teams sharing chat workspaces, SOPs, approvals and history | One developer inside an IDE or CLI | | Needs | Docker + Python 3 | Node.js 20+, Python 3.8+ and a coding assistant | | Workflows | Chat with Main Bot + custom SOPs on a visual canvas | Built-in Classic / Portable workflows | | Evidence | Shared run details, approvals and metrics in the web workspace | Artifacts under `artifacts/{task_slug}/` + optional local dashboard | ## FAQ **Do I need an API key to try it?** No. The demo SOP uses only a script and a human gate. Chat and agent steps need a key for the executor you pick. Model usage is not included; you bring your own credentials. **Do I need GitHub?** No. Chat, documents and new projects run in the task workspace. Connect GitHub when you want to change an existing repository or open PRs. **Should I use chat or an SOP?** Use chat to explore and iterate; Main Bot can still open a PR. Once you find a way of working you want every requirement to follow, with fixed reviewers, tests and sign-off, put it in an SOP. Main Bot can start, pause and take over SOP runs, so the two paths work together. **How is this different from Dify, n8n or Flowise?** Those are general-purpose AI and automation workflow builders. LoopForge is built for **software delivery with coding agents**: implementer and reviewer roles, Docker sandboxes with real repositories, GitHub delivery, human acceptance gates and run evidence. **How is this different from using Claude Code, Codex, CodeBuddy or another coding CLI directly?** LoopForge doesn't replace them; it orchestrates them. Each agent step and each chat turn runs one of those CLIs. LoopForge adds what surrounds it: who does what, in which sandbox, in which order, with which checks, and who signs off. **Is it safe to expose on the internet?** New installations listen on all interfaces and target a trusted team. Read the [account and access model](docs/deployment.md#accounts) and set up HTTPS before opening it up. Report vulnerabilities privately via the [security policy](SECURITY.md). ## Documentation | I want to… | Start here | | --- | --- | | Deploy, manage accounts, connect execution machines | [Deployment](docs/deployment.md) | | Understand chat workspaces, scheduled AI tasks and token pricing | [Conversation workspaces](docs/conversation-workspaces.md) · [AI scheduled tasks](docs/ai-scheduled-task-capabilities.md) · [Token pricing](docs/token-pricing.md) | | Install local workflows or choose an edition | [LoopForge Local](docs/local/usage.md) · [Editions](docs/local/editions.md) | | Extend the platform or use the HTTP / MCP API | [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) · [API reference](docs/api/README.md) · [Shared schedules API](docs/api/shared-schedules.md) | | Contribute to the UI | [Frontend design conventions](design.md) (Chinese) | | Check functional coverage and release readiness | [Validation record](docs/validation.md) · [Acceptance matrix](docs/testing/acceptance-matrix.md) · [Release review](docs/release-readiness.md) | | Understand source provenance and maintenance | [Public scope](docs/open-source-scope.md) · [Upstream synchronization](docs/upstream-sync.md) | ## Community Scan the QR code to join the LoopForge community group. ## Contributing Issues and PRs are welcome: share a use case, report a bug, or improve workflows, integrations and the platform experience. Start with the [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md). Security issues go through the [security policy](SECURITY.md). If LoopForge is useful to you, a star helps others find it. ## License [MIT](LICENSE). Third-party components keep their own licenses and notices; see [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

**六源快讯聚合**：财联社电报 / 金十数据 / 华尔街见闻 / 东方财富 / 同花顺 / 新浪财经 7×24，60 秒一轮轻量 JSON 端点轮询，写入本地 SQLite - **「快讯」阅读器 tab**：经 `registerView` 挂进主插件阅读器，密排时序 ticker 视图，独立于普通订阅列表 - **多源互证标记**：同一条新闻被多个源报道时自动聚类并标注源数——互证越多越重要 - **三通道提醒 + 桌面通知**：关键词命中 / 源标重要 / 多源互证，命中即经主插件通道弹桌面通知并跳快讯页 - **每小时「快讯快报」**：经 `registerBriefType` 注册条目供给器，由主插件的 LLM 产线整点生成 AI 摘要（≤12 条，互证优先）；评分免 LLM——多源互证 9 > 源原生热度 8 > 普通 6 - **数据全本地**：`companions/rss-news-flash-kuaixun/` 下的 `kuaixun.db` / `alerts.json`，随主插件完整备份覆盖 ## 安装 ```bash dsh plugin --profile <你的profile> add dsh-rss-news-flash-kuaixun ``` 或经 dshmarket 插件市场安装。装完重启 dsh 生效；首次加载若未检测到主插件会弹层指引。 ## 依赖 | 依赖 | 说明 | |---|---| | `dsh-rss-news-daily ≥ 1.1.0` | 宿主：提供 rndSources 服务（源注册 / 视图注册 / 快报产线 / 桌面通知） | | Node ≥ 22.18 | dsh 运行环境要求 | 内部标识：cordis entry id 为 `rss-news-flash-kuaixun`（去 `dsh-` 前缀的惯例，同主插件 `rss-news-daily`）；数据目录 `companions/rss-news-flash-kuaixun/`，旧名 `news-kuaixun` 的目录与 provider 源行在首次启动时自动迁移。 ## 为什么建议安装 browser-fetch **建议安装。不装也能正常使用，但同花顺和金十两个源将无法更新。** 快讯插件默认以程序方式直接获取数据，财联社、华尔街见闻、东方财富、新浪四个源工作正常。同花顺和金十的接口对非浏览器请求不响应或返回错误，需要一个真实的浏览器环境才能稳定取数。 [browser-fetch](https://github.com/terry2010/dsh-rss-news-browser-fetch) 提供的正是这个环境：它在本机运行一个专用的 Chrome 实例，以真实浏览器会话获取数据——等效于你自己打开网页查看，只是过程自动完成。该实例与你的日常浏览器完全独立，登录状态互不干扰，全部数据仅保存在本机。 **安装后可能观察到的现象（均属正常）：** - 专用 Chrome 窗口会按抓取周期出现新标签页——这是它在执行取数任务 - 标签页平时停在该网站的 `robots.txt` 待命页，用于为后续请求维持同源环境，并非在浏览其他内容 - 若关闭或退出该浏览器实例，同花顺和金十将暂停更新，恢复运行后自动继续 **是否必须安装？** 不是。缺少该插件时插件照常运行，仅上述两个源无数据，设置面板顶部会显示当前状态。安装后自动生效，无需任何配置。
点击我展开内容 传输层 node fetch 优先、浏览器回落： | 源 | 直连表现 | 机制 | |---|---|---| | 同花顺（10jqka） | node 请求连接挂起（tarpit） | 标记 `preferBrowser`，每轮直接走浏览器通道 | | 金十（jin10） | 5xx / 网络错误 | node 失败后自动回落 `bf.fetch`；缺席则持续失败、退避拉长轮询 | 浏览器通道请求发自用户本机浏览器会话（同源页内 fetch、自动携带该域 cookie）；若专用 Chrome 被关闭/退出，同花顺与金十断供，其余四源照常。
```bash dsh plugin --profile <你的profile> add dsh-rss-news-browser-fetch ``` ## 声明 - 本插件仅从各源**公开可访问的端点**读取快讯标题与摘要，全部数据保存在用户本地，不提供转发、再分发或商用数据服务 - 浏览器通道访问的是你本可在浏览器中手动打开的公开页面，请求发自你自己的浏览器会话；请自行确认并遵守目标站点的访问条款 - [金十数据](https://www.jin10.com/)、[财联社](https://www.cls.cn/)、[华尔街见闻](https://wallstreetcn.com/) 等源站提供官方的付费专业订阅，包含更及时、更全面、更深入的行情资讯。若你需要专业级的信息服务，请直接订阅源站官方产品——本插件仅汇总其公开快讯，不构成对专业订阅的替代 - 快讯原文版权归源站所有，点击条目跳转原站阅读；内容仅供参考，不构成任何投资建议 ## 开发 ```bash npm test # tsc 构建 + copy-assets + node --test node scripts/install-to-profile.mjs desktop # 装进本地 dsh profile 验证（需重启 dsh） ``` 开发前需把主插件 clone 到同级目录（devDep `file:` 引用 + 类型契约来源）： ```bash git clone https://github.com/terry2010/dsh-rss-news-daily ../dsh-rss-news-daily ``` 技术栈：TypeScript / cordis / rndSources API v3 / better-sqlite3。主插件接口契约见主仓库 `docs/PLUGINS.md`。 ## 相关插件 - **[dsh-rss-news-daily](https://github.com/terry2010/dsh-rss-news-daily)** —— 主插件（必需）：RSS 订阅 + AI 每日精选/时段快报 + 侧栏新闻阅读器，本插件的快报产线/通知/界面均由它提供 - **[dsh-rss-news-browser-fetch](https://github.com/terry2010/dsh-rss-news-browser-fetch)** —— browserFetch 浏览器传输服务（可选）：node fetch 响应不稳定时自动回落用户本机浏览器会话取数 ## License Apache-2.0

# dsh-combinagents

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh.md)

[![dsh-plugin topic](https://img.shields.io/badge/topic-dsh--plugin-blue)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)

A user-owned **reporting composition** for DSH (DeepSeek Harness) agents and
subagents.

DSH already gives each subagent a fixed native parent. This plugin adds a
separate, editable layer on top: you decide who reports to whom, independently
of the native subagent tree. The composition is an overlay. The plugin does not
move a session, rewrite its native parent, change its workspace, or change its
sandbox or permission policy.

> **Compatibility:** DSH `0.2.2-rc.5` on the desktop/web profile. This is an
> unpublished local plugin bundle, not an npm package to install from a
> registry. Node.js 22 or newer is required.

Part of the [dsh-plugin](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) topic.

## What you get

- A right-sidebar **Agent composition** tab.
- A separate count chip in the session header.
- Add local sessions or external agents, rename nodes, and set **Reports to**.
- Per-edge **message** and **interrupt** grants.
- Automatic mirroring when a subagent starts.
- **Sync native agents** to import native descendants.
- Clone a whole team, or bud one node into a new independent root.
- A plugin-owned task board, separate from DSH Team.
- Native-name model tools that use the composition, while keeping the native
  tool schemas.
- Cross-profile convergence: another DSH profile's edit becomes visible without
  restarting the Host.

## What it does not do

- It does **not** re-parent existing DSH sessions natively.
- It does **not** delete or rewrite DSH sessions when you remove nodes.
- It does **not** widen a sandbox, permission preset, or approval policy.
- It does **not** merge sessions or move a session to another workspace.
- It is **not** a cross-host or multi-user service. It is a local-profile
  feature.

Think of it as an editable organization chart beside the native subagent tree,
not a replacement for that tree.

## Requirements

- DSH `0.2.2-rc.5` with the desktop/web UI.
- Node.js 22 or newer.
- A **standard** DSH profile (or another preset that keeps the native
  delegation plugins mounted):
  - `tool-subagent-control`
  - `tool-subagent`
  - `tool-subagent-fork`
- The profile must expose `sessions`, `storageDomain`, `subagents`, and the
  sidebar-right client UI. Missing optional services degrade individual fields,
  not the whole tab.

The plugin can run beside other tool plugins. It keeps the native tool
definitions; it only intercepts execution for the six names listed below.

## Install

This checkout is a DSH **bundle** (`package.json` has a `dsh.bundle.patch`
entry). It is not published to npm.

1. Put the checkout in a stable local directory.
2. Register it in your DSH profile as a local bundle. Use the DSH Plugin Manager
   bundle installation for your DSH version, or the equivalent local package
   link in the profile.
3. Make sure the profile entry is enabled:

```yaml
- id: dsh-combinagents
  config:
    autoGrantDelegatedEdges: true
    # Optional: only needed when the JSONL session root is not $DSH_HOME/sessions.
    # sessionRoot: /absolute/path/to/sessions
  disabled: false
```

4. Keep the native delegation plugins mounted. Do **not** use the legacy
   `composed` preset that removes them; without the native definitions there is
   nothing for the plugin to intercept.
5. Restart the Host and refresh the GUI.

After a Host restart, open a **standard** session. Existing sessions created
under an older composed preset keep their old preset until you move them; they
receive a compatibility fallback, but a new standard session is recommended.

If the tab or header chip is missing, confirm the plugin is enabled in the
profile and refresh the page after the Host restart.

## Quick start

1. Open a normal standard session.
2. Open **Agent composition** from the right sidebar or the header chip.
3. Click **Create composition** if this session has no composition yet.
4. Click **Add a session** and select another session. Set its **Reports to**
   parent, or leave it as a root.
5. Open **Details** on an edge to allow messages or interrupts across that
   edge. New manual connections allow messages by default; interrupts stay off
   until enabled.
6. Start a subagent normally with `subagent` or `subagent_fork`. It is mirrored
   into the composition automatically, with its native parent and an
   auto-granted delegation edge.
7. Use **Sync native agents** if a native descendant is missing.

A session belongs to at most one composition. If you attach a session that is
already in another composition, its subtree moves; a remaining source forest is
re-keyed to another local root. The moved subtree keeps its internal grants, and
a new boundary edge inherits the previous incoming grant, so an explicit deny
stays denied. An ordinary DSH fork is a new root; it does not inherit
composition membership from its `parentSession` header.

## The tab

| Action | What it does |
|---|---|
| Add a session | Add an existing DSH session as a composition node |
| Add external | Add a placeholder for an external/non-local execution |
| Reports to | Set the node's parent; `No parent` makes it a root |
| Rename | Change the node label (not the DSH session title) |
| Message / Interrupt grants | Allow that action along the composition path |
| Sync native agents | Import native descendants that are not mirrored yet |
| Clone whole tree | Create a new independent tree; source stays unchanged |
| Bud as new root | Clone one node and its subtree as a new root |
| Show one-shot agents | Show one-shot nodes that are hidden by default |
| Composition tasks | Create, start, complete, reopen, and delete plugin tasks |
| Session cleanup | Preview orphaned clone sessions and one-shot placeholders, open a brief first-user/last-message excerpt, then delete in a separate confirmed step |
| Open conversation | Open a local session; external nodes never offer it |

Nodes show `live`, `saved`, or `archived` state, plus the native parent,
workspace, sandbox, permission preset, agent preset, and lifecycle mode when
available. The tab scrolls vertically. **Add a session** and **Add task** use the
same in-place panel pattern, each with **Cancel**; Escape also closes the session
picker.

The tab filters **one-shot** nodes by default. Enable **Show one-shot agents**
to see them. External nodes remain visible because they are placeholders, not
necessarily one-shot agents.

## Model tools

The plugin does not register shadow copies of the native tools. It registers a
`tools/execute` interceptor. For these six names, the native definition and
therefore the model-facing name, description, parameters, output schema,
presentation, prompt guidance, and restrictions stay unchanged; only the
execution path uses the composition:

| Tool | In this plugin |
|---|---|
| `list_agents` | Lists continuable composition nodes, with `mode=` in the description |
| `send_message` | Follows composition edges and grants; rejects one-shot targets |
| `interrupt_agent` | Follows composition ancestor/grant rules; can interrupt live one-shot agents |
| `subagent` | Starts a native child, mirrors it, and auto-grants the edge |
| `subagent_fork` | Same as `subagent`, using the fork provider |
| `wait_agent` | Native caller-inbox wait behavior |

`composition_task` is the only globally registered extra tool. The old
`composition_list_agents`, `composition_send_message`, and
`composition_interrupt_agent` aliases are removed. Native
`list_subagent_models` and other unique tools are untouched.

`list_agents` omits **one-shot** and **external** rows, matching the native
continuable listing. One-shot targets cannot receive follow-ups. The lifecycle
mode is shown in the row description because the native output schema does not
have a separate `mode` field.

### Lifecycle modes

Composition nodes carry the same native lifecycle distinction:

| Mode | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `continuable` | A long-lived child that can receive follow-up messages |
| `one-shot` | A terminal execution with no follow-up |
| `external` | An external execution with no local session |
| `unknown` | A legacy or not-yet-synced record |

A name is not a lifecycle mode. A child without an explicit name still gets a
generated `agent-N` name and can still be continuable. Use **Sync native agents**
to refresh modes from the native catalogs.

## Cross-profile consistency

The storages live under the DSH home, so two profiles can open the same
composition data. Each Host keeps its own in-memory storage-domain snapshot.
The plugin makes them converge:

- After a durable composition or policy write, a small `.revision` marker is
  updated.
- A reader that sees a newer marker reopens the storage domain and rebuilds
  session membership.
- Composition mutations take a process-shared `.mutation.lock`, so two profiles
  do not overwrite each other's read-modify-write.
- The tab polls `/state` every 3 seconds and the header chip polls `/summary`
  every 5 seconds while visible.

This is **eventual convergence**, not a synchronous distributed database.
Writes from an older plugin version do not publish the marker, and a custom
storage backend outside the default directory needs a `storageDir` override.

## Safety and authority

- The overlay never writes a DSH `SessionHeader`, native `subagent/catalog`,
  cwd, sandbox policy, or permission preset.
- Composition edges are advisory for organization. The plugin's `send_message`
  and `interrupt_agent` execution use composition grants; they do not bypass
  native session policy.
- Messages prefer the native relay inside a native tree. Live cross-tree
  targets use the composition relay.
- Crossing workspaces without full permission asks the approval service; only
  an accepted one-shot approval proceeds.
- Every delivered, denied, or approval-denied action is audited.
- External nodes cannot receive follow-ups.
- Removing a node removes only the overlay. It never deletes a DSH session.
- **Session cleanup** is the only destructive session operation. It never
  touches live sessions or composition members; it deletes only inactive,
  explicitly confirmed orphaned clone sessions and one-shot placeholders from
  the default JSONL session root. Set `sessionRoot` for a custom root. It
  reclaims the session-log directory; shared attachment/cache files are not
  deleted. This cannot be undone.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check |
|---|---|
| The six native-name tools still behave natively | Is the plugin enabled? Does the profile keep the native delegation rows? Restart the Host after installing. |
| `composition_*` tools are missing | They were removed by design; use the native names plus `composition_task`. |
| `NOT_IN_COMPOSITION` | Create a composition for this session, or use `subagent` from a top-level agent. |
| `AGENT_BUSY` | An affected agent or one of its composition ancestors/descendants is running. Wait for it to finish. |
| `another DSH profile is changing the composition` | Another profile holds the mutation lock. Retry after a moment. |
| `STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE` | The domain could not be reloaded; reads keep the last in-memory snapshot and writes fail closed. Restart the Host. |
| `storageMemory` warning | The storage domain could not open. Changes last until the Host restarts; check the DSH storage backend. |
| A one-shot agent is missing | It is hidden by default. Enable **Show one-shot agents**; use **Sync native agents** if its mode is still unknown. |
| The tree looks stale in another profile | Wait for the 3-second poll, refresh the page, or check that both profiles run this version. |
| The tab is absent | Confirm the plugin and client UI are enabled, then refresh after the Host restart. |

## Limitations

- One composition per session, and a strict `reports-to` forest.
- No native re-parenting and no merging of sessions.
- Labels are user-facing and may be duplicated; duplicate labels make
  `send_message` target selection ambiguous.
- The plugin does not change a session's workspace, sandbox, permission preset,
  or approval policy.
- Task-board state is plugin-owned, not DSH Team state.
- A very large archived composition under an enormous transcript can still make
  the surrounding session UI paint slowly; the bridge itself is not the
  bottleneck.
- Legacy composed sessions use fallback tool definitions until they migrate to
  a standard preset.
- The exact native request-prefix fingerprint is not part of the acceptance
  tests yet.

## Development

```bash
npm test
npm run check
```

Tests use only Node's built-in test runner. There is no build step and no
runtime dependency.

```text
index.js                 Host entry and bridge lifecycle
client.js                Right-sidebar tab, header utility, count chip
src/graph.js             Pure composition graph
src/clone.js             Pure clone/bud planner
src/clone-manager.js     Clone/bud host adapter
src/store.js             Storage domain, revision reload, mutation lock
src/discovery.js         Session and native-catalog discovery
src/manager.js           Serialized mutations and grants
src/http.js              Loopback JSON bridge
src/controls.js          Native tool execution interception
```

More detail:

- [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- [Product handoff](docs/HANDOFF.md)
- [DSH feasibility notes](docs/FEASIBILITY.md)
- [Standard-profile setup and migration](docs/COMPOSED-PROFILE.md)
- [Clone/bud spike](docs/CLONE-SPIKE.md)
- [Working contract for contributors](AGENTS.md)

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).
